children.title: SAT Foundations Complexity Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Foundational representations, canonical reductions, restricted languages, and structural regimes needed by the encoding and solving branches.

children.title: Formula Syntax Trees
children.top_down_role: Tree-based propositional representations, connective structure, and formula-size viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Formula Syntax Trees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree representation of finite propositional formulas over a fixed connective basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix variables \(X\) and a finite Boolean basis \(B\), where each \(b\in B\) has arity \(r(b)\). A formula syntax tree is a finite rooted ordered tree whose leaves are labeled by elements of \(X\cup\{0,1\}\), and whose internal nodes labeled \(b\) have exactly \(r(b)\) ordered children. Its value under \(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\) is obtained recursively from the leaves toward the root. Its tree size \(|T|\) is its number of nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propositional formula is an ordered rooted tree of variables, constants, and correctly aried connectives, evaluated bottom-up; its size counts all occurrences.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a set of propositional variables.
\(B\) is a finite basis of fixed-arity Boolean connectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) represents a Boolean function \(f_T:\{0,1\}^{X_T}\to\{0,1\}\), where \(X_T\subseteq X\) is the finite set of variables occurring in \(T\).

notation.meaning: Number of nodes in the syntax tree.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite propositional-formula syntax-tree definition

children.title: Boolean Circuit Graphs
children.top_down_role: Gate-based directed acyclic representations with explicit reuse of intermediate computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Circuit Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite acyclic Boolean circuits with explicit inputs, gates, and output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a variable set \(X\), a finite Boolean basis \(B\), and an arity function \(r:B\to\mathbb N\). A Boolean circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\) with a designated output vertex \(o\), input vertices labeled by elements of \(X\cup\{0,1\}\), and gate vertices labeled by elements of \(B\). Each gate labeled \(b\in B\) has an ordered list of exactly \(r(b)\) incoming neighbors. Under an assignment \(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\), the vertices are evaluated in topological order. Unless another convention is stated, circuit size is the number of gate vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean circuit is a finite acyclic graph of inputs and fixed-arity gates with one designated output; a computed gate value may be shared by several later gates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a set of propositional variables.
\(B\) is a finite basis of Boolean functions with arity map \(r:B\to\mathbb N\).
\(G\) is finite and acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) computes a well-defined Boolean function \(f_G:\{0,1\}^{X_G}\to\{0,1\}\), where \(X_G\subseteq X\) is the finite set of variables labeling its inputs.

notation.meaning: Arity of the Boolean function labeling a gate.

children.title: Formula–Circuit Translation
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence, expansion costs, and sharing preservation across the two representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Formula–Circuit Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics-preserving translations between formula trees and Boolean circuit DAGs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every formula syntax tree \(T\), orient each parent-child edge toward the parent and regard every internal node as a gate; the resulting circuit \(G_T\) satisfies \(f_{G_T}=f_T\) and has one gate per internal occurrence. Conversely, for a Boolean circuit \(G\), recursively replace each reference to a gate by a fresh copy of its defining connective and predecessors. The resulting formula \(T_G\) satisfies \(f_{T_G}=f_G\), although shared subcircuits may be duplicated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formula directly yields an equivalent circuit, while unfolding an equivalent circuit into a formula can duplicate every shared subcomputation.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(G\) use the same fixed-arity Boolean basis.
\(G\) is finite and acyclic.

notation.meaning: Circuit obtained from formula tree T.
Formula obtained by unfolding circuit G.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantics-preserving translations are precise, and representation is the correct content kind, but no relevant inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Sharing-Sensitive Size Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation-size behavior arising from duplicated subexpressions versus shared subcircuits.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharing-Sensitive Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size comparison under circuit sharing and formula-tree unfolding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a fan-in-at-most-\(d\) Boolean circuit of depth \(h\) with one output. Unfolding \(G\) into a formula produces at most \(1+d+\cdots+d^h\) nodes, hence size \(O(d^h)\), while direct formula-to-circuit translation is linear in formula size. This exponential dependence is attainable syntactically: defining \(g_0=x\) and \(g_{i+1}=g_i\land g_i\) uses \(n\) gates with sharing, whereas its complete unfolding contains \(2^{n+1}-1\) node occurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Formula-to-circuit conversion is linear, but unfolding shared circuit computations can create exponentially many formula occurrences in the circuit depth.
assumptions_latex: Circuit fan-in is bounded by \(d\geq 2\).
Size counts occurrences in formulas and gates in circuits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|T_G|=O(d^h)\), and an \(O(n)\)-size circuit description can have an unfolding of size \(2^{\Theta(n)}\).

notation.meaning: Complete formula unfolding of the circuit.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-fan-in unfolding bound and exponential syntactic example are mathematically consistent, and complexity_bound fits the leaf. A relevant source with a specific locator is absent.

children.title: Clausal Formula Representations
children.top_down_role: Ordered or syntactic CNF presentations viewed as propositional formulas.

knowledge_statements.title: Clausal Formula Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CNF represented as an explicit conjunction of indexed clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite variable set and \(L(X)=\{x,\neg x:x\in X\}\). A clausal formula is an indexed finite conjunction \(F=\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m}C_i\), where each clause is a finite disjunction \(C_i=\bigvee_{\ell\in L_i}\ell\) with \(L_i\subseteq L(X)\). The empty clause denotes false, and the empty conjunction denotes true. Indexing permits equal clauses to occur at different positions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clausal formula is an indexed conjunction of disjunctive clauses, with explicit conventions for empty clauses, empty conjunctions, and repeated clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite.
Each clause contains literals over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\alpha)=1\) exactly when every \(C_i\) contains a literal made true by \(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\).

notation.meaning: Positive and negative literals over X.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indexed-CNF representation and empty-object conventions are precise, but the record has no relevant citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Clause-Set Representations
children.top_down_role: Set-oriented CNF presentations used for structural analysis and solver input.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Set Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CNF represented extensionally as a finite set of literal sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite variable set \(X\), let \(L(X)=\{x,\neg x:x\in X\}\). A clause-set is a finite set \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{L(X)}\). Each \(C\in\mathcal F\) is interpreted as the disjunction of its literals, and \(\mathcal F\) as the conjunction of its clauses. For an assignment \(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\), extend \(\alpha\) to literals by \(\alpha(\neg x)=1-\alpha(x)\). Thus \(\varnothing\in\mathcal F\) makes \(\mathcal F\) unsatisfiable, whereas \(\mathcal F=\varnothing\) is satisfied by every assignment. Because \(\mathcal F\) is a set, repeated copies of an equal clause are identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clause-set is a finite set of clauses represented as literal sets; the empty clause is false, the empty clause-set is true, and duplicate clauses are identified.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite.
\(L(X)=\{x,\neg x:x\in X\}\).
\(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\) is extended to negative literals by \(\alpha(\neg x)=1-\alpha(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\models\mathcal F\) if and only if \(\forall C\in\mathcal F\;\exists\ell\in C\) such that \(\alpha(\ell)=1\).

notation.meaning: Set of positive and negative literals over X.
Truth assignment extended from variables to literals.

children.title: Literal–Clause Incidence Structure
children.top_down_role: Variable, literal, and clause incidence views shared by clausal representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Literal–Clause Incidence Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bipartite signed incidence representation of an indexed CNF instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an indexed clausal formula \(F=(C_1,\ldots,C_m)\), its literal-clause incidence graph is the bipartite graph \(I(F)=(L_F\mathbin{\dot\cup}[m],E)\), where \(L_F\) is the set of literals occurring in \(F\), \([m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and \((\ell,i)\in E\) exactly when \(\ell\in C_i\). Clause indices keep equal clauses at distinct indices separate. A variable-clause incidence representation may instead join \(x\) to \(i\) whenever \(x\in C_i\) or \(\neg x\in C_i\), labeling that incidence by the nonempty set of signs occurring in \(C_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The literal-clause incidence graph joins each occurring literal to every indexed clause containing it; clause indices preserve duplicate clauses, and a variable-based version records all occurring signs.
assumptions_latex: \(F=(C_1,\ldots,C_m)\) is an indexed CNF.
Each clause is a set of literals, so a literal has at most one occurrence within a clause.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{I(F)}(i)=C_i\) for every \(i\in[m]\), after literal vertices are identified with their labels.

notation.meaning: Set of literals occurring in F.

children.title: Duplicate-Clause Conventions
children.top_down_role: Set, multiset, and syntactic treatments of repeated clauses or literals.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Clause Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic and structural effects of retaining or quotienting duplicate clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(C_1,\ldots,C_m)\) be an indexed, unweighted CNF, and let \(\operatorname{set}(F)=\{C_i:i\in[m]\}\) discard duplicate clause occurrences. Every assignment satisfies \(F\) exactly when it satisfies \(\operatorname{set}(F)\), so duplicate removal preserves the model set and satisfiability. If duplicate clauses occur, then \(m>|\operatorname{set}(F)|\). Duplicate removal can also change clause indices, occurrence-based incidence structures, and proof objects referring to particular clause occurrences. Weighted variants require a separately declared rule for aggregating or retaining weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing duplicate clauses from an unweighted indexed CNF preserves all models, but changes occurrence counts and may change structures or certificates tied to clause indices; weighted variants need an explicit aggregation convention.
assumptions_latex: \(F=(C_1,\ldots,C_m)\) is an indexed finite CNF.
The clauses are unweighted and interpreted conjunctively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Mod}(F)=\operatorname{Mod}(\operatorname{set}(F))\); moreover, if \(F\) contains duplicate clauses, then \(m>|\operatorname{set}(F)|\).

notation.meaning: Clause-set obtained by deleting duplicate occurrences.
Set of satisfying assignments of F.
Number of indexed clause occurrences in F.

children.title: Truth Assignments
children.top_down_role: Total and partial valuations used to interpret propositional instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Truth Assignments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total and partial Boolean valuations on propositional variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a variable set \(X\), a total truth assignment is a function \(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\). A partial truth assignment is a function \(\rho:D\to\{0,1\}\) for some \(D\subseteq X\). Extend them to literals in their respective domains by \(\alpha(\neg x)=1-\alpha(x)\) for \(x\in X\) and \(\rho(\neg x)=1-\rho(x)\) for \(x\in D\). Values of formulas under total assignments are defined recursively using the Boolean functions labeling their connectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A total truth assignment maps every variable to false or true; a partial assignment does so on a specified subset, and each assignment extends to the corresponding literals by complementing negative literals.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a set of propositional variables.
Truth values are identified with \(\{0,1\}\).
\(D\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every total assignment \(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\) determines a unique value in \(\{0,1\}\) for each finite propositional formula over variables in \(X\).

children.title: Satisfying Models
children.top_down_role: Assignments retained as satisfying witnesses, including projected model views.

knowledge_statements.title: Satisfying Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model relation for propositional formulas and CNF instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a propositional formula over variables \(X_F\), and let \(\alpha:X\to\{0,1\}\) be total on a set \(X\supseteq X_F\). The assignment \(\alpha\) is a satisfying model of \(F\), written \(\alpha\models F\), exactly when recursive evaluation gives \(F(\alpha)=1\). The model set is \(\operatorname{Mod}(F)=\{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^{X_F}:\alpha\models F\}\); the formula is satisfiable exactly when this set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A satisfying model is a total assignment making the formula true; satisfiability means that at least one such assignment exists.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) has finitely many occurring variables \(X_F\).
\(\alpha\) assigns every variable in \(X_F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable if and only if \(\operatorname{Mod}(F)\neq\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The model relation, model set, and satisfiability equivalence are precise and definition is the correct content kind, but no relevant source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Residual Instances
children.top_down_role: Instances remaining after variables or literals receive fixed values.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CNF residual obtained by simplifying under a partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a clause-set and \(\rho:D\to\{0,1\}\) a partial assignment. The residual instance \(F\!estriction_{\rho}\) is obtained by deleting every clause containing a literal made true by \(\rho\), and deleting from each remaining clause every literal made false by \(\rho\). Unassigned literals are retained. The appearance of the empty clause records contradiction under \(\rho\), while deletion of all clauses yields the empty, hence true, instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a CNF deletes satisfied clauses and false literals from the others; an empty clause signals contradiction and no remaining clauses signal success.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite clause-set over \(X\).
\(\rho:D\to\{0,1\}\) with \(D\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\!\restriction_{\rho}\) is a clause-set over \(X\setminus D\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual clause-set construction and empty-clause conventions are mathematically precise, and representation fits the leaf. Relevant inspectable evidence is absent.

children.title: Restriction–Extension Relationships
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between partial assignments, residual solutions, and extensions to original instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction–Extension Relationships
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between models extending a partial assignment and models of its residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a clause-set over \(X\), let \(\rho:D\to\{0,1\}\), and let \(\beta:X\setminus D\to\{0,1\}\). Because their domains are disjoint, \(\rho\cup\beta\) is a total assignment on \(X\). Then \(\rho\cup\beta\models F\) if and only if \(\beta\models F\!\restriction_{\rho}\). Hence \(\rho\) extends to a model of \(F\) exactly when the residual instance is satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completing a partial assignment satisfies the original CNF exactly when the completion satisfies the residual CNF on the unassigned variables.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite clause-set over \(X\).
\(\rho\) and \(\beta\) have complementary disjoint domains \(D\) and \(X\setminus D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\cup\beta\models F\iff\beta\models F\!\restriction_{\rho}\), and \(\rho\) has a satisfying extension if and only if \(F\!\restriction_{\rho}\) is satisfiable.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restriction-extension equivalence has explicit complementary domains and a correct conclusion, and property fits the leaf. No relevant citation or locator supports it.

children.title: SAT Decision Tasks
children.top_down_role: Yes-or-no satisfiability questions for propositional instances.

knowledge_statements.title: SAT Decision Tasks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines propositional satisfiability as a binary decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite propositional formula \(F\) over variables \(V=\operatorname{Var}(F)\), the SAT decision task returns YES exactly when there exists an assignment \(a:V\to\{0,1\}\) whose standard Boolean evaluation satisfies \(F\): \[\operatorname{SAT}(F)=\mathrm{YES}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists a\in\{0,1\}^{V}\; F(a)=1.\] It returns NO exactly when every assignment makes \(F\) false. The input representation must permit polynomial-time evaluation of \(F(a)\), as do formulas and Boolean circuits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a finite Boolean formula, decide whether some Boolean assignment makes it true.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finitely represented propositional formula.
Truth is evaluated under the standard two-valued Boolean semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SAT}(F)=\mathrm{YES}\iff \exists a\in\{0,1\}^{\operatorname{Var}(F)}\;F(a)=1\).

notation.meaning: Boolean assignment to the variables of the formula

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of propositional SAT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and knowledge kind fit the SAT Decision Tasks leaf, but no inspectable authoritative citation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Model Search Tasks
children.top_down_role: Production, enumeration interfaces, or validation of satisfying assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Search Tasks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the witness-producing search version of propositional satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SAT model-search task takes a finite propositional formula \(F\) and must output an assignment \(a:\operatorname{Var}(F)\to\{0,1\}\) satisfying \(F(a)=1\), whenever such an assignment exists. If \(F\) is unsatisfiable, the permitted output is the distinguished symbol \(\bot\). Thus a correct output function \(S\) obeys \[S(F)=a\Longrightarrow F(a)=1,\qquad S(F)=\bot\Longleftrightarrow \forall a\in\{0,1\}^{\operatorname{Var}(F)}\;F(a)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a satisfying assignment when one exists, and otherwise report that no model exists.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite propositional formula.
\(\bot\) denotes the no-model output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid nonfailure output \(a\) satisfies \(F(a)=1\), while \(\bot\) is valid exactly when \(F\) is unsatisfiable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The search-task specification is mathematically appropriate and the definition kind fits the leaf, but it lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Unsatisfiability Refutation Tasks
children.top_down_role: Production or checking of evidence that an instance has no satisfying assignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsatisfiability Refutation Tasks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies refutations relative to a sound and complete propositional proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P(F,\pi)\) be a polynomial-time decidable proof-system relation. It is an unsatisfiability refutation system when soundness and completeness hold: \[P(F,\pi)\Longrightarrow \forall a\;F(a)=0,\qquad \bigl(\forall a\;F(a)=0\bigr)\Longrightarrow \exists\pi\;P(F,\pi).\] The associated task, on an unsatisfiable formula \(F\), outputs a finite string \(\pi\) with \(P(F,\pi)\). Verification consists of checking \(P(F,\pi)\); the certificate length need not be polynomially bounded unless separately required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Produce a checkable derivation of contradiction for an unsatisfiable formula under a specified sound, complete proof system.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is polynomial-time decidable.
\(P\) is sound and complete for propositional unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For unsatisfiable \(F\), a refutation is a string \(\pi\) satisfying \(P(F,\pi)\).

notation.meaning: Verification relation for a refutation of the formula

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the refutation-task leaf, but the Cook–Reckhow-style specification has no supporting citation, and the quantified assignments in the displayed soundness and completeness conditions lack an explicit domain.

children.title: Decision–Search Reductions
children.top_down_role: Oracle and self-reduction interfaces connecting satisfiability decisions with witness recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision–Search Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses SAT self-reducibility to recover a model from decision-oracle queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a satisfiable formula \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) and a SAT decision oracle, initialize \(G_0:=F\). For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), query whether \(G_{i-1}[x_i:=0]\) is satisfiable. If YES, set \(a_i:=0\) and \(G_i:=G_{i-1}[x_i:=0]\); otherwise set \(a_i:=1\) and \(G_i:=G_{i-1}[x_i:=1]\). After \(n\) queries, output \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\). Each \(G_i\) remains satisfiable, so \(F(a)=1\). An initial oracle query detects the unsatisfiable case, giving at most \(n+1\) queries overall.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A SAT oracle recovers a satisfying assignment by fixing each variable while preserving satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: The SAT oracle answers exactly on formulas obtained by assigning variables of \(F\).
\(F\) has \(n\) listed variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model search reduces to at most \(n+1\) SAT-decision queries plus polynomial-time formula restriction.

notation.meaning: Formula remaining after fixing the first i variables

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard self-reduction of SAT search to SAT decision

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The self-reduction algorithm is standard, appropriately scoped, and correctly classified as an algorithm, but no authoritative citation with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Computation-History Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau form of the bounded nondeterministic computation used in Cook–Levin reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a nondeterministic Turing machine and let \(T=T(|x|)\ge |x|\) bound an accepting computation on input \(x\). Introduce Boolean variables describing, for every time \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\) and tape position \(j\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), the symbol, head presence, and machine state. A formula \(\Phi_{M,x,T}\) requires a unique descriptor per cell, the initial configuration for \(x\), local transition consistency between consecutive rows, and an accepting state by time \(T\). Then \[\Phi_{M,x,T}\text{ is satisfiable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M\text{ has an accepting computation on }x\text{ of length at most }T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Boolean tableau is satisfiable exactly when it describes a bounded accepting computation of the machine.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) has a finite state set and tape alphabet.
\(T(|x|)\ge |x|\) bounds the time and relevant tape region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_{M,x,T}\) is satisfiable if and only if \(M\) accepts \(x\) within \(T\) steps.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits computation-history encodings, but the precise tableau construction and its bounded-acceptance equivalence require an authoritative Cook–Levin source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Consistency Reduction Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses global computation validity through bounded-neighborhood constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a computation tableau for a fixed machine \(M\), the descriptor of a cell at time \(t+1\) is constrained by a constant-size neighborhood of row \(t\). For each location, forbid every local pattern incompatible with \(M\)'s transition relation, and conjoin these clauses with uniqueness, initialization, and acceptance constraints. Because \(M\) is fixed, every local predicate has constant arity and a constant-size CNF representation. For a \((T+1)\)-by-\(T\) tableau, their conjunction has size polynomial in \(T\) and is satisfiable exactly when all local constraints assemble into a valid accepting computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant-size neighborhood constraints enforce a globally valid accepting computation with only polynomially many clauses.
assumptions_latex: The simulated machine \(M\) is fixed.
Each transition changes only a constant-radius tape neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjunction of local constraints is polynomial in \(T\) and is satisfiable exactly for valid accepting tableaux.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local-constraint architecture of the Cook–Levin construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local-consistency representation is plausible and fits the leaf, but its constant-size CNF and global-validity claims have no inspectable supporting source.

knowledge_statements.title: Circuit-Satisfiability Reduction Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factors an NP-to-SAT reduction through witness-verification circuits and Tseitin variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\in\mathrm{NP}\) have a polynomial-time verifier \(V(x,w)\) with polynomial witness bound. For each input \(x\), polynomial-time uniform compilation produces a polynomial-size Boolean circuit \(C_x\) satisfying \[x\in L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists w\;C_x(w)=1.\] Introduce one variable for each gate and conjoin constant-size clauses enforcing every gate relation, together with a unit clause setting the output to true. The resulting Tseitin CNF \(F_x\) has size linear in \(|C_x|\) and satisfies \[F_x\text{ is satisfiable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists w\;C_x(w)=1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compile an NP verifier into a circuit, then encode its gates by an equisatisfiable polynomial-size CNF.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) has a deterministic polynomial-time verifier with polynomially bounded witnesses.
The circuit basis has fixed bounded fan-in.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(x\mapsto F_x\) is polynomial-time computable and \(x\in L\iff F_x\in\mathrm{SAT}\).

notation.meaning: Circuit computing the verifier on fixed input x
Tseitin CNF encoding of the circuit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The verifier-to-circuit-to-CNF route is correctly classified as a representation, but the uniform compilation and linear-size Tseitin claims lack a cited authoritative source and locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical SAT Reduction Network
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the principal polynomial-time reduction links surrounding canonical SAT languages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under polynomial-time many-one reductions, every language \(L\in\mathrm{NP}\) reduces to CIRCUIT-SAT and hence to SAT through a gate-consistency encoding. SAT reduces to 3-SAT by introducing auxiliary variables that replace each long clause with an equisatisfiable chain of clauses of width at most three; short clauses may be padded or retained. Conversely, 3-SAT is a restriction of SAT, and formulas are special cases of circuits. Consequently, SAT, CNF-SAT, 3-SAT, and CIRCUIT-SAT are NP-complete, with each displayed transformation preserving satisfiability and having polynomial output size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verifier circuits, SAT, CNF-SAT, and 3-SAT are connected by polynomial satisfiability-preserving reductions and are NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: Reductions are polynomial-time many-one reductions.
Auxiliary variables are permitted in equisatisfiable encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le_m^p\mathrm{CIRCUIT\text{-}SAT}\le_m^p\mathrm{SAT}\le_m^p\mathrm{3SAT}\) for every \(L\in\mathrm{NP}\), and these target problems are NP-complete.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical network of Cook–Levin and SAT normal-form reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the reduction-network leaf, but the bundled NP-completeness and reduction claims require an authoritative complexity source with precise locators.

children.title: Horn SAT
children.top_down_role: Horn clause languages, associated tractable structure, and characteristic instance regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Horn SAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-chaining decision and model construction for Horn CNF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write each Horn clause as an implication \(x_1\land\cdots\land x_k\to y\) or \(x_1\land\cdots\land x_k\to\bot\), where a Horn clause has at most one positive literal. Initialize \(S:=\varnothing\). Repeatedly add \(y\) to \(S\) whenever every antecedent variable of a rule with head \(y\) lies in \(S\). Reject if the antecedent of any rule with head \(\bot\) becomes contained in \(S\). Otherwise, at the fixed point, output the assignment making exactly the variables in \(S\) true. This assignment is the least model, and indexed forward chaining runs in linear time in the formula size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward chaining decides Horn satisfiability in linear time and returns the least model when one exists.
assumptions_latex: The input is a finite CNF in which each clause has at most one positive literal.
Clause occurrences are indexed for forward chaining.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Horn SAT is decidable in linear time, and every satisfiable instance has the computed least model.

notation.meaning: Set of variables derived as true

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard forward-chaining algorithm for Horn SAT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward-chaining algorithm and least-model claim fit Horn SAT, but the linear-time bound and model characterization lack an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Dual-Horn SAT
children.top_down_role: Dual-Horn clause languages, associated tractable structure, and characteristic instance regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Horn SAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decides dual-Horn satisfiability by global polarity complementation and Horn propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-Horn clause contains at most one negative literal. Given a dual-Horn CNF \(F\) over variables \(V\), form \(D(F)\) by replacing every positive literal \(x\) with \(\neg x\) and every negative literal \(\neg x\) with \(x\). Then \(D(F)\) is Horn. Run the Horn forward-chaining algorithm on \(D(F)\). If it rejects, report that \(F\) is unsatisfiable. Otherwise, if \(b:V\to\{0,1\}\) is the resulting model of \(D(F)\), output \(a:V\to\{0,1\}\) defined by \(a(x):=1-b(x)\) for every \(x\in V\). The transformation is linear, preserves formula size, and gives \(F(a)=D(F)(b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complement every literal, solve the resulting Horn formula, and complement its model back.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF over a finite variable set \(V\), with at most one negative literal per clause.
Assignments map \(V\) into \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual-Horn SAT is decidable in linear time, with models transferred by \(a(x)=1-b(x)\) for every \(x\in V\).

notation.meaning: Finite variable set of the input formula
Horn formula obtained by complementing every literal of F
Complementary assignments for F and its Horn dual

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polarity reduction of dual-Horn SAT to Horn SAT

children.title: Polarity-Duality Interface
children.top_down_role: Polarity reversal and structural correspondence between the two restricted languages.

knowledge_statements.title: Polarity-Duality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global complementation exchanges Horn and dual-Horn formulas and their models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a CNF \(F\) over variables \(V\), define its polarity dual \(D(F)\) by complementing every literal while leaving clause boundaries unchanged. For each assignment \(a:V\to\{0,1\}\), define \(\bar a(x)=1-a(x)\). Clausewise Boolean evaluation gives \[F(a)=D(F)(\bar a).\] Hence \(a\mapsto\bar a\) is a bijection between the models of \(F\) and those of \(D(F)\), and \(F\) is satisfiable exactly when \(D(F)\) is. Moreover, \(D\) is an involution and maps Horn CNFs precisely to dual-Horn CNFs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementing all literals and assignment values bijectively exchanges Horn formulas with dual-Horn formulas while preserving satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF over Boolean variables.
Polarity complementation is applied to every literal globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(a)=D(F)(\bar a)\), \(D(D(F))=F\), and Horn CNF is exchanged with dual-Horn CNF.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind exactly fits the polarity-duality leaf, and the statement is internally consistent, but no authoritative citation with a specific locator supports it.

children.title: Mixed Horn Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Language extensions or mixtures that alter tractability and closure behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Horn Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Allowing clauses from both polarity classes destroys tractability already at width three.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider CNFs of clause width at most three in which every clause is permitted to be either Horn or dual-Horn, with the choice made independently per clause. Every clause of width at most three belongs to this union: a clause with at most one positive literal is Horn, while a clause with at least two positive literals has at most one negative literal and is dual-Horn. Therefore this mixed language contains every 3-CNF formula, and its satisfiability problem is exactly 3-SAT on the same inputs. It is consequently NP-complete, despite pure Horn SAT and pure dual-Horn SAT being polynomial-time decidable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing Horn and dual-Horn clauses per clause already captures all 3-CNF formulas, making satisfiability NP-complete.
assumptions_latex: Each clause has width at most three.
Every clause may independently be Horn or dual-Horn.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Satisfiability for mixed Horn-or-dual-Horn 3-CNF is NP-complete.

notation.meaning: CNF whose clauses have width at most three

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct clause-count argument plus standard NP-completeness of 3-SAT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the width-three clause argument is coherent, but the NP-completeness conclusion lacks an authoritative 3-SAT citation with a specific locator.

children.title: 2-SAT Clause Language
children.top_down_role: Binary-clause instances and their restricted-language characteristics.

knowledge_statements.title: 2-SAT Clause Language
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Boolean language underlying the implication-graph correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A 2-SAT instance is a Boolean formula \(F=\bigwedge_{j=1}^{m}C_j\) in conjunctive normal form over variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), where every clause has the form \(C_j=(\ell_{j1}\lor\ell_{j2})\). Each \(\ell_{jt}\) is a literal \(x_i\) or \(\neg x_i\); repeated literals are permitted, so unit clauses are representable. An assignment \(a\in\{0,1\}^n\) satisfies \(F\) exactly when at least one literal in every clause evaluates to true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A 2-SAT formula is a conjunction of clauses containing at most two Boolean literals; it is satisfiable when every clause has a true literal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in\mathrm{2CNF}\) and \(a\models F\iff (\forall j)(\exists t\in\{1,2\})\,a(\ell_{jt})=1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard, but no citation is supplied. A source must also confirm the intended at-most-two convention; the LaTeX presentation uses exactly two literal positions with repetition while the plain statement says at most two literals.

children.title: Implication-Graph Representation
children.top_down_role: Directed literal graphs used to expose consequences and contradictions in binary clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Implication-Graph Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the directed-graph encoding of a 2-CNF formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a 2-CNF formula \(F\), its implication graph \(G_F=(L,E)\) has one vertex for every literal in \(L=\{x_i,
eg x_i:1\le i\le n\}\). Each clause \((p\lor q)\) contributes the arcs \((
eg p,q)\) and \((
eg q,p)\). These arcs encode the equivalent implications \(
eg p\Rightarrow q\) and \(
eg q\Rightarrow p\). Consequently, every satisfying assignment is closed under directed implication: if it makes a vertex literal true, it makes every literal reachable from that vertex true.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each binary clause becomes two directed implications between literals, producing a graph whose paths encode implications forced by the formula.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite 2-CNF formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((p\lor q)\equiv(\neg p\Rightarrow q)\land(\neg q\Rightarrow p)\).

notation.meaning: Set of positive and negative literals.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication-graph construction, path interpretation, content kind, and local scope are standard and internally consistent, but the record has no inspectable source or locator.

children.title: Strong-Component Regimes
children.top_down_role: Component structure relevant to satisfiability, contradiction localization, and solution organization.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Component Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the strong-component satisfiability criterion for finite 2-SAT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite 2-CNF formula and \(G_F\) its implication graph. Then \(F\) is satisfiable if and only if, for every variable \(x_i\), the vertices \(x_i\) and \(\neg x_i\) belong to distinct strongly connected components of \(G_F\). Thus a component containing complementary literals certifies unsatisfiability, whereas the absence of every such component guarantees a satisfying assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A 2-CNF formula is satisfiable exactly when no variable and its negation lie in the same strongly connected component.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite 2-CNF formula.
\(G_F\) is formed by the standard two-arcs-per-clause construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is satisfiable}\iff\forall i,\ \operatorname{SCC}(x_i)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(\neg x_i)\).

notation.meaning: Strongly connected component containing literal p.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated strongly connected component criterion is the standard finite 2-SAT theorem and fits the theorem container, but its biconditional and certificate claim require an authoritative theorem citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Graph-Based Witness Recovery
children.top_down_role: Assignment extraction interfaces derived from implication-graph structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Based Witness Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovers a satisfying assignment from the condensation DAG of a satisfiable 2-SAT instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a 2-CNF formula \(F\) whose implication graph passes the complementary-component test. Compute the strongly connected components and a topological ordering of their condensation DAG. Process components in reverse topological order. When neither a component \(S\) nor its complementary component \(\bar S=\{\neg p:p\in S\}\) has been assigned, set every literal in \(S\) true and every literal in \(\bar S\) false. Stop after all component pairs are assigned and output the induced variable assignment \(a(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process complementary component pairs in reverse topological order, assigning one component true and its complement false, to recover a satisfying assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite satisfiable 2-CNF formula.
No strongly connected component contains complementary literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\in\{0,1\}^n\) and \(a\models F\).

notation.meaning: Component containing the complements of literals in S.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record appropriately describes a witness-recovery algorithm, but no source verifies the chosen topological-order orientation and truth-assignment convention. Those convention-sensitive details must be checked against an authoritative algorithm statement.

children.title: Affine Boolean Systems
children.top_down_role: Boolean constraint systems represented through affine relations over a finite field.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Boolean Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines affine linear equation systems over the two-element field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An affine Boolean system consists of a matrix \(A\in\mathbb F_2^{m\times n}\), a vector \(b\in\mathbb F_2^m\), and the feasibility requirement \(Ax=b\) for \(x\in\mathbb F_2^n\). Its solution set is either empty or an affine subspace of \(\mathbb F_2^n\). If \(x_0\) is one solution, every solution is uniquely expressible as \(x=x_0+z\) with \(z\in\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine Boolean system is a linear system over the two-element field; a nonempty solution set is a translate of the nullspace.
assumptions_latex: All arithmetic is over \(\mathbb F_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\) or \(\{x:Ax=b\}=x_0+\ker A\).

notation.meaning: Nullspace of A over the two-element field.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-system definition and translate-of-kernel characterization are standard, precise, and suitable for this container, but no supporting finite-field linear-algebra source is cited.

children.title: XOR-SAT Instances
children.top_down_role: Parity-clause presentations and their satisfiability structure.

knowledge_statements.title: XOR-SAT Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines XOR clauses and their conjunctive satisfiability semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An XOR-SAT instance over Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) is a conjunction of parity clauses. Each clause has the form \(\ell_{i_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\ell_{i_k}=c\), where each \(\ell_{i_t}\) is a literal, \(c\in\{0,1\}\), and \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two. An assignment satisfies the instance exactly when the parity equation of every clause holds. Clause arities may vary unless a fixed-width XOR-SAT language is specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An XOR-SAT formula is a conjunction of Boolean parity equations, each requiring its literals’ modulo-two sum to equal a prescribed bit.
assumptions_latex: Variables and clause constants take values in \(\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\models F\iff\forall j,\ \bigoplus_{t=1}^{k_j}a(\ell_{j,t})=c_j\).

notation.meaning: Required parity bit of clause j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated parity semantics are coherent, but XOR-SAT conventions differ over whether literals, variables, and explicit parity constants are allowed. A specific source and locator are required for this chosen language.

children.title: Affine–XOR Translation
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between equation-system and parity-clause presentations.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine–XOR Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the exact translation between XOR clauses and affine equations over \(\mathbb F_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Identify false and true with \(0\) and \(1\). For a literal \(\ell_t\) on variable \(x_{i_t}\), write its value as \(x_{i_t}+s_t\) in \(\mathbb F_2\), where \(s_t=0\) for \(x_{i_t}\) and \(s_t=1\) for \(\neg x_{i_t}\). Then the XOR clause \(\ell_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\ell_k=c\) is equivalent to the affine equation \(\sum_{t=1}^{k}x_{i_t}=c+\sum_{t=1}^{k}s_t\pmod 2\). Translating every clause yields \(Ax=b\), with exactly the same satisfying assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each negated literal by one plus its variable modulo two; every XOR clause then becomes an equivalent affine equation.
assumptions_latex: Boolean values are identified with elements of \(\mathbb F_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\models F_{\mathrm{XOR}}\iff Aa=b\text{ over }\mathbb F_2\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient matrix and right-hand side after translation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The literal-to-affine translation over the two-element field is mathematically consistent and fits a representation container, but the exact equivalence has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Rank-Sensitive Solution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Solution-space behavior organized by dependence, rank, and redundant constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Sensitive Solution Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies consistency and solution count by finite-field ranks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb F_2^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb F_2^m\), and \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\). The affine system \(Ax=b\) is consistent exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}([A\mid b])\). If consistent, its solution set has affine dimension \(n-r\) and contains exactly \(2^{n-r}\) assignments. In particular, the solution is unique exactly when the system is consistent and \(r=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal coefficient and augmented ranks characterize consistency; a consistent rank-r system in n variables has exactly 2^(n-r) solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are finite-dimensional over \(\mathbb F_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\text{ is consistent}\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}([A\mid b])\), and then \(|\{x:Ax=b\}|=2^{n-r}\).

notation.meaning: Rank of A over the two-element field.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank consistency criterion and solution count are standard and correctly specialized to finite systems over the two-element field. They nevertheless require a cited linear-algebra result; the source should also support treating this combined result as a property rather than a theorem in the terminal container.

children.title: Bounded-Clause-Width SAT
children.top_down_role: SAT languages restricted by a fixed upper bound on literals per clause.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Clause-Width SAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines SAT restricted by maximum clause width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(k\ge 1\), a bounded-clause-width SAT instance is a conjunctive-normal-form formula \(F=\bigwedge_{j=1}^{m}C_j\) in which every clause satisfies \(|C_j|\le k\). The associated decision problem, \(k\)-SAT, asks whether there exists a Boolean assignment satisfying all clauses. Under the at-most-width convention, clauses shorter than \(k\), including unit clauses, are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: k-SAT asks whether a CNF formula whose clauses contain at most k literals has a satisfying Boolean assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a fixed positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in k\text{-CNF}\iff\max_j|C_j|\le k\).

notation.meaning: Number of literals in clause j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent under the explicitly stated at-most-width convention, but literature also uses exactly-k clauses. No authoritative SAT source with a specific locator is supplied for the selected convention.

children.title: Bounded-Variable-Occurrence SAT
children.top_down_role: SAT languages restricted by how often each variable may appear.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable-Occurrence SAT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines SAT restricted by total literal occurrences per variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(d\ge 0\), a bounded-variable-occurrence SAT instance is a CNF formula \(F\) such that each variable \(x_i\) occurs, counting both positive and negative literals and counting multiplicity, in at most \(d\) clause positions. Writing \(\operatorname{occ}_F(x_i)\) for this total, the restriction is \(\max_i\operatorname{occ}_F(x_i)\le d\). The decision question remains whether \(F\) admits a satisfying Boolean assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Occurrence-bounded SAT limits each variable’s total positive and negative appearances to d while retaining the ordinary CNF satisfiability question.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is a fixed nonnegative integer.
Occurrences are counted with multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in\mathrm{SAT}[\operatorname{occ}\le d]\iff\forall i,\ \operatorname{occ}_F(x_i)\le d\).

notation.meaning: Total occurrences of variable i in F, irrespective of polarity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record clearly defines total polarity-independent occurrences with multiplicity and fits a definition container, but this convention-sensitive restriction has no supporting citation.

children.title: Joint Width–Occurrence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Combined restrictions whose interaction changes expressiveness or complexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Width–Occurrence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the two-parameter family combining clause-width and variable-occurrence restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed integers \(k\ge 1\) and \(d\ge 0\), a CNF formula \(F=\bigwedge_j C_j\) belongs to the joint width–occurrence regime \(\mathrm{SAT}(k,d)\) exactly when \(|C_j|\le k\) for every clause and \(\operatorname{occ}_F(x_i)\le d\) for every variable. Satisfiability is then studied with \((k,d)\) fixed rather than encoded as part of the input. Membership in a smaller parameter pair implies membership in every coordinatewise larger pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SAT(k,d) consists of CNF formulas with clause width at most k and total occurrence at most d for every variable.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) and \(d\) are fixed integers with \(k\ge1\) and \(d\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in\mathrm{SAT}(k,d)\iff(\forall j,|C_j|\le k)\land(\forall i,\operatorname{occ}_F(x_i)\le d)\).

notation.meaning: Jointly width- and occurrence-bounded CNF family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint restriction and coordinatewise monotonicity claim are mathematically consistent and fit a condition container. A source is required for the SAT(k,d) convention and for treating both parameters as fixed rather than input data.

children.title: Restriction Threshold Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Parameter values separating tractable, hard, or structurally exceptional language classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Threshold Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records classical width and occurrence boundaries separating tractable and NP-complete SAT restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under polynomial-time many-one reductions, SAT for clauses of width at most two is solvable in polynomial time, while 3-SAT is NP-complete. Moreover, bounding occurrences alone does not generally restore tractability: 3-SAT remains NP-complete when every variable occurs in at most four clauses. Hence fixed width and fixed occurrence are not individually sufficient explanations of tractability; the exact parameter values and any additional structural restrictions determine the regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The width boundary lies between 2-SAT and 3-SAT, and 3-SAT remains NP-complete even with at most four occurrences per variable.
assumptions_latex: Complexity is measured for finite explicitly represented CNF formulas.
Occurrence counts include both polarities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{2SAT}\in\mathrm P\), whereas \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) and occurrence-at-most-four \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) are NP-complete.

notation.meaning: Satisfiability of CNF formulas with clauses of width at most three.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, but the NP-completeness assertions require exact theorem citations. In particular, the occurrence-at-most-four result depends on conventions concerning clause width, repeated literals, and whether occurrences or distinct containing clauses are counted.

children.title: Schaefer Dichotomy Interface
children.top_down_role: Navigation to the Boolean constraint-language classification without duplicating the broader constraint-satisfaction treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Schaefer Dichotomy Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Boolean constraint languages under the classical Schaefer satisfiability model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma\) be a finite set of finitary relations on \(\{0,1\}\), and let \(\operatorname{SAT}(\Gamma)\) ask whether a conjunction of constraints using relations from \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable. The problem is polynomial-time solvable if every relation in \(\Gamma\) is simultaneously of one of the following types: Horn, dual-Horn, bijunctive, affine, \(0\)-valid, or \(1\)-valid. If none of these six uniform conditions holds for \(\Gamma\), then \(\operatorname{SAT}(\Gamma)\) is NP-complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite Boolean constraint language yields either polynomial-time satisfiability through one of six closure types or an NP-complete problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is finite and Boolean.
Constraints may reuse variables and are combined conjunctively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SAT}(\Gamma)\in\mathrm{P}\) under one of the six uniform classes; otherwise \(\operatorname{SAT}(\Gamma)\) is NP-complete.

notation.meaning: satisfiability problem over constraints from Gamma

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the Schaefer dichotomy interface and is stated in the standard finite Boolean constraint-language setting, but it has no citation. The supplied local inventory contains no source supporting Schaefer's dichotomy, so the six tractable cases and NP-completeness conclusion cannot be evidence-reviewed.

knowledge_statements.title: Formula-Graph Width Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard primal, incidence, and dual graph representations of a CNF formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a CNF formula \(F\), its primal graph \(G_p(F)\) has vertex set \(\operatorname{var}(F)\), joining distinct variables that occur together in a clause. Its incidence graph \(G_i(F)\) is bipartite on \(\operatorname{var}(F)\cup F\), with an edge for each variable-clause incidence. Its dual graph \(G_d(F)\) has the clauses as vertices, joining clauses sharing a variable. The corresponding width parameters are \(\operatorname{tw}(G_p(F))\), \(\operatorname{tw}(G_i(F))\), and \(\operatorname{tw}(G_d(F))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CNF formula induces primal, incidence, and clause-dual graphs; their treewidths measure different forms of variable-clause interaction.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\mapsto\bigl(\operatorname{tw}(G_p(F)),\operatorname{tw}(G_i(F)),\operatorname{tw}(G_d(F))\bigr)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard CNF graph representations and treewidth parameters
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the primal, incidence, and clause-dual graph descriptions are mathematically standard. No SAT-specific source or inspectable locator is supplied; a source should also state the convention for formulas with duplicate clauses when defining the dual graph.

children.title: Strong Backdoor Sets
children.top_down_role: Backdoor parameters requiring every relevant assignment branch to enter a selected tractable class.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Backdoor Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment backdoors into a fixed tractable class of CNF formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula and \(\mathcal C\) a class of CNF formulas. A set \(B\subseteq\operatorname{var}(F)\) is a strong \(\mathcal C\)-backdoor set if, for every truth assignment \(\tau:B\to\{0,1\}\), the simplified residual formula \(F[\tau]\) belongs to \(\mathcal C\). Here simplification deletes clauses satisfied by \(\tau\) and removes falsified literals from all remaining clauses. The strong backdoor number is the minimum cardinality of such a set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong backdoor reaches the target class under every assignment to its variables; its minimum size is the strong backdoor number.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(\mathcal C\) is a specified target class of CNF formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sbd}_{\mathcal C}(F)=\min\{|B|:B\subseteq\operatorname{var}(F),\ \forall\tau:B\to\{0,1\},\ F[\tau]\in\mathcal C\}\).

notation.meaning: strong backdoor number into the target class

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind and universal-assignment condition fit strong backdoor sets, but no supporting source is cited. An authoritative definition is also needed to confirm the intended target-class assumptions or the convention for the backdoor number when no strong backdoor exists.

children.title: Weak Backdoor Sets
children.top_down_role: Backdoor parameters based on the existence of a favorable assignment branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Backdoor Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Satisfying assignment backdoors into a fixed tractable CNF class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula and \(\mathcal C\) a class of CNF formulas. A set \(B\subseteq\operatorname{var}(F)\) is a weak \(\mathcal C\)-backdoor set if there exists an assignment \(\tau:B\to\{0,1\}\) such that the simplified residual formula \(F[\tau]\) belongs to \(\mathcal C\) and is satisfiable. The weak backdoor number is the minimum cardinality of such a set, with value \(\infty\) when no weak backdoor exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak backdoor has at least one assignment producing a satisfiable residual formula in the target class.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(\mathcal C\) is a specified target class of CNF formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{wbd}_{\mathcal C}(F)=\min\{|B|:\exists\tau:B\to\{0,1\},\ F[\tau]\in\mathcal C\text{ and }F[\tau]\text{ is satisfiable}\}\).

notation.meaning: weak backdoor number into the target class

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes a weak backdoor by requiring one assignment whose residual is both in the target class and satisfiable. It nevertheless lacks any source reference or inspectable locator, and the local inventory does not cover SAT backdoors.

children.title: Structural Modulators
children.top_down_role: Deletion or modification sets measuring distance from a structurally restricted instance class.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Modulators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-deletion distance of a formula representation to a chosen structural graph class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a graph representation \(G(F)\) of each CNF formula \(F\) and a graph class \(\mathcal H\). A structural modulator of \(F\) to \(\mathcal H\) is a vertex set \(X\subseteq V(G(F))\) such that \(G(F)-X\in\mathcal H\). Its modulator number is \(\operatorname{mod}_{\mathcal H}(F)=\min\{|X|:G(F)-X\in\mathcal H\}\). The definition depends on the selected representation, such as the primal or incidence graph, and on whether deletable vertices may represent variables, clauses, or both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structural modulator deletes representation-graph vertices until the remaining graph belongs to a prescribed structural class.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(G(F)\) and the admissible deletion vertices are fixed.
\(\mathcal H\) is a specified graph class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\text{ is a modulator}\iff X\subseteq V(G(F))\text{ and }G(F)-X\in\mathcal H\).

notation.meaning: chosen graph representation of the formula

No source supports this formula-specific formulation or notation, so an authoritative locator specifying the representation and admissible deleted vertices is required.

children.title: Target-Class Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of parameter usefulness on the chosen tractable or structural target class.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Class Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic dependence of assignment-backdoor numbers on the target class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal D\) be target classes. Every strong \(\mathcal C\)-backdoor is a strong \(\mathcal D\)-backdoor, so \(\operatorname{sbd}_{\mathcal D}(F)\leq\operatorname{sbd}_{\mathcal C}(F)\). Every weak \(\mathcal C\)-backdoor is likewise a weak \(\mathcal D\)-backdoor, so \(\operatorname{wbd}_{\mathcal D}(F)\leq\operatorname{wbd}_{\mathcal C}(F)\). Thus backdoor size is not intrinsic to \(F\); enlarging the target class can only decrease, and may strictly decrease, either parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backdoor numbers depend on the target class and cannot increase when that class is enlarged.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal D\) are classes interpreted with the same residual-formula convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sbd}_{\mathcal D}(F)\leq\operatorname{sbd}_{\mathcal C}(F)\) and \(\operatorname{wbd}_{\mathcal D}(F)\leq\operatorname{wbd}_{\mathcal C}(F)\).

notation.meaning: strong backdoor number into class C
weak backdoor number into class C

children.title: Clause–Variable Deficiency
children.top_down_role: Clause-count imbalance relative to the variable set and its structural refinements.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause–Variable Deficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global clause surplus for a finite CNF formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite CNF formula \(F\), let \(c(F)\) be its number of clauses and let \(n(F)=|\operatorname{var}(F)|\) count variables occurring in at least one clause. The clause-variable deficiency of \(F\) is the integer \(\delta(F)=c(F)-n(F)\). For a clause-set presentation, duplicate clauses are counted or removed according to the declared convention; the convention must therefore remain fixed when deficiency is compared across formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause-variable deficiency is the number of clauses minus the number of variables that actually occur in the formula.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula with a fixed duplicate-clause convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta(F)=c(F)-|\operatorname{var}(F)|\).

notation.meaning: number of occurring variables in F

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches clause-variable deficiency and explicitly notes the duplicate-clause convention. No SAT or clause-set source is cited, however, and none of the inventoried sources supports this definition or convention.

children.title: Variable-Occurrence Parameters
children.top_down_role: Frequency-based measures for variables across clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Occurrence Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-variable and aggregate clause-incidence counts in CNF formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite CNF formula \(F\) and variable \(x\in\operatorname{var}(F)\), define \(d_F(x)=|\{C\in F:x\in C\text{ or }\neg x\in C\}|\), counting each clause once even if the presentation repeats a literal. The maximum and minimum variable occurrences are \(\Delta_v(F)=\max_x d_F(x)\) and \(\delta_v(F)=\min_x d_F(x)\). The total variable-clause incidence count is \(L(F)=\sum_x d_F(x)=\sum_{C\in F}|\operatorname{var}(C)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-occurrence parameters count how many clauses contain each variable and summarize these counts by minima, maxima, or totals.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Clauses contain no repeated occurrence of the same variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(F)=\sum_{x\in\operatorname{var}(F)}d_F(x)=\sum_{C\in F}|\operatorname{var}(C)|\).

notation.meaning: number of clauses containing variable x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard CNF occurrence and incidence counts
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The occurrence and incidence formulas are standard under the stated clause convention, but there is no supporting citation. A source-backed revision should also specify whether the empty-variable case is excluded or how the minimum and maximum over an empty variable set are defined.

children.title: Literal-Occurrence Profiles
children.top_down_role: Polarity-sensitive frequency patterns and degree distributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Occurrence Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed occurrence data refining unsigned variable degrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each variable \(x\) of a finite CNF formula \(F\), define \(d_F^+(x)=|\{C\in F:x\in C\}|\) and \(d_F^-(x)=|\{C\in F:\neg x\in C\}|\). The literal-occurrence profile is the indexed multiset \(P(F)=\{(d_F^+(x),d_F^-(x)):x\in\operatorname{var}(F)\}\). It refines the unsigned occurrence sequence because \(d_F(x)=d_F^+(x)+d_F^-(x)\), while the imbalance \(b_F(x)=d_F^+(x)-d_F^-(x)\) records polarity asymmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A literal-occurrence profile records positive and negative clause counts separately for every variable, exposing polarity imbalance hidden by unsigned degrees.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Clauses contain no repeated literal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(F)=\{(d_F^+(x),d_F^-(x)):x\in\operatorname{var}(F)\}\) and \(d_F(x)=d_F^+(x)+d_F^-(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: signed refinement of standard occurrence counts
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

Moreover, the assumption that clauses contain no repeated literal does not exclude a clause containing both x and its negation; under the prerequisite's clause-counting definition this can invalidate d_F(x)=d_F^+(x)+d_F^-(x). A source is needed to establish the intended non-tautological clause convention before fixing the statement.

children.title: Joint Deficiency–Occurrence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instance classes organized through simultaneous imbalance and frequency constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Deficiency–Occurrence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined structural parameterization by clause surplus and occurrence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite CNF formula \(F\), a joint deficiency-occurrence regime is specified by a parameter vector such as \(J(F)=(\delta(F),\Delta_v(F),\Delta_\ell(F))\), where \(\Delta_\ell(F)=\max_{\ell}d_F(\ell)\) ranges over literals. A bounded regime with constants \(a,b,c\) is the class \(\mathcal R_{a,b,c}=\{F:\delta(F)\leq a,\ \Delta_v(F)\leq b,\ \Delta_\ell(F)\leq c\}\). Bounds may be imposed independently; none is determined by deficiency alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint regimes classify formulas simultaneously by clause-variable deficiency, maximum variable occurrence, and maximum signed-literal occurrence.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(a,b,c\) are fixed integer bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in\mathcal R_{a,b,c}\iff\delta(F)\leq a,\ \Delta_v(F)\leq b,\ \Delta_\ell(F)\leq c\).

notation.meaning: regime defined by the three bounds

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

The symbol d_F(ell) is not defined, and the maximum over literals is undefined for a formula with no occurring literals unless a convention or nonempty-domain assumption is added. An authoritative source is required to determine the intended coordinates and conventions.

children.title: Random k-CNF Models
children.top_down_role: Canonical distributions for randomly generated fixed-width CNF instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Random k-CNF Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform fixed-size random CNF model with independently sampled clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix integers \(n\geq k\geq1\) and \(m\geq0\). In the uniform random \(k\)-CNF model \(F_k(n,m)\), each of the \(m\) clauses is sampled independently and uniformly, with replacement, from the \(2^k\binom{n}{k}\) non-tautological clauses containing \(k\) distinct variables from \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\), each assigned an independent polarity. The resulting ordered sample may contain duplicate clauses; a without-replacement model is distinct and must be identified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uniform random k-CNF model samples m independent signed k-clauses over n variables, usually with replacement.
assumptions_latex: \(n\geq k\geq1\) and \(m\geq0\) are integers.
Every sampled clause uses distinct variables and is non-tautological.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_k(n,m)\sim\operatorname{Unif}\bigl((\mathcal C_{n,k})^m\bigr)\), where \(|\mathcal C_{n,k}|=2^k\binom{n}{k}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard fixed-size uniform random k-SAT model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the random k-CNF model, and the stated sample space has the claimed cardinality. Because random-SAT literature uses several non-equivalent sampling conventions, the with-replacement ordered model requires an explicit authoritative citation and locator; none is supplied.

children.title: Clause-Density Parameters
children.top_down_role: Density controls used to organize random-instance behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Density Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-to-variable scaling parameter for random CNF sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a CNF formula with \(n\geq1\) variables and \(m\) clauses, its clause density is \(\alpha=m/n\). In an asymptotic random \(k\)-CNF sequence, one fixes \(k\) and a real \(\alpha\geq0\), lets \(n\to\infty\), and chooses an integer clause count satisfying \(m(n)/n\to\alpha\), commonly \(m(n)=\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\). Thus constant-density regimes have \(m=\Theta(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause density is the clause-to-variable ratio; constant-density random-CNF regimes use a linear number of clauses.
assumptions_latex: \(n\geq1\) and \(m\geq0\).
For asymptotics, \(k\) and \(\alpha\) are fixed while \(n\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha=\frac{m}{n}\), and \(m(n)/n\to\alpha\) in the associated asymptotic regime.

notation.meaning: number of clauses at size n

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind and asymptotic scaling statement fit clause-density parameters. The formulas are standard, but the record has no source reference, and the supplied inventory contains no random-SAT source supporting the fixed-k, constant-density convention.

children.title: Satisfiability Threshold Regimes
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic regions surrounding transitions between typical satisfiable and unsatisfiable behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Satisfiability Threshold Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic threshold regimes for a fixed random-CNF model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{n,m}^{(k)}\) be random \(k\)-CNF on \(n\) variables with \(m\) independently sampled clauses, and put \(p_n(\alpha)=\Pr(F_{n,\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor}^{(k)}\text{ is satisfiable})\). A constant \(\alpha_k\) is a sharp satisfiability threshold when, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[p_n(\alpha_k-\varepsilon)\longrightarrow 1,\qquad p_n(\alpha_k+\varepsilon)\longrightarrow 0.\] Densities bounded below and above these values form the satisfiable and unsatisfiable regimes, respectively. More generally, a threshold sequence \(r_k(n)\) satisfies the analogous limits after replacing \(\alpha_k\) by \(r_k(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold separates clause densities where random k-CNF is satisfiable with probability tending to one from densities where that probability tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(k\ge 2\) is fixed.
\(n\to\infty\) and \(m=\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_n(\alpha_k-\varepsilon)\to1\) and \(p_n(\alpha_k+\varepsilon)\to0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: Random k-CNF formula with n variables and m clauses.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard asymptotic definition of a sharp random-SAT threshold
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the threshold-regime leaf and its content kind, but no inspectable citation is supplied. The clause-sampling convention is not fixed, and the final threshold-sequence sentence does not specify whether the sequence is a density or clause-count threshold, so the exact mathematical version requires a source.

children.title: Finite-Size Scaling Windows
children.top_down_role: Threshold broadening and empirical transition behavior for bounded instance sizes.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Size Scaling Windows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling-window definition relative to a chosen probability interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0<q_-<q_+<1\), define the finite-size transition window of \(F_{n,m}^{(k)}\) by \[W_n(q_-,q_+)=\{\alpha\ge0:q_-\le p_n(\alpha)\le q_+\}.\] If \(p_n\) is nonincreasing, its width is \(w_n=\sup W_n-
obreak\inf W_n\) whenever the set is nonempty. A finite-size scaling law with center \(\alpha_n\), scale \(w_n>0\), and profile \(G\) holds when \[p_n(\alpha_n+t w_n)\longrightarrow G(t)\] at every continuity point of the nonincreasing function \(G:\mathbb R\to[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaling window is the density interval where satisfiability probability is neither near zero nor near one; rescaling it may yield a limiting profile.
assumptions_latex: \(p_n(\alpha)=\Pr(F_{n,\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor}^{(k)}\text{ is satisfiable})\) is nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_n(\alpha_n+t w_n)\to G(t)\) at continuity points of \(G\).

children.title: Solution-Cluster Geometry
children.top_down_role: Organization of satisfying assignments into separated regions under natural adjacency notions.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Cluster Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial clusters under single-variable satisfying moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a satisfiable CNF formula \(F\) on variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), let \(S(F)\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be its satisfying assignments. Form the graph \(G_F=(S(F),E_F)\), where \(\{u,v\}\in E_F\) exactly when the Hamming distance satisfies \(d_H(u,v)=1\). A solution cluster is a connected component \(C\) of \(G_F\). Its internal diameter is \(\max_{u,v\in C}d_H(u,v)\), and the separation of distinct clusters \(C,D\) is \(d_H(C,D)=\min_{u\in C,v\in D}d_H(u,v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Satisfying assignments form a Hamming graph; its connected components are solution clusters, characterized by their diameters and mutual separations.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a satisfiable CNF formula on \(n\) Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\subseteq S(F)\) is a solution cluster exactly when \(C\) is a connected component of \(G_F\).

notation.meaning: Set of satisfying assignments of F.
Graph of single-bit moves between satisfying assignments.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard combinatorial definition of SAT solution clusters
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
