children.title: Frozen-Variable Structure
children.top_down_role: Variables constrained to fixed values within clusters or across the full solution space.

knowledge_statements.title: Frozen-Variable Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frozen variables are defined relative to one solution cluster.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a solution cluster of a satisfiable formula \(F\). A variable \(x_i\) is frozen in \(C\) when there exists \(b_i\in\{0,1\}\) such that \(u_i=b_i\) for every \(u\in C\); otherwise it is unfrozen in \(C\). The frozen set and frozen pattern are \[\operatorname{Fr}(C)=\{i:u_i=v_i\text{ for all }u,v\in C\},\qquad b_C=(b_i)_{i\in\operatorname{Fr}(C)}.\] Thus every assignment in \(C\) agrees with \(b_C\) on \(\operatorname{Fr}(C)\), while each unfrozen coordinate assumes both Boolean values somewhere in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable is frozen in a cluster when every assignment in that cluster gives it the same value.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty solution cluster of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in\operatorname{Fr}(C)\iff (\exists b_i\in\{0,1\})(\forall u\in C)\,u_i=b_i\).

notation.meaning: Indices of variables frozen in cluster C.

children.title: Clustering Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Random-instance regions where solution-space organization changes qualitatively.

knowledge_statements.title: Clustering Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational asymptotic definition based on extensive cluster count and separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_n(\alpha)\) be a random satisfiable CNF ensemble and let \(N_n(\alpha)\) be the number of connected components of its satisfying-assignment graph. A density interval is exponentially clustered when constants \(c,\delta>0\) exist such that, conditional on satisfiability, \[\Pr\!\left(N_n(\alpha)\ge e^{cn}\ \text{and}\ \min_{C\ne D}d_H(C,D)\ge\delta n\right)\longrightarrow1.\] A clustering transition value \(\alpha_{m cl}\\) is a boundary at which this property changes from absent below \(\alpha_{m cl}\) to present above it, within the satisfiable regime. The definition depends on the ensemble and cluster adjacency convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clustering transition marks the onset of exponentially many solution components separated by linear Hamming distance, under a specified random-CNF model and adjacency rule.
assumptions_latex: \(F_n(\alpha)\) specifies a random-CNF ensemble.
Clusters use the fixed single-variable satisfying-move convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_n(\alpha)\ge e^{cn}\) and \(d_H(C,D)\ge\delta n\) hold with conditional probability tending to one in the clustered regime.

children.title: Geometry-Induced Search Hardness
children.top_down_role: Search difficulties associated with separation, rigidity, or frozen-variable effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Induced Search Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A rigorous limitation for search restricted to satisfying local moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) have two solution clusters \(C\) and \(D\) with \(d_H(C,D)>r\). Any search method whose state is always a satisfying assignment and whose update changes at most \(r\) variables cannot move from \(C\) to \(D\): every such update path remains inside its initial connected component in the graph joining satisfying assignments at Hamming distance at most \(r\). Consequently, separated-cluster geometry certifies failure of this restricted local-search model to explore all solutions. It does not, by itself, establish worst-case or average-case hardness for algorithms allowed to traverse unsatisfying assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clusters separated beyond the permitted move radius trap searches that must remain satisfying, but this alone does not prove general SAT hardness.
assumptions_latex: \(C,D\subseteq S(F)\) are distinct clusters under radius-\(r\) adjacency.
Every search update preserves satisfiability and changes at most \(r\) variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_0\in C\implies u_t\notin D\) for every iterate \(u_t\) of the restricted search.

notation.meaning: Maximum Hamming radius of one search update.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct graph-connectivity obstruction for solution-preserving local search
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated conclusion does not follow merely from \(d_H(C,D)>r\) when \(C\) and \(D\) are clusters under the earlier radius-one convention: an admissible radius-r path could pass through satisfying assignments in other radius-one clusters. The assumptions instead redefine them as radius-r components, making the argument tautological and inconsistent with the statement's cluster terminology. The failure-boundary content kind fits the leaf, but this record is mathematically unsound as written.

children.title: Boolean-to-CNF Encoding Calculus
children.top_down_role: Translation families, constraint-specific constructions, representation tradeoffs, and reconstruction obligations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2: CNF Encodings; Chapter 13: Symmetry and Satisfiability

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent CNF Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truth-equivalent CNF obtained by exhaustive propositional distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a Boolean formula \(\varphi\), first eliminate implications and equivalences, push negations to atoms, and repeatedly apply \[A\lor(B\land C)\equiv(A\lor B)\land(A\lor C)\] and its symmetric form until a conjunction of disjunctions of literals is obtained. Denote the result by \(\operatorname{CNF}_{\rm eq}(\varphi)\). For every assignment \(a\) to the original variables, \[a\models\varphi\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\models\operatorname{CNF}_{\rm eq}(\varphi).\] No auxiliary variables are introduced. The number of clauses can be exponential in the size of \(\varphi\), because distributing a disjunction over several conjunctions forms Cartesian products of their clause sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive distribution produces a CNF equivalent on every original assignment, but its number of clauses may grow exponentially.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is a finite propositional formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi\equiv\operatorname{CNF}_{\rm eq}(\varphi)\), possibly with exponentially larger representation size.

notation.meaning: Truth-equivalent distributive CNF expansion of φ.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary propositional distributivity and known expansion-size behavior
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind and truth-equivalence claim fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the transformation procedure and exponential-size behavior. Standard-field rationale alone is insufficient for this review.

knowledge_statements.title: Tseitin Definitional Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-size equisatisfiable encoding using one variable per subformula or gate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a Boolean formula DAG with output node \(o\). Introduce a variable \(v_g\) for every noninput node \(g\). For each gate \(g=f(g_1,\ldots,g_t)\), add a constant-size CNF template equivalent to \(v_g\leftrightarrow f(v_{g_1},\ldots,v_{g_t})\), and add the unit clause \((v_o)\). assumptions_latex: The variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are Boolean.

The exactly-one constraint is represented by \[F_{\mathrm{pw}}\land(x_1\lor\cdots\lor x_n).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forbid every pair of selection variables from being simultaneously true. Adding one clause requiring some variable to be true yields an exactly-one encoding.

At an internal node with child vectors \(a_1,\ldots,a_r\) and \(b_1,\ldots,b_s\), introduce \(o_1,\ldots,o_{r+s}\) and a CNF encoding of \[o_t\leftrightarrow\left(\sum_{p=1}^r a_p+\sum_{q=1}^s b_q\ge t\right),\qquad 1\le t\le r+s,\] under the invariant that each child vector is unary and monotone. Hence the unit clause \((\neg o_{k+1})\) represents \(\sum_i x_i\le k\); asserting \(o_k\) similarly represents a lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any full binary tree \(T\) with the same \(n\) input leaves, correct untruncated totalizer merges make the root output satisfy \(o_t\leftrightarrow\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge t\), independently of tree shape. eg o_{b+1}),\] or equivalently invoke an incremental SAT solver on \(F_T\) under the assumption literal \(

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparator network specialized to the leading outputs needed by an at-most-\(k\) bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\le k<n\). A cardinality network for this bound has retained outputs \(y_1,\ldots,y_{k+1}\) satisfying \[y_j\leftrightarrow\left(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge j\right),\qquad 1\le j\le k+1.\] Encode each comparator retained by the chosen cardinality-network construction using full CNF equivalences for its maximum and minimum outputs. The resulting CNF together with the unit clause \((\neg y_{k+1})\) has, after projection onto \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), exactly the models satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le k\). The specialization need not expose thresholds beyond \(k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integer bound from zero through n minus one, a cardinality network computes the leading thresholds through k+1. Setting output k+1 false yields an at-most-k encoding.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality-Network Encodings

children.title: Comparator Topology Families
children.top_down_role: Network organizations that determine depth, size, regularity, and propagation behavior.

assumptions_latex: The inputs are Boolean variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).
Every comparator maps \((p,q)\) to \((p\lor q,p\land q)\), with outputs ordered nonincreasingly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every input assignment, the terminal wires satisfy \(y_j=1\iff \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge j\).

notation.meaning: Directed acyclic comparator network on n Boolean wires

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines topology families extensionally through comparator placement and the sorting property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A comparator topology is a layered directed acyclic network \(N=(L_1,\ldots,L_d)\), where each layer \(L_t\) contains pairwise wire-disjoint comparators. A topology family \((N_n)_{n\ge 1}\) is a sorting-network family when, for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), evaluating each comparator as \((p,q)\mapsto(p\lor q,p\land q)\) produces outputs \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\) satisfying \(y_j=1\iff\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge j\). Distinct families are determined by their comparator incidence, layering, size, and depth; their Tseitin encodings differ accordingly while representing the same sorted-output relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A comparator topology family fixes layered comparator placements whose Boolean outputs sort every input; families may differ in comparator count, depth, and resulting CNF structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Comparator Topology Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sorting-network characterization is mathematically plausible and the definition kind fits the leaf, but no citation is supplied. An authoritative comparator-network or SAT-encoding source with a specific section, theorem, or page is required to support the topology-family scope and the claim about corresponding Tseitin encodings.

children.title: Truncated-Output Regimes
children.top_down_role: Constructions retaining only outputs relevant to the requested cardinality bound.

assumptions_latex: The intended constraint is \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le K\), where \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(0\le K<n\).
The retained comparator network correctly computes its first \(K+1\) outputs in nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint is represented by the retained network clauses together with \(\neg y_{K+1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers upper-bound cardinality encodings retaining only outputs needed to detect violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a truncated-output regime for \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\le K\), retain only comparators and auxiliary wires required to compute \(y_1,\ldots,y_{K+1}\), where \(y_j=1\iff\sum_i x_i\ge j\). Encode each retained comparator by clauses defining its Boolean outputs and add the unit clause \(\neg y_{K+1}\). The resulting CNF is satisfiable under an input assignment exactly when at most \(K\) inputs are true. Outputs \(y_j\) with \(j>K+1\), and network components influencing only those outputs, may be omitted without changing this projection onto the input variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an at-most-K constraint, computing only the first K+1 sorted outputs and forcing output K+1 false preserves the accepted input assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated-Output Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the truncated-output leaf, but the record provides no citation. The precise dependency-based pruning condition and preservation of the input projection require an authoritative sorting/cardinality-network source with a specific locator.

children.title: Commander Encodings
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical group-summary constructions for mutual-exclusion constraints.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) are partitioned into nonempty groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\).
The target constraint is \(\sum_i x_i\le 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constructed CNF is satisfiable over its auxiliary variables exactly when \(\sum_i x_i\le 1\).

notation.meaning: A CNF encoding of at most one variable in S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard recursive grouped encoding of an at-most-one constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A commander encoding introduces one Boolean variable \(c_j\) for each group \(G_j\). It contains \(\operatorname{AMO}(G_j)\) and the implication clauses \((\neg x\lor c_j)\) for every \(x\in G_j\). It also imposes \(\operatorname{AMO}(\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\})\), recursively by further grouping or directly at a chosen terminal size. Thus any selected input activates its group commander, while the commander-level constraint prohibits selections from distinct groups and each local constraint prohibits two selections within one group. Existentially quantifying all commanders yields exactly \(\sum_i x_i\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Commander encoding partitions an at-most-one constraint, links each input to a group commander, and recursively enforces at most one commander.
knowledge_statements.title: Commander Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and stated AMO construction are plausible, but no source supports the selected commander variant, its recursive termination, or its projection claim. A primary or authoritative SAT-encoding citation with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Bimander Encodings
children.top_down_role: Grouped constructions combining local exclusions with compact group identifiers.

assumptions_latex: The variables \(X\) are partitioned into nonempty groups \(G_0,\ldots,G_{m-1}\).
Each group index has a distinct \(q\)-bit code, where \(q=\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The CNF projects onto exactly the assignments satisfying \(\sum_{x\in X}x\le1\).

notation.meaning: Bit r of the code assigned to group j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the standard binary-selector grouped encoding for an at-most-one constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bimander encoding places pairwise at-most-one clauses \((
eg x\lor
eg x')\) for distinct \(x,x'\in G_j\). It introduces shared selector bits \(b_1,\ldots,b_q\). For every \(x\in G_j\) and bit position \(r\), it adds \((
eg x\lor b_r)\) when \(\gamma_{jr}=1\), and \((
eg x\lor
eg b_r)\) when \(\gamma_{jr}=0\). Two true variables in one group violate a local clause; true variables in different groups require incompatible selector codes. Conversely, any assignment with at most one true input extends to the selector bits, so the CNF represents \(\sum_{x\in X}x\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bimander encoding combines pairwise clauses within groups with shared binary bits that prevent simultaneous selections from differently coded groups.
knowledge_statements.title: Bimander Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Bimander encodings and the fixed-code construction is plausible, but the record has no citation. A primary Bimander source with a section, theorem, definition, or page must confirm the exact selector-clause convention and projection claim.

children.title: Group-Partition Choices
children.top_down_role: Partition size, balance, and hierarchy choices controlling encoding structure.

assumptions_latex: The \(n\) input variables are partitioned into \(m\) nonempty groups of sizes \(s_1,\ldots,s_m\).
A bimander encoding with distinct fixed-length group codes is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(m\), balanced sizes minimize \(\sum_j\binom{s_j}{2}\); choosing \(m\) trades local clauses against selector clauses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the elementary clause-count criterion for choosing bimander groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A valid group partition satisfies \(s_j\ge1\) and \(\sum_{j=1}^m s_j=n\). Under the fixed-length bimander construction, its direct clause count is \[C(s_1,\ldots,s_m)=\sum_{j=1}^m\binom{s_j}{2}+n\lceil\log_2m\rceil.\] For fixed \(m\), the first term is minimized precisely when \(|s_j-s_k|\le1\) for all \(j,k\); hence balanced groups minimize this count. Selecting \(m\) then amounts to minimizing \(C\), or a stated solver-weighted variant, over \(1\le m\le n\). This criterion concerns syntactic size and does not by itself order partitions by solving performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced groups minimize bimander's within-group pairwise clauses for fixed group count; the group count balances those clauses against binary selector links.
knowledge_statements.title: Group-Partition Choices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is suitable for a partition-choice criterion, and the displayed direct clause count is internally coherent for the stated fixed-length construction. However, no source is supplied for that construction-dependent cost model or its use as a selection regime.

children.title: Compactness–Propagation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tradeoff regions determined by clause count, auxiliary state, and propagation strength.

assumptions_latex: Two CNF encodings represent the same Boolean constraint after existentially quantifying auxiliary variables.
Propagation is evaluated by unit propagation under partial assignments to input variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Clause compactness alone does not determine propagation strength; both size and the unit-propagation closure must be specified.

notation.meaning: Unit-propagation closure of CNF F under partial assignment alpha

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates syntactic compactness from input-level propagation completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an encoding \(F(X,Z)\), compactness is measured by declared resources such as auxiliary-variable count and \(|F|_c\). Input-level propagation completeness means that, for every partial input assignment \(\alpha\), unit propagation derives contradiction whenever the represented constraint has no extension, and derives every input literal logically forced by that constraint and \(\alpha\). A compactness–propagation regime is therefore a pair consisting of a resource bound and this propagation predicate, or an explicitly weaker predicate. Comparing commander, bimander, or other grouped encodings solely by clause count is incomplete because equisatisfiable encodings can have different \(\operatorname{UP}(F,\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grouped encoding's regime must state both its size measure and what unit propagation detects; equisatisfiability and clause count alone do not determine propagation strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Compactness–Propagation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf and the distinction between size and propagation strength is mathematically standard, but no citation is provided. An authoritative source must identify the exact propagation-completeness notion and support its application to grouped encodings.

children.title: Pseudo-Boolean-to-CNF Encodings
children.top_down_role: CNF compilation interfaces only; native pseudo-Boolean optimization and proof systems remain in neighboring chapters.

assumptions_latex: The pseudo-Boolean inequality is \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le B\), with \(a_i,B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
The binary arithmetic circuit is encoded by satisfiability-preserving gate clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting CNF projects onto exactly the Boolean assignments satisfying \(\sum_i a_i x_i\le B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers binary arithmetic-circuit encodings of nonnegative pseudo-Boolean upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adder-based encoding constructs a Boolean circuit whose input contribution for \(x_i\) is the binary word representing \(a_i x_i\). Half adders, full adders, or equivalent carry-save components combine these words into a binary output word representing \(S=\sum_i a_i x_i\). A comparator circuit enforces \(S\le B\). Introducing a variable for each internal wire and clauses defining every gate, together with a unit clause asserting the comparator output, gives a CNF \(F(X,Z)\) such that \(\exists Z\,F(X,Z)\) holds exactly for input assignments satisfying the original inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adder encodings build a binary circuit for the weighted sum, compare it with the bound, and translate the circuit gates into CNF.
knowledge_statements.title: Adder-Based Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the topic and the circuit-to-CNF projection claim is plausible under fully defining gate clauses. No relevant citation is supplied, however, so the adder architecture, comparator assertion convention, and exactness claim remain unsupported.

assumptions_latex: The inequality is \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le B\), with nonnegative integer coefficients.
The decision diagram follows the fixed variable order \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Asserting the root and rejecting terminal defines a CNF whose input projection is exactly the pseudo-Boolean inequality.

notation.meaning: Accumulated sum before processing level i
Decision-diagram node at level i and state s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses an ordered decision diagram whose states are capped partial weighted sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a layered decision diagram with state \(s\) at level \(i\), representing \(s=\sum_{j<i}a_jx_j\). Its \(x_i=0\) arc goes to state \(s\), while its \(x_i=1\) arc goes to \(s+a_i\) if \(s+a_i\le B\) and to the rejecting terminal \(\bot\) otherwise. Equivalent states may be merged. Introduce a Boolean variable for each retained node and encode each node as the conditional choice between its two successors. Assert the root true and \(\bot\) false. The resulting CNF has an auxiliary extension exactly for assignments whose root-to-terminal path respects the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision-diagram encoding tracks partial weighted sums, sends overflow transitions to rejection, and translates the resulting ordered diagram into CNF.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Diagram Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits decision-diagram encodings, but the phrase "encode each node as the conditional choice" does not fix the CNF semantics sufficiently without a cited construction. A source with a specific locator is needed to confirm node reduction, terminal handling, and the exact input-projection result.

assumptions_latex: The coefficients and bound in \(\sum_i a_i x_i\le B\) are nonnegative integers.
Every node stores attainable subtree sums, with all values above \(B\) represented by one overflow value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Forbidding overflow at the root yields an equisatisfiable CNF representation of \(\sum_i a_i x_i\le B\).

notation.meaning: Distinguished value representing every sum greater than B
Proposition that subtree t attains at least or exactly the encoded value s, according to the declared variant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes a generalized totalizer with sums capped at one overflow value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generalized totalizer places the weighted literals at leaves of a binary tree. For each internal node \(t\) with children \(p,q\), it forms capped sums \(r=\min\{s_p+s_q,\omega\}\), where \(\omega=B+1\), and introduces indicators \(u_{t,r}\) for the retained sum values. Merge clauses ensure that each compatible pair of child indicators implies the corresponding parent indicator; the chosen exact-sum or monotone-threshold convention must be used consistently. At the root, the overflow indicator \(u_{r,\omega}\) is forced false. Existentially quantifying the indicators then accepts exactly the inputs with weighted sum at most \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized totalizer merges attainable weighted sums in a tree, caps values above the bound as overflow, and forbids overflow at the root.
knowledge_statements.title: Totalizer-Based Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied and the statement deliberately leaves exact-sum versus monotone-threshold indicators unresolved. Those variants have different required clauses, so a cited construction is needed before the formula and equisatisfiability conclusion can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Watchdog Encodings
children.top_down_role: Threshold-detection constructions for weighted pseudo-Boolean constraints.

assumptions_latex: The constraint is \(\sum_i a_i x_i\le B\), with nonnegative integer coefficients and a fixed positional radix system.
Digit counters and carry relations are encoded consistently with that radix system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The watchdog literal is true exactly when the represented weighted sum exceeds \(B\), so asserting its negation enforces the inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the overflow interface; the precise watchdog circuit variant remains source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A watchdog encoding decomposes each coefficient \(a_i\) into radix digits, aggregates the selected digits by cardinality counters, and propagates carries toward more significant positions. It exposes a literal \(w\) whose defining clauses enforce \(w\leftrightarrow(S>B)\), where comparison includes the final carry and the lexicographic comparison of normalized digits with those of \(B\). The unit clause \(\neg w\) therefore encodes the upper bound. Under a complete assignment to the inputs and a consistent assignment to counter and carry variables, the value of \(w\) is a directly checkable certificate of whether overflow occurred.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A watchdog aggregates radix digits and carries into an overflow literal; forcing that literal false enforces the pseudo-Boolean upper bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Watchdog Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf concerns an encoding family, so representation is likely a better terminal role than certificate; the final literal may serve as an overflow indicator but does not by itself make the construction a certificate. No primary watchdog citation is supplied to establish the exact biconditional, carry handling, or propagation guarantees.

children.title: Mixed-Radix Encodings
children.top_down_role: Digit-based weighted-sum representations using nonuniform positional bases.

assumptions_latex: The bases satisfy \(r_j\in\mathbb Z\) and \(r_j\ge2\).
Only finitely many digits are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nonnegative integer has a unique normalized digit vector in the fixed mixed-radix system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the mixed-radix numeral representation used by radix-based pseudo-Boolean encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-radix system is a sequence of integer bases \((r_0,r_1,\ldots)\) with \(r_j\ge2\) and place values \(R_0=1\) and \(R_j=\prod_{h=0}^{j-1}r_h\). A normalized representation of \(A\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is a finite digit sequence satisfying \[A=\sum_{j\ge0}d_jR_j,\qquad 0\le d_j<r_j.\] In a pseudo-Boolean encoding, each coefficient is expanded in these place values; selected digits are aggregated columnwise, and every total of \(r_j\) units at position \(j\) contributes one carry to position \(j+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed radix represents integers with position-dependent bases; pseudo-Boolean encodings aggregate coefficient digits columnwise and propagate base-specific carries.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Radix Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numeral-system definition is standard, but the leaf is Mixed-Radix Encodings and the record also makes encoding-specific aggregation and carry claims; definition alone therefore only partially captures its role. No relevant pseudo-Boolean encoding source with a specific locator is provided to support that connection.

children.title: Radix Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Base choices governed by coefficient distributions and target bounds.

assumptions_latex: A finite admissible set \(\mathcal R\) of radix sequences is specified.
For each radix sequence, a deterministic encoding construction and resource-cost function are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected radix is any \(\rho^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\rho\in\mathcal R}C(\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes exact selection over a declared finite candidate set and cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given coefficients \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\), bound \(B\), and finite candidate set \(\mathcal R\), expand every \(a_i\) and \(B\) in each \(\rho\in\mathcal R\). Construct the prescribed digit counters, carries, and overflow comparison symbolically, and compute a declared cost \(C(\rho)\), such as clause count, auxiliary-variable count, or a fixed weighted combination. Initialize \(\rho^*\) to the first candidate and replace it whenever a candidate has lower cost, using a fixed tie rule. After all candidates are evaluated, output \(\rho^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\rho\in\mathcal R}C(\rho)\) and instantiate the encoding with that radix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate each admissible radix using a fixed encoding cost, select a minimum-cost candidate with deterministic tie-breaking, and build the corresponding encoding.
knowledge_statements.title: Radix Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the explicit finite enumeration procedure, but the record supplies no primary radix-selection source. The admissible candidate set, symbolic construction, cost computation, and claim that this formalizes the intended radix-selection regime are construction-dependent and require a specific citation.

children.title: Overflow-Detection Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Structural links between digit aggregation, bound violation, and emitted CNF constraints.

assumptions_latex: The input literals encode a pseudo-Boolean inequality \(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le B\), where \(a_i,B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) and \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\).
A fixed radix or mixed-radix network computes a valid digit representation of \(S=\sum_i a_i x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The designated literal \(o\) is true exactly when \(S>B\), so \(\neg o\) enforces the inequality.

notation.meaning: weighted sum represented by the radix network

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic interface for overflow outputs in radix-based pseudo-Boolean encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(\mathbf x,\mathbf d,o,\mathbf z)\) be a CNF encoding whose digit variables \(\mathbf d\) represent \(S=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\), with auxiliary variables \(\mathbf z\). It is an overflow-detection interface for bound \(B\) when, for every assignment \(\alpha\) to \(\mathbf x\), extensions satisfying \(F\) exist and every such extension satisfies \[o\leftrightarrow\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\alpha(x_i)>B\right).\] Consequently, \(F\land\neg o\) is satisfiable under \(\alpha\) exactly when the encoded pseudo-Boolean inequality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overflow output is a verifiable interface literal that is true exactly when the radix-represented weighted sum exceeds the prescribed bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Overflow-Detection Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited for the exact radix-network overflow semantics. The statement is framed as a semantic condition/definition of an interface rather than a certificate, and the intended encoding variant must be documented before review.

children.title: Finite-Domain Constraint Encodings
children.top_down_role: Generic SAT compilation interfaces; global-constraint semantics and propagation algorithms remain in the constraint-programming chapter.

children.title: Direct Value Encodings
children.top_down_role: Finite-domain representations assigning a Boolean indicator to each candidate value.

assumptions_latex: The finite-domain variable \(X\) has nonempty domain \(D_X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one value literal \(x_a\) is true, and it uniquely determines the value of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-hot, also called direct, encoding of one finite-domain variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(a\in D_X\), introduce a Boolean value literal \(x_a\) with semantics \(x_a\leftrightarrow(X=a)\). The direct value representation is constrained by \[\left( igvee_{a\in D_X}x_aight)\land igwedge_{\substack{a,b\in D_X\a
e b}}(
eg x_a\lor
eg x_b).\] Thus every satisfying Boolean assignment selects exactly one domain value, and every assignment \(X=a\) has the unique Boolean representation in which \(x_a\) is true and every \(x_b\), for \(b
e a\), is false.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct encoding introduces one Boolean literal per domain value and imposes exactly-one constraints, producing a one-to-one representation of assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct Value Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-hot direct-value representation is mathematically standard and internally consistent, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Support Encodings
children.top_down_role: Constraint encodings organized around allowed supporting values.

assumptions_latex: Variables \(X,Y\) use direct value literals and have finite domains \(D_X,D_Y\).
A binary relation \(R\subseteq D_X\times D_Y\) specifies the allowed value pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each selected value of \(X\) forces at least one compatible selected value of \(Y\), and symmetrically if both clause families are included.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary extensional support encoding over direct value literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a\in D_X\), define \(S_Y(a)=\{b\in D_Y:(a,b)\in R\}\). The support clause for \(a\) is \[\neg x_a\lor\bigvee_{b\in S_Y(a)}y_b,\] where an empty disjunction is false. Adding these clauses for every \(a\in D_X\), together with the symmetric clauses \(\neg y_b\lor\bigvee_{a:(a,b)\in R}x_a\), compiles \(R\): under exactly-one domain constraints, a complete value assignment satisfies the clauses exactly when its pair belongs to \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support encoding makes every selected value imply that some compatible value is selected for each related variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary support-clause formulation is coherent under the stated exactly-one representation, but it has no cited authoritative source or locator.

children.title: Conflict Encodings
children.top_down_role: Finite-domain constructions organized around incompatible value combinations.

assumptions_latex: Variables \(X,Y\) use direct value literals over finite domains.
A binary relation \(R\subseteq D_X\times D_Y\) lists the allowed pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every pair outside \(R\) is excluded, while every pair in \(R\) satisfies all conflict clauses.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise conflict encoding of a binary extensional relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\overline R=(D_X\times D_Y)\setminus R\). For every forbidden pair \((a,b)\in\overline R\), introduce the conflict clause \[\neg x_a\lor\neg y_b.\] Conjoin all such clauses with the exactly-one constraints for \(X\) and \(Y\). A complete direct-encoding assignment selecting \(a\) for \(X\) and \(b\) for \(Y\) satisfies the resulting CNF if and only if \((a,b)\in R\); hence the clauses are an exact extensional compilation of the relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict encoding adds one binary clause for every forbidden value pair, preventing both corresponding value literals from being true together.
knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clause-per-forbidden-pair representation is internally correct under exactly-one domain constraints, but no supporting citation or locator is provided.

children.title: Support–Conflict Duality
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between allowed-support and forbidden-pair presentations.

assumptions_latex: The literals \(y_b\), for \(b\in D_Y\), satisfy an exactly-one constraint.
For fixed \(a\in D_X\), the support set is \(S_Y(a)=\{b:(a,b)\in R\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The support clause for \(a\) and all conflict clauses against its nonsupports are logically equivalent under the exactly-one constraint for \(Y\).

notation.meaning: support set in the domain of \(Y\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical equivalence for one binary-relation row under direct exactly-one encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under \(\sum_{b\in D_Y}y_b=1\), the support formulation for a fixed value \(a\), \[
eg x_a\lor igvee_{b\in S_Y(a)}y_b,\] is logically equivalent to the conjunction of conflict clauses \[ igwedge_{b\in D_Y\setminus S_Y(a)}(
eg x_a\lor
eg y_b).\] Therefore support clauses aggregate all permitted partners, whereas conflict clauses enumerate all forbidden partners; after imposing exactly-one semantics, both formulations accept exactly the same assignments to \(x_a\) and the value literals of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exactly one value selected for the neighboring variable, requiring a support is equivalent to forbidding every nonsupport.
knowledge_statements.title: Support–Conflict Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated row-wise equivalence follows under exactly-one semantics for the neighboring variable, but the claimed support–conflict duality lacks an inspectable source.

assumptions_latex: The variable \(X\) has ordered domain \(D_X=\{v_1<\cdots<v_m\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every value of \(X\) corresponds bijectively to a monotone Boolean threshold vector.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-vector order encoding for a single ordered finite-domain variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(m-1\) Boolean literals \(q_i\leftrightarrow(X\ge v_{i+1})\) for \(1\le i<m\), and impose the monotonicity clauses \[\bigwedge_{i=1}^{m-2}(\neg q_{i+1}\lor q_i).\] The value \(X=v_k\) is represented by \(q_i=1\) exactly for \(i<k\) and \(q_i=0\) exactly for \(i\ge k\). Hence the satisfying threshold vectors are precisely \(1^{k-1}0^{m-k}\), one for each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order encoding represents an ordered-domain value by a monotone vector of threshold literals, with one prefix pattern per value.
knowledge_statements.title: Order Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold-vector order representation and monotonicity direction are consistent, but no authoritative order-encoding source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Logarithmic Domain Encodings
children.top_down_role: Compact finite-domain representations indexed by a logarithmic number of Boolean variables.

assumptions_latex: The finite domain \(D_X\) has cardinality \(m\ge 1\).
An injective code \(c:D_X\to\{0,1\}^k\) is fixed with \(k=\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value of \(X\) is represented using \(k\) primary Boolean variables, subject to excluding unused codewords.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General injective logarithmic encoding, including non-power-of-two domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k=\lceil\log_2|D_X|\rceil\) and introduce \(\mathbf b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{k-1})\). Fix an injection \(c:D_X\to\{0,1\}^k\) and interpret \(X=a\) exactly when \(\mathbf b=c(a)\). A complete logarithmic domain encoding additionally enforces \[\mathbf b\in c(D_X).\] It therefore uses \(k\) primary bits, represents every domain value uniquely, and admits no Boolean assignment corresponding to a codeword outside the image of \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logarithmic encoding assigns each of m values a distinct bit string of length ceiling log2 m and excludes all unused strings.
knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic Domain Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The injective logarithmic representation, including exclusion of unused words, is coherent but unsupported by a cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Binary Value Encodings
children.top_down_role: Bit-vector presentations of finite-domain values and associated constraint translations.

assumptions_latex: The domain is \(D_X=\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\) with \(m\ge 1\).
Let \(k=\lceil\log_2m\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bits represent \(X\) by its ordinary base-two expansion, with the range restriction \(X<m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard unsigned binary specialization of logarithmic domain encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce bits \(b_0,\ldots,b_{k-1}\) and impose the semantic equality \[X=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}2^j b_j\] together with \(\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}2^j b_j<m\). For every \(a\in D_X\), the unique bit assignment is the length-\(k\) unsigned binary expansion of \(a\). Conversely, every bit assignment satisfying the range restriction denotes exactly one value in \(D_X\); when \(m=2^k\), the restriction is vacuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary value encoding uses the ordinary weighted base-two expansion and a range constraint when the domain size is not a power of two.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary Value Encodings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unsigned binary specialization and range restriction are mathematically consistent, but no relevant source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Invalid-Code Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Treatment of bit patterns lying outside non-power-of-two domains.

assumptions_latex: An injective encoding \(c:D_X\to\{0,1\}^k\) represents the legal values.
The set of unused words is \(U=\{0,1\}^k\setminus c(D_X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One blocking clause per unused word excludes exactly the invalid codes.

notation.meaning: literal falsified exactly when bit \(b_j\) equals \(u_j\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact CNF exclusion of unused words in a finite bit code.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(u=(u_0,\ldots,u_{k-1})\in U\), define \(\ell_{j,u}=b_j\) when \(u_j=0\) and \(\ell_{j,u}=\neg b_j\) when \(u_j=1\). The invalid-code exclusion formula is \[F_U=\bigwedge_{u\in U}\left(\bigvee_{j=0}^{k-1}\ell_{j,u}\right).\] Each clause is false only on its indexed word \(u\). Consequently, an assignment \(\beta\in\{0,1\}^k\) satisfies \(F_U\) if and only if \(\beta\in c(D_X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalid codes are removed by blocking each unused bit string with a clause that is false exactly on that string.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid-Code Exclusion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The blocking-clause construction correctly excludes each unused word, but it is a compilation representation rather than merely a condition, and no supporting citation is supplied.

children.title: Bit-Level Propagation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Propagation behavior induced by compact bit-oriented representations.

assumptions_latex: The variable \(X\) has binary domain encoding \(X=b_0+2b_1\) over \(D_X=\{0,1,2,3\}\).
The finite-domain restriction is \(X\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restriction removes one value but unit propagation fixes neither bit, demonstrating that bit-level propagation can be weaker than value-literal propagation.

notation.meaning: least and most significant encoding bits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary between bit consistency and value-level deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under \(X=b_0+2b_1\), the restriction \(X
e0\) is encoded by \(b_0\lor b_1\). Unit propagation on this clause with no assigned bits derives neither \(b_0\) nor \(b_1\), although the finite-domain consequence \(0
otin D_X\) is immediate. In a direct value encoding, the same restriction is the unit clause \(
eg x_0\). Thus propagation complete at the individual bit level need not expose every deletion available at the value-literal level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting one encoded value may force no individual bit; therefore unit propagation on bits can miss a deletion made explicit by a direct value literal.
knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Level Propagation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly shows that the clause b_0 or b_1 fixes neither bit while a direct encoding exposes the value deletion. A source is still required for the broader propagation-regime interpretation.

children.title: Allowed-Tuple Table Compilation
children.top_down_role: CNF compilation from extensional lists of permitted finite-domain tuples.

assumptions_latex: Variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_r\) use direct value literals.
A finite table \(T\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_r\) lists exactly the allowed tuples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compiled CNF has a satisfying extension exactly for assignments belonging to \(T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selector-based compilation of a positive extensional table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce a selector \(s_t\) for each \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\in T\). Conjoin \[\left(\bigvee_{t\in T}s_t\right)\land\bigwedge_{t\in T}\bigwedge_{i=1}^r(\neg s_t\lor x_{i,t_i})\land\bigwedge_{i=1}^r\bigwedge_{a\in D_i}\left(\neg x_{i,a}\lor\bigvee_{t\in T:t_i=a}s_t\right).\] With exactly-one constraints on the value literals, the formula admits an extension of a complete assignment precisely when its value tuple is in \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An allowed-table compilation selects at least one listed tuple and links each selector bidirectionally to its component value literals.
knowledge_statements.title: Allowed-Tuple Table Compilation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selector-based allowed-table compilation is internally coherent under exactly-one value constraints, but no authoritative table-encoding source with a locator is cited.

children.title: Forbidden-Tuple Table Compilation
children.top_down_role: CNF compilation from extensional lists of prohibited finite-domain tuples.

assumptions_latex: Variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_r\) use direct value literals.
A finite table \(F\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_r\) lists exactly the forbidden tuples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compiled CNF rejects exactly the complete assignments in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-per-tuple compilation of a negative extensional table.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every forbidden tuple \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\in F\), add the blocking clause \[C_t=\bigvee_{i=1}^r\neg x_{i,t_i}.\] Under exactly-one constraints for each variable, \(C_t\) is false exactly when all variables simultaneously take the components of \(t\). Therefore \(\bigwedge_{t\in F}C_t\) is satisfied by a complete finite-domain assignment if and only if its tuple lies in \((D_1\times\cdots\times D_r)\setminus F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forbidden-table compilation adds one blocking clause per listed tuple, rejecting exactly assignments that match every component of a forbidden tuple.
knowledge_statements.title: Forbidden-Tuple Table Compilation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clause-per-forbidden-tuple compilation has the stated exact semantics under exactly-one constraints, but it lacks an inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Automaton-State Compilation
children.top_down_role: CNF representations derived from state-transition views of sequence constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Automaton-State Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CNF compilation of a finite-domain sequence constraint recognized by a deterministic automaton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) be a total deterministic finite automaton and let \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\Sigma\). Introduce one-hot literals \(X_{i,a}\) and state literals \(S_{i,q}\). Enforce exactly one \(X_{i,a}\) for each \(i\), exactly one \(S_{i,q}\) for each layer \(i\), the unit literal \(S_{0,q_0}\), and, for every \(i,q,a\), the clause \(\neg S_{i-1,q}\lor\neg X_{i,a}\lor S_{i,\delta(q,a)}\). Finally impose \(\bigvee_{q\in F}S_{n,q}\). The resulting CNF is satisfiable exactly when the encoded word is accepted by \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Layered state variables and transition clauses produce a CNF satisfiable exactly for words accepted by the given deterministic finite automaton.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is finite, deterministic, and total.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CNF}_A(x,S)\text{ is satisfiable in }S\iff A\text{ accepts }x_1\cdots x_n.\)

notation.meaning: The automaton is in state q after i symbols.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and automaton-acceptance claim are mathematically plausible and fit the leaf, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator. An authoritative source for the layered CNF encoding and its projection-exactness is required.

children.title: Table–Automaton Hybrid Regimes
children.top_down_role: Compilation choices combining local tuple structure with compact transition structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Table–Automaton Hybrid Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise compilation using tables for macro-transitions and automaton states at block boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition positions into consecutive blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_t\). For each block define the allowed macro-transition table \(T_j=\{(p,w,q):w\in\Sigma^{|B_j|},\ \delta^*(p,w)=q\}\). Introduce one-hot boundary-state variables \(S_{j,q}\), and compile the table constraint \((S_{j-1},x_{B_j},S_j)\in T_j\) by any projection-preserving table encoding. Fix \(S_{0,q_0}\) and require \(S_{t,q}\) for some \(q\in F\). The conjunction of the block encodings is satisfiable exactly when the complete word is accepted; singleton blocks recover transition compilation, while one block recovers an allowed-tuple table.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tables encode block-level automaton transitions, while boundary-state variables connect blocks; the hybrid remains exact and interpolates between transition and full-table encodings.
assumptions_latex: \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) is a total deterministic finite automaton.
\((B_1,\ldots,B_t)\) partitions the sequence in order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigwedge_{j=1}^{t}[(S_{j-1},x_{B_j},S_j)\in T_j]\iff A\text{ accepts }x_1\cdots x_n.\)

notation.meaning: State q holds at boundary j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this specialized hybrid construction. A source is also needed to pin down the projection-preserving table interface, the interpretation of boundary-state tuples, and the initial and accepting-state constraints omitted from the displayed conclusion.

children.title: XOR-Chain Encodings
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable chains decomposing long XOR constraints into smaller components.

knowledge_statements.title: XOR-Chain Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-size Tseitin chain for one Boolean parity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge2\), the parity constraint \(x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_n=b\) is represented by auxiliaries \(y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1}\) satisfying \(y_1\leftrightarrow x_1\oplus x_2\), \(y_i\leftrightarrow y_{i-1}\oplus x_{i+1}\) for \(2\le i\le n-1\), and the unit constraint \(y_{n-1}=b\). Each gate \(z\leftrightarrow u\oplus v\) is encoded by \((u\lor v\lor
eg z)\land(
eg u\lor
eg v\lor
eg z)\land(u\lor
eg v\lor z)\land(
eg u\lor v\lor z)\). Existentially eliminating the auxiliaries yields exactly the original parity relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parity equation becomes a chain of binary XOR gates, each represented by four clauses, giving an exact linear-size CNF extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y\,\operatorname{ChainCNF}(x,y,b)\iff x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_n=b.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-clause XOR gate and linear chain are standard and the representation kind fits, but no citation or locator is supplied for the encoding or its projection-exactness.

children.title: Parity Constraint Encodings
children.top_down_role: CNF representations for even-parity or odd-parity relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Parity Constraint Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended-CNF encoding of a Boolean affine equation over the binary field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coefficients \(a_i,b\in\{0,1\}\), a parity constraint is the Boolean affine equation \(\bigoplus_{i:a_i=1}x_i=b\). A CNF formula \(E(x,y)\), with auxiliary variables \(y\), is an exact parity encoding when every assignment \(\alpha\) to \(x\) satisfies the equation if and only if \(\alpha\) extends to an assignment \((\alpha,\beta)\) satisfying \(E\). Thus exactness is the projection identity \(\{\alpha:\bigoplus_{i:a_i=1}\alpha_i=b\}=\operatorname{proj}_x(\operatorname{Mod}(E))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact parity encoding is a CNF extension whose satisfying assignments project precisely onto solutions of a Boolean linear equation modulo two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\text{ is exact}\iff\operatorname{proj}_x(\operatorname{Mod}(E))=\{x:\bigoplus_{i:a_i=1}x_i=b\}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition captures projection-exact parity encoding, but the finite index domain for the variables and coefficients is not introduced. No authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied, so the corrected formulation cannot be source-validated.

children.title: Chain Decomposition Shapes
children.top_down_role: Linear, balanced, and sharing-aware organizations of parity decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Chain Decomposition Shapes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path and balanced-tree decompositions of an n-ary parity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be any full binary tree whose leaves are \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\). Associate an auxiliary variable \(y_v\) with every internal node and impose \(y_v\leftrightarrow y_{v_1}\oplus y_{v_2}\), interpreting leaf values as the corresponding \(x_i\); constrain the root to \(b\). This gives an exact representation of \(\bigoplus_i x_i=b\) using \(n-1\) binary XOR gates. A path-shaped tree has depth \(n-1\), whereas a balanced tree has depth \(\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\); both have linear size but expose different propagation and parallel-evaluation structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any binary tree of XOR gates exactly represents parity; path and balanced shapes retain linear size but have linear and logarithmic depth, respectively.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a full binary tree with the input variables as leaves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{\mathrm{root}}=b\iff\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}x_i=b.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tree representation fits the leaf and is plausible, but the exact meaning of a balanced tree underlying the claimed depth must be specified. The construction and size-depth claims also lack a cited source and locator.

children.title: Parity Propagation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of clause-level propagation relative to native parity reasoning.

knowledge_statements.title: Parity Propagation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of clause-level unit propagation on parity systems encoded equation by equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The four-clause encoding of \(z\leftrightarrow u\oplus v\) determines any one gate variable by unit propagation once the other two are assigned. Consequently an XOR chain propagates through a constraint when all but one of its variables are fixed. This local completeness does not extend to systems of parity equations: for \(x\oplus y=0\) and \(x\oplus y=1\), separately encoded exact CNFs contain no unit clause under the empty assignment, although their conjunction is unsatisfiable. Detecting this contradiction requires cross-equation parity reasoning, such as elimination over \(\mathbb F_2\), or additional clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: XOR-gate CNF propagates a final unknown locally, but separate encodings can miss contradictions that require combining multiple parity equations.
assumptions_latex: Each parity equation is encoded with fresh equation-local auxiliaries.
Inference is restricted to ordinary CNF unit propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{UP}(E_0\land E_1)\not\vdash\bot\quad\text{while}\quad E_0\land E_1\models\bot.\)

notation.meaning: Exact CNF encoding of x XOR y = c.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon fits the terminal container, but projection-exactness alone does not imply that an encoding has no unit clauses. The counterexample must explicitly fix the standard four-clause binary-XOR encodings, and an authoritative propagation source with a locator is required.

children.title: Reachability Encodings
children.top_down_role: CNF representations of path existence or source-to-target connectivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Reachability Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warshall-style exact CNF representation of reflexive directed reachability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and let \(e_{ij}\) denote a directed edge. Introduce \(r_{ij}^{k}\) meaning that \(j\) is reachable from \(i\) using only intermediate vertices in \(\{1,,k\}\). Set \(r_{ij}^{0}\leftrightarrow(e_{ij}\lor[i=j])\), and for \(1\le k\le n\) impose \(r_{ij}^{k}\leftrightarrow(r_{ij}^{k-1}\lor(r_{ik}^{k-1}\land r_{kj}^{k-1}))\). Tseitin CNF encodings of these equivalences are projection-exact. The output variable \(r_{ij}=r_{ij}^{n}\) is true exactly when a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\) exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Layered dynamic-programming variables encode directed reachability exactly by allowing intermediate vertices one at a time.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite directed graph.
Reachability is reflexive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{ij}^{n}=1\iff\text{there is a directed path from }i\text{ to }j.\)

notation.meaning: Reachability using the first k vertices internally.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Warshall-style representation is appropriate, but the intermediate-vertex set is malformed as \(\{1,,k\}\), presumably meaning \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\). No source or inspectable locator supports the recurrence and CNF exactness claim.

children.title: Transitivity Encodings
children.top_down_role: CNF representations enforcing transitive closure properties over binary relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Transitivity Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CNF condition enforcing transitivity of a represented binary relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite vertex set \(V\), let \(r_{ij}\) encode membership of \((i,j)\) in a binary relation \(R\). The clause family \(\neg r_{ij}\lor\neg r_{jk}\lor r_{ik}\), for every \(i,j,k\in V\), is satisfied exactly when \(R\) is transitive. These clauses enforce closure under composition but do not by themselves make \(R\) the least transitive relation containing a given edge relation; exact transitive closure additionally requires reachability witnesses, layered recurrence, or another minimality mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One ternary clause per vertex triple enforces transitivity, but transitivity alone does not force the least closure of the input edges.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigwedge_{i,j,k\in V}(\neg r_{ij}\lor\neg r_{jk}\lor r_{ik})\iff R\circ R\subseteq R.\)

notation.meaning: Indicator that i is related to j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clause family correctly expresses transitivity and the condition kind fits the leaf, but the record has no source reference or specific locator for either the equivalence or the stated least-closure limitation.

children.title: Closure-Variable Representations
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary relation variables used to expose graph closure information.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Variable Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primary variables representing the reflexive transitive closure of an edge relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given edge variables \(e_{ij}\) on a finite directed graph, closure variables \(r_{ij}\) represent the reflexive transitive closure when \(r_{ij}\leftrightarrow\bigvee_{\ell=0}^{n-1}\bigvee_{v_0=i,\,v_\ell=j}\bigwedge_{h=0}^{\ell-1}e_{v_hv_{h+1}}\). Repeated vertices may be removed, so paths of at most \(n-1\) edges suffice when \(i\ne j\), while length zero establishes \(r_{ii}\). An exact CNF representation may realize this formula through layered reachability auxiliaries; its projection onto \((e,r)\) contains exactly the graph–closure pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closure variables denote existence of bounded simple paths, with layered auxiliaries providing an exact CNF realization of that semantics.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) has \(n\) vertices.
Reachability includes paths of length zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{ij}=1\iff j\text{ belongs to the reflexive transitive closure of }i.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended closure-variable semantics fit the leaf, but the displayed disjunction does not explicitly quantify all path vertices over the finite vertex set. The bounded-path and projection-exact CNF claims have no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Sparse–Dense Graph Regimes
children.top_down_role: Encoding-size and propagation tradeoffs across differing graph densities.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse–Dense Graph Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size regimes for explicit edge, closure, and eager transitivity representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a directed graph with \(n\) vertices and \(m\) candidate edges, an adjacency-list edge representation has \(\Theta(m)\) indicators, whereas an adjacency-matrix representation has \(\Theta(n^2)\). Explicit all-pairs closure variables require \(\Theta(n^2)\) variables in both sparse and dense regimes. Instantiating every transitivity clause requires \(\Theta(n^3)\) clauses. Thus sparsity reduces the input representation when \(m=o(n^2)\), but it does not reduce an explicit all-pairs closure interface; dense graphs have \(m=\Theta(n^2)\), making matrix and edge-list input sizes asymptotically equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse graphs admit linear-in-edges input encodings, but explicit all-pairs closure remains quadratic and eager transitivity remains cubic.
assumptions_latex: All ordered vertex pairs are exposed by the closure interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{edge}}=\Theta(m),\quad S_{\mathrm{closure}}=\Theta(n^2),\quad C_{\mathrm{trans}}=\Theta(n^3).\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is suitable, but \(m\) must consistently mean candidate edge variables rather than realized graph edges for the \(\Theta(m)\) encoding claim. The size bounds lack an authoritative source and specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Static Symmetry-Breaking Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lex-leader constraints selecting canonical representatives of Boolean symmetry orbits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act by variable permutations on Boolean assignments, and suppose a formula \(F\) is invariant under this action. Fix a total lexicographic order and add \(x\le_{\mathrm{lex}}g(x)\) for every \(g\in G\). The augmented formula is satisfiable exactly when \(F\) is satisfiable, because every finite orbit has a lexicographically least member. If constraints are added for all elements of \(G\), exactly one assignment from each orbit remains; using only selected generators is satisfiability-preserving but need not select a unique orbit representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lex-leader constraints preserve satisfiability and, when imposed for every group element, retain exactly the least assignment in each symmetry orbit.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting by variable permutations.
\(F(x)=F(g(x))\) for every \(g\in G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is satisfiable}\iff F\land\bigwedge_{g\in G}(x\le_{\mathrm{lex}}g(x))\text{ is satisfiable}.\)

notation.meaning: Assignment obtained by applying symmetry g.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lex-leader principle is mathematically plausible and fits static symmetry breaking, including the distinction between all group elements and selected generators. No authoritative symmetry-breaking citation or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Native Structured-Reasoning Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed Boolean interface retaining structured constraints alongside ordinary CNF clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A native structured instance is a conjunction \(\Phi=C\land\bigwedge_p P_p\), where \(C\) is CNF and each \(P_p\) is a constraint with explicitly defined Boolean semantics, such as parity, automaton acceptance, or graph reachability. An assignment satisfies \(\Phi\) exactly when it satisfies every clause of \(C\) and every native predicate \(P_p\). A solver interface is sound when each propagated literal is entailed by the current conjunction and each reported conflict is inconsistent with it. A certification interface must either provide checkable native inference rules or translate every \(P_p\) projection-exactly into a checkable Boolean representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured solver may retain parity, automaton, or reachability constraints natively, provided propagation is sound and certificates expose checkable semantics or exact translations.
assumptions_latex: All native predicates have finite Boolean semantics.
The CNF and native components share a declared variable map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha\models\Phi\iff\alpha\models C\text{ and }\alpha\models P_p\text{ for every }p.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed CNF/native representation matches the topic, but the certification assertion is not precise enough to determine the required proof system or checkability conditions. No source with a specific locator supports the interface, soundness, and certification claims.

children.title: Logical-Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Encodings preserving truth behavior over their shared visible variables.

assumptions_latex: The original formula \(F\) and encoding \(E\) are Boolean formulas over the same variable set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) and \(E\) have exactly the same satisfying assignments on \(X\).
review_flags: Relevant SAT-specific source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines equivalence without auxiliary variables; equivalence is evaluated assignment by assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) and \(E\) be Boolean formulas over the same variable set \(X\). The encoding \(E\) is logically equivalent to \(F\) precisely when
\[
\forall \alpha\in\{0,1\}^{X},\qquad \alpha\models E\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\alpha\models F.
\]
Equivalently, \(E\equiv F\). This regime preserves satisfiability, unsatisfiability, and the complete model set over \(X\), rather than merely preserving whether at least one model exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logical equivalence requires the original formula and its CNF encoding to agree on every assignment of their common variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Logical-Equivalence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The assignment-wise equivalence definition is standard and fits the leaf, but no inspectable SAT-specific citation is supplied. The record should also state consistently whether E is required to be CNF.

children.title: Equisatisfiability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Encodings preserving the existence or absence of satisfying assignments.

assumptions_latex: The formulas \(F\) and \(E\) may use different Boolean variable sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable if and only if \(E\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: Encoded Boolean formula, usually in CNF

review_flags: Relevant SAT-specific source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the weakest global satisfiability-preservation regime, allowing unrelated model spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Boolean formulas \(F\) and \(E\) are equisatisfiable when
\[
\operatorname{Mod}(F)\neq\varnothing\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\operatorname{Mod}(E)\neq\varnothing.
\]
Their variable sets and individual models need not correspond. Thus equisatisfiability preserves the yes-or-no answer to the SAT decision problem, including unsatisfiability, but by itself neither preserves assignments to original variables nor supplies a rule for recovering a model of \(F\) from a model of \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equisatisfiable formulas are either both satisfiable or both unsatisfiable, although their variables and individual satisfying assignments may differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Equisatisfiability Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and its distinction from model preservation are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but the record has no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Extension-Variable Semantics
children.top_down_role: Semantic role of auxiliary variables introduced by satisfiability-preserving translations.

assumptions_latex: The original variables \(X\) and auxiliary variables \(Y\) are finite and disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An assignment to \(X\) satisfies \(F\) exactly when it extends to a satisfying assignment of \(E\).

notation.meaning: Original formula and extended CNF encoding
Restriction of an assignment to original variables

review_flags: Relevant SAT-specific source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses existential extension semantics for auxiliary variables in a definitional CNF encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(X)\) be a Boolean formula and let \(E(X,Y)\) be a CNF formula with \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\). The variables in \(Y\) have extension-variable semantics when
\[
\forall \alpha\in\{0,1\}^{X},
\quad \alpha\models F\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\exists \gamma\in\{0,1\}^{Y}: (\alpha\cup\gamma)\models E.
\]
Hence \(E\) represents \(F\) after existentially quantifying \(Y\), written \(F(X)\equiv\exists Y\,E(X,Y)\). Auxiliary assignments may be nonunique unless additional defining clauses enforce uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary variables are existential witnesses: an original assignment is feasible exactly when it can be extended to satisfy the CNF encoding.
knowledge_statements.title: Extension-Variable Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential-extension semantics are precise and the representation kind fits the leaf, but an inspectable SAT-encoding source is required.

children.title: Projection-Sensitive Preservation
children.top_down_role: Guarantees required when models are projected onto original variables.

assumptions_latex: The original variables \(X\) and auxiliary variables \(Y\) are finite and disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection onto \(X\) of the encoding's model set equals the model set of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Projection of assignments onto variables in X

review_flags: Relevant SAT-specific source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States exact model preservation after forgetting auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(X)\) and an encoding \(E(X,Y)\) with \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\), projection-sensitive preservation is the equality
\[
\pi_X\bigl(\operatorname{Mod}(E)\bigr)=\operatorname{Mod}(F),
\qquad
\pi_X(S):=\{\beta|_X:\beta\in S\}.
\]
It requires both soundness, \(\pi_X(\operatorname{Mod}(E))\subseteq\operatorname{Mod}(F)\), and completeness, \(\operatorname{Mod}(F)\subseteq\pi_X(\operatorname{Mod}(E))\). It is strictly more informative than bare equisatisfiability because every encoded model projects correctly and every original model has an encoded extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection-sensitive preservation means that forgetting auxiliary variables yields exactly all satisfying assignments of the original formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Sensitive Preservation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection equality correctly expresses sound and complete preservation over the original variables and fits the property container, but it lacks a cited source and locator.

children.title: Clause-Count Growth
children.top_down_role: Encoding expansion measured through the number of generated clauses.

assumptions_latex: An encoding family \((E_n)_{n\geq 1}\) is indexed by an input-size parameter \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Clause-count growth is the asymptotic behavior of \(C(n)=|E_n|\).

notation.meaning: CNF encoding for size parameter n
Number of clauses in the encoding

review_flags: Relevant SAT-encoding source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures representation size by clauses, independently of their widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a family of CNF encodings \((E_n)_{n\geq1}\), define the clause count by
\[
C(n):=|E_n|.
\]
A bound \(C(n)=O(g(n))\) means that constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\) exist such that \(|E_n|\leq c g(n)\) for every \(n\geq n_0\); analogous definitions apply to \(\Omega(g(n))\) and \(\Theta(g(n))\). Clause count alone does not control total representation length when clause width is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause-count growth tracks how the number of CNF clauses scales with the input-size parameter, without accounting for clause widths.
knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Count Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The measure is standard, but the statement defines clause-count growth rather than asserting a particular complexity bound. Its content kind should be reconsidered after SAT-specific sourcing is supplied.

children.title: Literal-Count Growth
children.top_down_role: Encoding expansion measured through total literal occurrences.

assumptions_latex: An encoding family \((E_n)_{n\geq 1}\) consists of finite CNF formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Literal-count growth is the asymptotic behavior of \(L(n)=\sum_{K\in E_n}|K|\).

notation.meaning: CNF encoding and one of its clauses
Number of literals in a clause

review_flags: Relevant SAT-encoding source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts literal occurrences, retaining information lost by clause count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite CNF encoding \(E_n\), its literal-occurrence count is
\[
L(n):=\sum_{K\in E_n}|K|,
\]
where \(|K|\) is the width of clause \(K\). If every clause has width at most \(w(n)\), then \(C(n)\leq L(n)\leq w(n)C(n)\), where \(C(n)=|E_n|\). Consequently, bounded-width encodings have \(L(n)=\Theta(C(n))\), whereas clause count can understate size when widths grow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Literal-count growth measures total literal occurrences; it agrees asymptotically with clause count only when clause width is bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Count Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No SAT-specific source is cited. As written, C(n)≤L(n) and the claimed Theta equivalence fail if empty clauses are permitted; the assumptions must exclude empty clauses or qualify the inequalities. The record defines a size measure rather than a particular complexity bound.

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Cost
children.top_down_role: Fresh-variable requirements and their effect on representation size.

assumptions_latex: The encoding \(E(X,Y)\) uses disjoint finite sets of original variables \(X\) and auxiliary variables \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The auxiliary-variable cost is \(A(E;X)=|\operatorname{Var}(E)\setminus X|\).
review_flags: Relevant SAT-encoding source locator is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts distinct added variables, not their occurrences or branching impact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a CNF encoding \(E(X,Y)\) whose designated original-variable set is \(X\), define its auxiliary-variable cost by
\[
A(E;X):=|\operatorname{Var}(E)\setminus X|.
\]
When every member of \(Y\) occurs in \(E\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(E)\subseteq X\cup Y\), this equals \(|Y|\). The measure counts distinct added Boolean variables; clause count, literal occurrences, and solver effort are separate costs and are not determined by \(A(E;X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary-variable cost is the number of distinct encoding variables beyond the designated original variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The auxiliary-variable count is precise and its definition kind fits the leaf, but no relevant source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Size–Auxiliary Tradeoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Construction choices that exchange clauses or literals for additional variables.
