knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every decision, the algorithm selects an unassigned variable of maximum current exponentially decayed conflict activity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exponentially decayed variable-state-independent decaying-sum branching rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(a_0(x)=0\) for every variable \(x\). After conflict \(t\), update each score by \(a_t(x)=\rho a_{t-1}(x)+\mathbf{1}_{B_t}(x)\), where \(B_t\) contains variables selected by conflict analysis. At a decision point, choose an unassigned variable maximizing \(a_t(x)\), resolve ties by a fixed rule, and assign a phase supplied by a separate polarity policy. Equivalent implementations may decay the bump increment rather than all stored scores and may rescale all scores by a common positive factor without changing the selected variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: VSIDS repeatedly bumps conflict variables, exponentially discounts older bumps, and branches on the highest-scoring unassigned variable.
knowledge_statements.title: VSIDS Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exponentially decayed scoring rule is a recognizable VSIDS-style variant, but the exact bump set, decay convention, and equivalence claim require a source identifying the variant.

children.title: Clause-Activity Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching signals derived from clause activity or clause participation.

assumptions_latex: Each learned clause has a nonnegative activity updated from conflict participation.
At least one unassigned variable remains when a branching decision is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected variable maximizes the chosen aggregate activity of currently retained clauses containing it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A precise aggregate clause-activity variant of activity-based variable branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(a(C)=0\) for learned clauses. Whenever conflict analysis uses a learned clause \(C\), increase \(a(C)\) by one; after each conflict multiply all clause activities by a fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\). At a decision point compute \(s(x)=\sum_{C\in\mathcal D:\,x\in\operatorname{var}(C)}a(C)\) for every unassigned variable \(x\). Select a variable maximizing \(s(x)\), break ties deterministically, and obtain its truth value from a separate phase rule. Clause deletion removes deleted clauses from subsequent aggregates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score each variable by the decayed activities of retained clauses containing it, then branch on a maximum-score unassigned variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Activity Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes that this aggregate of retained clause activities is a recognized clause-activity branching scheme. The exact update and selection rule therefore remain source-dependent.

children.title: Activity Decay Regimes
children.top_down_role: Timescale choices governing activity persistence and responsiveness.

assumptions_latex: Activities obey \(a_t(x)=\rho a_{t-1}(x)+b_t(x)\) with \(0<\rho<1\).
The bump sequence satisfies \(b_t(x)\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The score is an exponentially weighted history whose effective memory increases as \(\rho\) approaches one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form interpretation of multiplicative activity decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For initial activity \(a_0(x)\), the recurrence \(a_t(x)=\rho a_{t-1}(x)+b_t(x)\) has the representation \[a_t(x)=\rho^t a_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{t}\rho^{t-i}b_i(x).\] Thus a bump from \(k\) updates earlier has weight \(\rho^k\). Smaller \(\rho\) emphasizes recent conflicts, while larger \(\rho\) retains history longer. Multiplying every activity by the same positive scalar, including global overflow rescaling, preserves all score comparisons and therefore leaves the branching choice unchanged when tie-breaking is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicative decay makes activity an exponentially weighted conflict history; the decay factor controls memory length, while common rescaling preserves rankings.
knowledge_statements.title: Activity Decay Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recurrence expansion and invariance under common positive rescaling are mathematically correct, but the record provides neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Activity-Heuristic Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Stagnation, overreaction, and weak-signal regimes in activity-guided search.

assumptions_latex: Branching scores depend only on past conflict participation and do not encode a polarity choice.
Initial scores are tied and ties are resolved deterministically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Activity scores alone cannot guarantee a conflict-avoiding initial decision and phase on all CNF formulas.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-history scores cannot by themselves resolve cold-start ties or choose polarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(F_+=(x\lor y)\land(x\lor
eg y)\) and \(F_-=(
eg x\lor y)\land(
eg x\lor
eg y)\). Before any conflict, an activity-only rule has identical zero-score information on both formulas. If its tie rule selects \(x\), choosing phase false causes immediate contradictory propagation in \(F_+\), whereas choosing phase true causes it in \(F_-\). The opposite phases satisfy the respective forced value of \(x\). Hence no polarity decision based solely on the identical activity state avoids this conflict on both instances; tie-breaking and phase selection require information beyond decayed conflict counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two formulas with identical initial activities require opposite phases, so conflict activity alone cannot avoid a bad cold-start decision on both.
knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Heuristic Failure Modes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The paired formulas support the stated cold-start polarity limitation for a rule restricted to activity state, but the restriction and its relevance to the intended activity heuristic need authoritative sourcing.

children.title: Learning-Rate Branching
children.top_down_role: Variable prioritization based on observed learning participation.

knowledge_statements.title: Learning-Rate Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conflict-participation learning-rate policy for selecting CDCL decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every variable \(x\), initialize \(s_x=0\), \(a_x=0\), and \(c_x=0\). During a learning interval, increment \(a_x\) whenever \(x\) is assigned and increment \(c_x\) whenever \(x\) participates in conflict analysis. When the interval closes, form \(r_x=c_x/\max\{1,a_x\}\) and update \(s_x\leftarrow(1-\alpha)s_x+\alpha r_x\), where \(0<\alpha\leq1\); then reset the interval counters. At each decision, choose an unassigned variable maximizing \(s_x\), with deterministic or random tie-breaking, and assign its phase using the separate phase-control policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a recency-weighted estimate of each variable’s conflict participation per assignment, and branch on an unassigned variable with maximum estimated learning rate.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a CNF formula processed by a CDCL solver.
Conflict analysis identifies the variables participating in each analyzed conflict.
\(0<\alpha\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next decision variable belongs to \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\text{ unassigned}}s_x\).

notation.meaning: current branching score of variable x
assignment and conflict-participation counts in the current interval

review_flags: Exact published learning-rate branching update and interval convention require an authoritative SAT-solver source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this exact interval-based learning-rate update. Published learning-rate branching conventions may differ in the credited events, interval boundaries, denominator, and score update, so the mathematical algorithm cannot be validated from the supplied evidence.

children.title: Conflict-History Branching
children.top_down_role: Variable prioritization based on accumulated conflict involvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-History Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A recency-sensitive branching rule driven by recorded conflict involvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each variable \(x\) with a score \(q_x\), initially zero, and record its most recent conflict index \(h_x\). At conflict \(t\), let \(C_t\) be the variables credited by conflict analysis. For each \(x\in C_t\), set \(r_{x,t}=g(t-h_x)\), update \(q_x\leftarrow(1-\alpha)q_x+\alpha r_{x,t}\), and set \(h_x\leftarrow t\), where \(g\) is nonincreasing and \(0<\alpha\leq1\). Scores of variables outside \(C_t\) remain unchanged or undergo a specified global decay. Choose an unassigned variable of maximum \(q_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reward variables appearing in recent conflicts, smooth their rewards into persistent scores, and branch on the highest-scoring unassigned variable.
assumptions_latex: Conflict events are indexed by \(t=1,2,\ldots\).
\(g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}\) is nonincreasing.
\(0<\alpha\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decision variable is selected from \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\text{ unassigned}}q_x\).
review_flags: The intended conflict-history branching variant and its published reward formula require source identification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended conflict-history heuristic and reward function are uncited. Moreover, the initial value of h_x is unspecified and the alternative between unchanged scores and global decay does not define one determinate algorithm; an authoritative variant is needed.

children.title: History-Horizon Variants
children.top_down_role: Short-memory, long-memory, and adaptive-history branching regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Horizon Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window and exponentially discounted representations of conflict history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_{x,t}\geq0\) be the conflict signal credited to variable \(x\) at event \(t\). A length-\(H\) history score is \(S^{(H)}_{x,t}=\sum_{j=0}^{\min\{H-1,t-1\}}z_{x,t-j}\). An exponentially discounted score is \(S^{(\lambda)}_{x,t}=\sum_{j=0}^{t-1}\lambda^jz_{x,t-j}\), where \(0\leq\lambda<1\), equivalently \(S^{(\lambda)}_{x,t}=z_{x,t}+\lambda S^{(\lambda)}_{x,t-1}\) with \(S^{(\lambda)}_{x,0}=0\). The effective history grows with \(H\) or with \(1/(1-\lambda)\); branching ranks unassigned variables by the selected score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict history may use a hard window of H events or exponential discounting, with larger H or discount factor retaining longer memory.
assumptions_latex: \(z_{x,t}\geq0\) is defined for each variable and conflict event.
\(H\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq1}\) or \(0\leq\lambda<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hard-window and discounted scores provide two explicit history-horizon variants for ranking variables.

notation.meaning: conflict signal for variable x at event t

review_flags: Generic horizon representation is mathematically explicit, but its intended SAT-specific attribution requires a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The windowed and exponentially discounted formulas are internally coherent and the representation content kind fits the leaf, but no source establishes these constructions as the intended SAT conflict-history variants.

children.title: Signal Reliability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Sparse, delayed, or misleading feedback regimes for history-based branching.

knowledge_statements.title: Signal Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which finite conflict observations cannot reliably rank branching variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each observed signal \(Z_{x,i}\in[0,1]\) has mean \(\mu_x\), and variable \(x\) is ranked by \(\widehat\mu_x=n_x^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_x}Z_{x,i}\). For two variables with gap \(\Delta=|\mu_x-\mu_y|\), reliable ordering requires estimation error below \(\Delta/2\). If observations are independent, Hoeffding bounds give error probability at most \(2e^{-n_x\Delta^2/2}+2e^{-n_y\Delta^2/2}\). Thus small samples or \(\Delta\) near zero make the ranking statistically unresolved; under nonstationary or selection-biased conflict signals, this guarantee does not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict scores cannot reliably distinguish nearly equal variables from few observations, and standard concentration guarantees fail under drift or selection bias.
assumptions_latex: For the stated bound, signals are independent and lie in \([0,1]\).
Each variable has at least one observation.
\(\Delta=|\mu_x-\mu_y|>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(n_x\Delta^2\) or \(n_y\Delta^2\) is small, empirical conflict-signal ordering is unreliable.

notation.meaning: true score gap between two variables

review_flags: The concentration calculation is standard, but its interpretation as the intended SAT signal boundary needs a relevant source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The concentration argument is a plausible generic statistical boundary, but no cited source supports modeling CDCL conflict signals as independent samples with fixed means or identifies this as the intended SAT reliability boundary.

children.title: Phase Saving
children.top_down_role: Retention and reuse of previously assigned variable polarities.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase Saving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CDCL polarity selection using each variable’s most recently recorded assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a saved phase \(p_x\in\{0,1\}\) for every variable \(x\), initialized by a fixed default. Whenever \(x\) receives an assignment \(b\in\{0,1\}\), whether by decision or propagation under the chosen saving convention, set \(p_x\leftarrow b\). When the branching rule later selects an unassigned variable \(x\), decide \(x=p_x\). Backtracking and restarting remove trail assignments but do not erase saved phases. The procedure changes only decision polarity; variable selection, propagation, conflict analysis, clause learning, and termination remain those of the underlying CDCL solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remember each variable’s latest assigned truth value and reuse it as the polarity when that variable is selected again.
assumptions_latex: The solver uses Boolean variables and CDCL backtracking.
A fixed convention states which assignments update saved phases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each selected variable \(x\) is assigned its stored phase \(p_x\).

notation.meaning: saved Boolean phase of variable x

review_flags: A canonical SAT reference is needed for the exact saving convention and historical attribution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm captures the general phase-saving idea, but the exact assignment events that update saved phases are deliberately left to an unspecified convention. A SAT source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Rephasing Policies
children.top_down_role: Periodic or triggered replacement of saved polarity states.

knowledge_statements.title: Rephasing Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global replacement of saved decision phases during CDCL search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=(p_x)_{x\in V}\) be the saved-phase vector and let \(0<\tau_1<\tau_2<\cdots\) be rephasing times measured in conflicts, restarts, or another fixed resource. At time \(\tau_k\), compute a replacement vector \(q^{(k)}\in\{0,1\}^{V}\) from a declared source, such as all-false, all-true, random, best-known, or inverted saved phases, and set \(p_x\leftarrow q^{(k)}_x\) for every eligible variable. Between rephasings, ordinary phase saving updates \(p\). Variable selection is unchanged, and subsequent decisions use the current \(p_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At scheduled search times, replace some or all saved phases using a declared global source, then resume ordinary phase saving.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is the finite set of Boolean variables.
Rephasing times and the replacement source are fixed by the policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After event \(\tau_k\), eligible variables satisfy \(p_x=q^{(k)}_x\) until later updates.
review_flags: Solver-specific rephasing schedules and sources vary; an authoritative implementation or algorithm source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic replacement-vector construction fits an algorithmic rephasing-policy leaf, but the listed sources and scheduling semantics are not supported by an authoritative solver or algorithm reference.

children.title: Phase-Source Variants
children.top_down_role: Saved, fixed, randomized, model-guided, and globally biased phase sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Source Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A unified representation of alternative sources for CDCL decision polarities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each decision on variable \(x\) at search state \(s\), a phase-source policy is a map \(\phi(x,s)\in\{0,1\}\). Standard variants are saved phase \(\phi(x,s)=p_x\), fixed phase \(\phi(x,s)=b\), random phase with \(\Pr[\phi(x,s)=1]=\rho\), occurrence-based phase maximizing the number or weight of initially satisfied literal occurrences, and model-guided phase \(\phi(x,s)=m_x\) from a complete or partial reference assignment. A precedence rule must resolve undefined sources and combinations; the selected decision is \(x=\phi(x,s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision polarity may come from saved, fixed, random, occurrence-based, or model-guided values, with an explicit fallback order.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is an unassigned Boolean variable.
Every partial source has a declared fallback.
\(0\leq\rho\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A phase source determines the Boolean value \(\phi(x,s)\) assigned at the decision.
review_flags: The taxonomy of phase sources is standard solver practice but lacks a supplied SAT-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The phase-source map is coherent and representation is an appropriate content kind, but no source supports the proposed taxonomy or the occurrence-based and model-guided conventions in this exact form.

children.title: Phase-Control Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search stagnation or destructive reset regimes caused by phase control.

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Control Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search regimes in which fixed or persistent polarity choices can cause severe redundant exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Phase control does not alter CDCL soundness or completeness when both polarities remain reachable through propagation, conflicts, learned clauses, and backtracking. Its performance can nevertheless fail sharply: if a persistent phase vector \(p\) repeatedly reconstructs the same large partial assignment after restarts while every satisfying assignment disagrees with \(p\) on a set \(D\), then progress requires conflicts or decisions that overturn variables in \(D\). When learned clauses do not quickly force those reversals, repeated phase reconstruction may revisit essentially the same search region. Rephasing can mitigate this mechanism but supplies no general polynomial-time guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent phases preserve correctness but may repeatedly rebuild an unproductive region when solutions require coordinated polarity reversals that learned clauses do not force.
assumptions_latex: The underlying CDCL solver is sound and complete independently of its phase heuristic.
Restarts preserve learned clauses and saved phases.
Every satisfying assignment differs from \(p\) on a nonempty set \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent phase control may cause repeated exploration without improving worst-case CDCL complexity.

notation.meaning: variables whose saved phases disagree with every solution under consideration

review_flags: A concrete published family or empirical characterization is needed to certify this phase-control failure mechanism.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record states a plausible qualitative failure mechanism but supplies neither a formal instance family nor empirical or theoretical evidence showing the claimed repeated reconstruction behavior. A relevant CDCL source is required.

children.title: Universal Restart Schedules
children.top_down_role: Instance-agnostic restart sequences designed for unknown runtime distributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Universal Restart Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The Luby-style static cutoff sequence for unknown runtime distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(u_1=1\). For \(i\geq2\), choose the unique \(k\) with \(2^{k-1}\leq i<2^k\), and set \(u_i=2^{k-1}\) if \(i=2^k-1\), otherwise set \(u_i=u_{i-2^{k-1}+1}\). Given scale \(B\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq1}\), run CDCL attempt \(i\) for at most \(Bu_i\) conflicts unless it terminates earlier; on cutoff, restart while retaining information permitted by the solver. Thus the cutoffs begin \(B,B,2B,B,B,2B,4B,\ldots\). Output the first SAT or UNSAT result produced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the recursively defined Luby cutoffs, scaled by B, restarting after each cutoff until the solver returns SAT or UNSAT.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq1}\).
Each attempt has a well-defined conflict cutoff.
Restarts preserve solver correctness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Attempt \(i\) receives cutoff \(Bu_i\), yielding \(B,B,2B,B,B,2B,4B,\ldots\).
review_flags: The exact universal-restart theorem and its runtime assumptions require the original or authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed recurrence generates the stated Luby sequence, but no source supports its use or universality interpretation in this CDCL setting. Retaining learned information also differs from the independent-restart model underlying standard universal-restart results.

children.title: Geometric Restart Schedules
children.top_down_role: Restart intervals scaled through a fixed multiplicative progression.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Restart Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static restart cutoffs increasing by a fixed multiplicative factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a base budget \(B>0\) and growth factor \(\gamma>1\). For attempt \(i=1,2,\ldots\), set the integer conflict cutoff to \(T_i=\lceil B\gamma^{i-1}\rceil\). Run the CDCL search until it proves SAT or UNSAT or reaches \(T_i\) conflicts. If the cutoff is reached, restart according to the solver’s retention policy and continue with attempt \(i+1\); otherwise return the solver’s result. The schedule is fixed before search and satisfies \(T_{i+1}\) approximately equal to \(\gamma T_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with budget B and multiply successive restart cutoffs by a fixed factor greater than one until the solver terminates.
assumptions_latex: Conflict counts are reset or consistently measured at each attempt.
The restart operation preserves correctness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(i\)-th restart cutoff is \(T_i=\lceil B\gamma^{i-1}\rceil\).
review_flags: A SAT-specific authoritative source is needed for the convention and parameterization of geometric schedules.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The geometric cutoff algorithm is mathematically explicit and appropriately classified, but no SAT-specific citation with a locator supports the resource-counting and restart conventions.

children.title: Schedule Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Base interval, growth factor, and rescaling choices across restart schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Schedule Scaling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: How multiplicative cutoff scaling changes restart frequency without changing schedule shape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((u_i)_{i\geq1}\) be a dimensionless positive restart sequence and let \(T_i(B)=\lceil Bu_i\rceil\) for scale \(B>0\). For any \(c>0\), ignoring integer rounding, \(T_i(cB)=cT_i(B)\), so scaling preserves all cutoff ratios \(T_i/T_j\) and changes only their absolute resource units. Small \(B\) yields frequent early restarts and limits uninterrupted propagation; large \(B\) yields fewer restarts and longer individual attempts. Consequently, universality or geometric shape alone does not determine behavior until the resource unit and base scale are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying the base scale multiplies every cutoff while preserving schedule shape; small scales restart frequently, whereas large scales permit longer attempts.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i>0\) for every \(i\).
All cutoffs use the same resource unit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Apart from rounding, \(T_i(cB)=cT_i(B)\) and \(T_i(cB)/T_j(cB)=T_i(B)/T_j(B)\).
review_flags: The algebraic scaling property is immediate, but SAT-specific regime claims need an authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scale identity apart from ceiling effects is immediate, but the claims about propagation and practical restart frequency are SAT-specific and uncited. No supplied evidence supports the complete property record.

children.title: Schedule Mismatch Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Overly frequent or overly delayed restart behavior relative to search progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Schedule Mismatch Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime penalties when static restart cutoffs miss the productive attempt length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider independent search attempts whose success probability is zero for every cutoff \(T<L\) and is \(p>0\) for every cutoff \(T\geq L\), with success detected by time \(L\). Any static schedule that spends cumulative budget \(W\) on cutoffs below \(L\) incurs expected runtime at least \(W+L/p\). A constant cutoff below \(L\) never succeeds, while cutoffs much larger than \(L\) can waste excess work after unsuccessful attempts. Hence a schedule mismatched to the productive scale \(L\) can be arbitrarily worse than repeatedly using cutoff \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cutoffs below the minimum productive length cannot succeed, while oversized cutoffs waste work; either mismatch can be arbitrarily costly.
assumptions_latex: Search attempts are independent under the stated runtime model.
Success probability is \(0\) below \(L\) and \(p>0\) at or above \(L\).
A successful attempt terminates by time \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Subthreshold budget \(W\) adds unavoidable cost, and a permanently subthreshold schedule has infinite expected completion time.

notation.meaning: success probability of a productive attempt
cumulative budget spent below the productive threshold

review_flags: The abstract restart countermodel is explicit, but a source is needed to connect it to the intended CDCL mismatch boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold countermodel is explicit and the failure-boundary content kind fits, but no source connects its independent-attempt assumptions and expected-runtime conclusion to the intended CDCL schedule-mismatch boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Restart Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online CDCL restart rule driven by a statistic of recent conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a CDCL state, a conflict statistic sequence \(q_1,q_2,\ldots\), a window length \(w\ge 1\), and a threshold rule \(\tau_t\). After conflict \(t\), update the history \(H_t=(q_{\max\{1,t-w+1\}},\ldots,q_t)\). Restart exactly when the measurable predicate \(R_t=R(H_t,\tau_t)\) is true: backtrack to decision level zero while retaining learned clauses and persistent heuristic state specified by the solver. Reset the restart-local counters and continue CDCL. Terminate only upon deriving the empty clause or constructing a satisfying assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic policy monitors recent conflict statistics and restarts when an online threshold predicate fires, preserving learned clauses and designated heuristic state.
assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb N_{\ge 1}\)
\(R_t\) depends only on information available by conflict \(t\)
Each restart preserves CDCL soundness invariants
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_t=1\Longrightarrow\) restart after conflict \(t\)

notation.meaning: Statistic observed at the t-th conflict

review_flags: No supplied source addresses dynamic CDCL restart policies or their precise state-preservation convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Dynamic Restart Policies, but its precise trigger and state-preservation conventions are solver-dependent and have no cited SAT/CDCL source.

children.title: Literal-Block Distance
children.top_down_role: Decision-level diversity as a learned-clause quality signal.

knowledge_statements.title: Literal-Block Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard LBD measure for a learned clause at its derivation state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a learned clause and let \(\delta(\ell)\in\mathbb N\) denote the decision level at which the variable of literal \(\ell\in C\) is assigned in the current trail. The literal-block distance of \(C\) is \[\operatorname{LBD}(C)=\left|\{\delta(\ell):\ell\in C\}\right|.\] Thus literals assigned at the same decision level form one block; in particular, \(1\le \operatorname{LBD}(C)\le |C|\) for every nonempty \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LBD is the number of distinct decision levels represented by the literals of a nonempty learned clause at measurement time.
assumptions_latex: \(C\ne\varnothing\) is a learned clause
Every variable occurring in \(C\) is assigned on the current trail
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{LBD}(C)=|\{\delta(\ell):\ell\in C\}|\)

notation.meaning: Decision level of the variable of literal l

review_flags: Standard SAT definition, but none of the supplied source locators concerns CDCL or LBD.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The LBD definition and bounds are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but no authoritative CDCL/LBD source with an inspectable locator is cited.

children.title: Clause-Activity Measures
children.top_down_role: Dynamic clause utility estimated from recent search participation.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Activity Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic decaying activity score used to rank learned clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each learned clause \(C\), maintain an activity \(a_t(C)\ge 0\) after conflict \(t\). Given a decay factor \(\rho\in(0,1]\) and a nonnegative bump \(b_t(C)\), define \[a_{t+1}(C)=\rho a_t(C)+b_t(C),\] where \(b_t(C)>0\) only when the solver-designated event involving \(C\) occurs, such as participation in conflict analysis. At a fixed reduction event, larger \(a_t(C)\) denotes greater recent usefulness under this measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause activity is a decaying score bumped when a learned clause participates in designated useful events; higher current activity means greater recent use.

notation.meaning: Activity of clause C after conflict t

review_flags: Exact bump and decay conventions are solver-dependent; supplied locators provide no CDCL source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decaying-score abstraction fits clause-activity measures, but the recurrence and bump semantics are solver-dependent and unsupported by a cited CDCL source.

children.title: Clause-Size Measures
children.top_down_role: Clause length as a retention and prioritization signal.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause-Size Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic size measures for learned clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a learned clause \(C=\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\ell_k\) containing no repeated literal, its literal-count size is \(s(C)=|C|=k\). Relative to a variable set \(V_0\), its projected size is \(s_{V_0}(C)=|\{\ell\in C:\operatorname{var}(\ell)\in V_0\}|\). The first measures total clause width, while the second measures width restricted to a designated variable block; both are nonnegative integers and \(0\le s_{V_0}(C)\le s(C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause size counts literals; projected size counts only literals whose variables belong to a designated block.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a finite clause without repeated literals
\(V_0\) is a designated set of variables

notation.meaning: Size projected onto variable set V0

review_flags: Definition is standard, but supplied source locators do not support SAT clause-size terminology.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Literal-count size is standard, but the projected-size measure is an additional construction whose status in the intended SAT taxonomy cannot be established without a relevant source.

children.title: Composite Clause-Quality Scores
children.top_down_role: Combined use of structural, historical, and propagation-oriented clause signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Clause-Quality Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized scalar aggregation of several learned-clause quality measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let learned clause \(C\) have feature vector \(z(C)=(z_1(C),\ldots,z_m(C))\), where every normalized feature satisfies \(z_i(C)\in[0,1]\) and is oriented so that smaller values mean preferred retention. For weights \(w_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^m w_i=1\), define the composite quality score \[Q(C)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i z_i(C).\] Then \(Q(C)\in[0,1]\), and a reduction policy may rank clauses in increasing \(Q\), subject to mandatory protection constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite score is a weighted average of normalized, consistently oriented clause features; lower scores rank clauses as preferable to retain.
assumptions_latex: \(z_i(C)\in[0,1]\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
\(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i w_i=1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(C)=\sum_i w_i z_i(C)\in[0,1]\)

notation.meaning: Normalized quality feature i of clause C

review_flags: This is a generic formalization; solver-specific composite scores require an appropriate SAT implementation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted aggregation is internally correct and fits the leaf broadly, but it is a generic construction rather than a documented CDCL clause-quality score and lacks supporting evidence.

children.title: Clause Reduction Policies
children.top_down_role: Timing and selection policies for removing learned clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Reduction Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic deletion of eligible learned clauses under a bounded database target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a reduction event, input the learned-clause database \(D\), a protected subset \(P\subseteq D\), a priority score \(Q:D\to\mathbb R\), and a target size \(B\ge|P|\). Form the eligible set \(E=D\setminus P\), order \(E\) from least to most desirable according to \(Q\), and delete the first \(\max\{0,|D|-B\}\) clauses, breaking ties deterministically. Output \(D'\) with \(P\subseteq D'\subseteq D\) and \(|D'|\le B\) whenever \(|P|\le B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each reduction, protect mandatory clauses and delete the lowest-ranked eligible clauses until the learned database meets its target size.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq D\)
\(B\in\mathbb N\) and \(B\ge|P|\)
\(Q\) induces a deterministic total preorder on eligible clauses
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\subseteq D'\subseteq D\) and \(|D'|\le B\)
review_flags: Generic reduction template lacks support from a supplied CDCL source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is coherent and reaches the claimed target because the eligible set has sufficient size, but the reduction-policy template is unsupported by a cited CDCL source.

children.title: Clause Retention Policies
children.top_down_role: Protection criteria for preserving useful learned clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Retention Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate selecting learned clauses that survive a database reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At reduction time \(t\), let \(D_t\) be the learned-clause database. A retention policy is a predicate \(K_t:D_t\to\{0,1\}\) computed from information available at time \(t\). Its retained set is \[R_t=\{C\in D_t:K_t(C)=1\}.\] Mandatory clauses \(P_t\subseteq D_t\), including clauses protected by current propagation dependencies, must satisfy \(P_t\subseteq R_t\). Any additional capacity constraint is enforced by choosing the discretionary members of \(R_t\setminus P_t\) according to the policy's quality ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retention predicate selects clauses that survive reduction, while every mandatory protected clause must be retained regardless of its quality rank.
assumptions_latex: \(D_t\) is finite
\(P_t\subseteq D_t\)
\(K_t\) uses only state available at reduction time
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_t=\{C\in D_t:K_t(C)=1\}\) and \(P_t\subseteq R_t\)

notation.meaning: Set retained at reduction time t

review_flags: Formal policy abstraction is standard but unsupported by the supplied non-SAT locators.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition-based abstraction fits clause retention policies, but mandatory protection and discretionary ranking conventions require a relevant CDCL source.

children.title: Locked-Clause Protection
children.top_down_role: Treatment of clauses currently serving as propagation reasons.

knowledge_statements.title: Locked-Clause Protection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Protection condition for clauses currently serving as propagation reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CDCL trail \(T\), a clause \(C\) is locked if there exists an assigned literal \(\ell\in C\) such that \(C=\operatorname{reason}(\ell)\) and \(\ell\) is the literal made true by that propagation. Define \[\operatorname{locked}_T(C)\iff \exists\ell\in C\;\bigl(C=\operatorname{reason}(\ell)\bigr).\] A sound in-place database reduction must not delete \(C\) while \(\operatorname{locked}_T(C)\) holds, unless all affected reason references are first replaced or invalidated by a trail update preserving propagation invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clause is locked when it is the recorded reason for a current propagated assignment; reduction must preserve it while that reference remains live.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a consistent CDCL trail
\(\operatorname{reason}(\ell)\) records the clause justifying a propagated literal
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{locked}_T(C)\Longrightarrow C\) is protected from immediate deletion

notation.meaning: Reason clause for propagated literal l
Clause C has a live reason reference on T

review_flags: Standard implementation invariant, but no supplied locator supports locked-clause terminology.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The locked-clause condition and protection invariant fit the leaf, but no cited source supports the terminology or implementation requirement.

children.title: Database Churn Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Excessive deletion, excessive retention, and unstable database turnover.

knowledge_statements.title: Database Churn Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A counting boundary for learned-clause insertion and deletion churn.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Over conflicts \(1,\ldots,T\), let \(I_t\) and \(D_t\) be the numbers of learned clauses inserted and deleted after conflict \(t\), and define cumulative churn \(\Gamma_T=\sum_{t=1}^T(I_t+D_t)\). If \(I_t\le i_{\max}\) and reductions occur at most once every \(r\ge1\) conflicts, deleting at most \(d_{\max}\) clauses each, then \[\Gamma_T\le i_{\max}T+d_{\max}\left\lceil T/r\right\rceil.\] Without bounds on insertion or reduction size and frequency, no finite bound depending only on \(T\) follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded insertions and bounded, spaced reductions yield a linear churn bound; removing those controls eliminates any conflict-count-only bound.
assumptions_latex: \(I_t\le i_{\max}\) for every \(t\)
At most one reduction occurs in each block of \(r\) conflicts
Each reduction deletes at most \(d_{\max}\) clauses
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma_T\le i_{\max}T+d_{\max}\lceil T/r\rceil\)

notation.meaning: Clause insertions and deletions after conflict t
Cumulative database churn through conflict T

review_flags: Elementary counting statement; a SAT source is needed to justify its intended lifecycle interpretation.

children.title: Restart-Frequency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search disruption or stagnation caused by restart timing extremes.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart-Frequency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress boundary for restart schedules measured in conflicts between restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_k\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) be the conflict budget of restart epoch \(k\). If \(\sup_k u_k=U<\infty\), then no epoch can explore a branch requiring more than \(U\) conflicts without interruption. Conversely, if \(u_k\to\infty\) and each epoch executes ordinary CDCL for its full budget unless it terminates, then every fixed finite conflict horizon is eventually available within one epoch. This horizon property alone does not guarantee polynomial runtime or prevent repeated search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded restart epochs exclude uninterrupted searches beyond that bound; unbounded epoch budgets eventually permit every fixed finite conflict horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(u_k\ge1\) is the conflict budget of epoch \(k\)
Restarts occur only at epoch boundaries unless solving terminates
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_k\to\infty\Longrightarrow \forall H<\infty\;\exists k\;(u_k\ge H)\)

notation.meaning: Conflict budget of restart epoch k

review_flags: Boundary is mathematically direct, but its CDCL interpretation needs a suitable restart-analysis source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The horizon implication is mathematically direct, but the claim about exploring a branch across CDCL conflicts is interpretation-dependent and lacks a restart-analysis source.

children.title: Search-Memory Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Benefits and costs of preserving learned state across restarts.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Memory Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case learned-database growth under unrestricted clause retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a Boolean formula on \(n\) variables, every non-tautological clause is determined by assigning each variable one of three states: absent, positive, or negative. Hence at most \(3^n-1\) distinct nonempty non-tautological clauses exist. A CDCL solver retaining every distinct learned clause therefore has learned-clause memory \(O(n3^n)\) literal occurrences in the worst case. A polynomial database cap cannot simultaneously retain all possible distinct learned clauses; it must delete clauses or restrict learning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining every distinct learned clause can require exponentially many clauses and literal occurrences; polynomial memory therefore requires deletion or restricted learning.
assumptions_latex: The formula has \(n\) Boolean variables
Tautological and duplicate clauses are not stored
Clause memory is measured in stored literal occurrences
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|D|\le3^n-1\) and total stored literals are \(O(n3^n)\)

notation.meaning: Set of distinct retained learned clauses

review_flags: Combinatorial bound is elementary, but no supplied source explicitly connects it to CDCL learned-clause memory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The combinatorial clause count and literal-occurrence bound are correct and fit a search-memory boundary, but their CDCL memory interpretation has no cited supporting source.

children.title: Heavy-Tail Runtime Regimes
children.top_down_role: Highly variable search-duration behavior relevant to restart design.

knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tail Runtime Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-law tail criterion for randomized SAT-solver runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\ge0\) be the runtime of a randomized SAT-solving run on a fixed instance or instance distribution. The runtime is regularly varying with tail index \(\alpha>0\) if, for every \(x>0\), \[\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\Pr(T>xt)}{\Pr(T>t)}=x^{-\alpha}.\] Such a runtime is heavy-tailed: its moment \(\mathbb E[T^p]\) is infinite for \(p>\alpha\), while it is finite for \(0<p<\alpha\), subject to the usual slowly varying tail factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A runtime has a regularly varying heavy tail when scaling time by x scales its survival probability asymptotically by x to minus alpha.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a nonnegative random variable
\(\Pr(T>t)>0\) for all sufficiently large \(t\)
The displayed regular-variation limit holds for every \(x>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p>\alpha\Longrightarrow\mathbb E[T^p]=\infty\), and \(0<p<\alpha\Longrightarrow\mathbb E[T^p]<\infty\)
review_flags: Standard probability definition, but supplied locators do not cover heavy-tailed SAT runtimes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regular-variation definition and moment conclusions for orders strictly below or above the tail index are correct, but no probability or SAT-runtime source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Restart–Memory Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction between search resets and retained solver state.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart–Memory Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational coupling between CDCL restarts and retention of learned clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula. A restarting CDCL solver maintains a learned-clause database \(D_t\) at time \(t\). A restart erases the current decision trail but retains a selected database \(D_{t+1}\subseteq D_t\), so subsequent propagation is performed on \(F\land\bigwedge D_{t+1}\). Completeness is preserved whenever every deleted learned clause is redundant with respect to \(F\), while runtime behavior depends jointly on the restart schedule and the retention rule because retained clauses transfer conflict information across restarted search episodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CDCL restarts discard decisions but retain selected learned clauses. Completeness survives sound clause deletion, while runtime depends jointly on restart timing and retained memory.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Every learned clause is logically implied by \(F\).
Clause deletion does not remove clauses required by the underlying complete search procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restarting with sound learned-clause retention preserves satisfiability and completeness, while coupling restart frequency to persistent search memory.

notation.meaning: learned-clause database before a restart at time t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the restart-memory coupling leaf, but no SAT/CDCL source is cited. The completeness claim depends on fairness and progress conditions for the restart and deletion policy, not merely redundancy of deleted learned clauses; the third assumption gestures at these conditions without specifying them.

children.title: Failed-Literal Testing
children.top_down_role: Single-assumption contradiction testing used for forced assignments or pruning.

knowledge_statements.title: Failed-Literal Testing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-level look-ahead using unit propagation under a tentative literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\) under partial assignment \(\alpha\) and an unassigned literal \(\ell\), compute unit propagation on \(F\mid(\alpha\cup\{\ell\})\). If propagation derives the empty clause, declare \(\ell\) failed, permanently extend \(\alpha\) by \(\neg\ell\), and propagate again. Otherwise restore \(\alpha\) and report that this test did not force \(\neg\ell\). Repeat until no tested literal fails or a contradiction is derived.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tentatively assign a literal and run unit propagation. If this causes contradiction, its complement is forced and may be permanently propagated.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(\alpha\) is consistent and \(\ell\) is unassigned under \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A conflict under \(\alpha\cup\{\ell\}\) certifies \(F\land\alpha\models\neg\ell\).

notation.meaning: formula simplified by partial assignment alpha

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role and failed-literal implication are mathematically appropriate, but the record has no inspectable SAT source or locator.

children.title: Multi-Level Look-Ahead
children.top_down_role: Nested speculative propagation beyond single-literal testing.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Level Look-Ahead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth-bounded recursive probing beyond failed-literal testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\), partial assignment \(\alpha\), and depth bound \(d\geq 0\), define \(L(F,\alpha,0)\) as unit propagation of \(F\mid\alpha\). For \(d>0\), select an unassigned variable \(x\), recursively evaluate both \(L(F,\alpha\cup\{x\},d-1)\) and \(L(F,\alpha\cup\{\neg x\},d-1)\), and return conflict if both branches conflict. If exactly one conflicts, retain the opposite literal and continue propagation; otherwise restore \(\alpha\) and return the collected branch scores or common implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively probe both values of selected variables to bounded depth, retaining forced branches, conflicts, common implications, or branching scores.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(d\) is a nonnegative integer.
Each recursive probe restores its tentative assignments before another branch is examined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure soundly derives forced literals or conflict and otherwise supplies depth-\(d\) look-ahead information.

notation.meaning: look-ahead procedure at remaining depth d

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but no source identifies this particular recursive variant. The meanings and sound extraction rules for collected branch scores and common implications are not defined precisely enough to review independently of a cited formulation.

children.title: Look-Ahead Depth Regimes
children.top_down_role: Shallow, selective, and deeper probing configurations.

knowledge_statements.title: Look-Ahead Depth Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case size of full binary look-ahead at fixed or growing depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each probe at one search node performs unit propagation in time \(U(F)\), and full look-ahead explores both truth values at every level to depth \(d\). It visits at most \(2^{d+1}-1\) probe nodes and therefore costs \(O(2^d U(F))\). Thus constant \(d\) gives polynomial per-decision overhead whenever \(U(F)\) is polynomial; \(d=O(\log |F|)\) remains polynomial; and unrestricted \(d=\Theta(n)\) permits exponential overhead in the number \(n\) of unassigned variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full depth-d binary look-ahead costs exponentially in d: constant or logarithmic depth has polynomial overhead, while linear depth may be exponential.
assumptions_latex: Both truth-value branches are explored at every probing level.
One propagation call costs at most \(U(F)\).
No memoization merges distinct probe nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The probing cost is \(O(2^d U(F))\), separating constant, logarithmic, and linear-depth regimes.

notation.meaning: worst-case cost of one unit-propagation probe

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the depth-regime leaf, and the full-binary-tree accounting is plausible under the stated assumptions. An inspectable source is still required for the probing model and its claimed SAT look-ahead interpretation.

children.title: Probing-Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where speculative propagation costs exceed pruning benefits.

knowledge_statements.title: Probing-Cost Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which probing overhead can dominate saved search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search state \(s\), let \(P_d(s)\) be the cost of depth-\(d\) probing, \(T_0(s)\) the expected remaining cost without probing, and \(T_d(s)\) the expected remaining cost after using its deductions and branch choice. Probing is cost-beneficial exactly when \(P_d(s)+T_d(s)<T_0(s)\). It is nonbeneficial at the boundary \(P_d(s)\geq T_0(s)-T_d(s)\); in particular, exponentially growing \(P_d(s)\) can dominate when deeper probes yield no additional forced literals or search reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probing helps only when its cost is smaller than the search work it saves; otherwise deeper probing increases total runtime.
assumptions_latex: All costs use the same computational resource measure.
\(T_0(s)\) and \(T_d(s)\) refer to the same solver state and stopping objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The probing-cost boundary is \(P_d(s)=T_0(s)-T_d(s)\).

notation.meaning: cost of depth-d probing at state s
remaining costs without and with probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the displayed boundary is an accounting identity based on undefined expected-cost quantities rather than a sourced SAT probing result. A source must establish the intended cost model and conditions under which the comparison is meaningful.

knowledge_statements.title: Look-Ahead Branching Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch scores computed from propagation effects in both tentative branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a CNF formula \(F\) under assignment \(\alpha\), let \(r_x^+\) and \(r_x^-\) be nonnegative measures of the reductions obtained by unit propagation after tentatively setting an unassigned variable \(x\) true and false. A look-ahead branching measure is any function \(B(x)=\phi(r_x^+,r_x^-)\) used to rank candidate variables, where \(\phi\) is nondecreasing in each argument and favors progress in both branches; common forms include \(r_x^+r_x^-\) and \(\min(r_x^+,r_x^-)+\varepsilon\max(r_x^+,r_x^-)\) for \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A look-ahead branching measure combines the propagation reductions from both tentative values of a variable into a score used for branch selection.
assumptions_latex: Branch reductions are measured consistently across candidate variables.
Both tentative branches are restored after scoring.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A branching variable may be selected from \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_x B(x)\).

notation.meaning: reductions produced by the two tentative assignments of x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is suitable for this topic container, but the proposed class of measures and the two specific score forms have no source. The phrase 'favors progress in both branches' is also not a formal condition beyond coordinatewise monotonicity.

children.title: Cube Generation
children.top_down_role: Look-ahead-based production of partial assignments defining subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Cube Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Look-ahead partitioning of a CNF formula into assumption cubes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\) and a cutoff predicate \(K\), begin with the empty assignment and recursively apply propagation and look-ahead branching. At a nonterminal state choose a literal \(\ell\) and recurse on both extensions by \(\ell\) and \(\neg\ell\). Discard branches proved inconsistent. When \(K\) holds, output the conjunction of decision literals on that branch as a cube. Continue until every consistent frontier branch has produced a cube, yielding a finite set \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Look-ahead search branches until a cutoff holds, discards contradictory branches, and outputs each surviving decision path as a cube.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
The branching rule eventually assigns a new variable on every uncut branch.
The cutoff predicate terminates every surviving branch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated cubes satisfy \(F\models\bigvee_{C\in\mathcal C}C\), and \(F\) is satisfiable exactly when some \(F\land C\) is satisfiable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits cube generation and its coverage conclusion is plausible for exhaustive binary partitioning with inconsistent branches discarded. No cube-and-conquer source or specific locator is supplied to support the formulation.

children.title: Conquer Solving
children.top_down_role: Complete solving of generated subproblems, commonly with CDCL engines.

knowledge_statements.title: Conquer Solving
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent complete SAT solving under generated cube assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\) and cubes \(\mathcal C=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\) covering all surviving assignments, invoke a complete SAT solver independently on each \(F\land C_i\). Stop and return SAT with the first satisfying assignment found. Return UNSAT only after every subproblem is certified unsatisfiable; the collection of valid subproblem certificates, together with the cube-coverage justification, certifies unsatisfiability of \(F\). Subproblems may be processed sequentially or in parallel without changing correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve every cube-restricted subproblem with a complete SAT solver. One model proves SAT; all subproblems must be refuted to conclude UNSAT.
assumptions_latex: \(F\models\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}C_i\).
Each conquer solver is sound and complete for CNF under assumptions.
Every reported unsatisfiability certificate is independently valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable iff some \(F\land C_i\) is satisfiable; if all are unsatisfiable, then \(F\) is unsatisfiable.

notation.meaning: cube supplied as assumptions to a conquer solver

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role and SAT/UNSAT aggregation logic fit the leaf, but there is no inspectable cube-and-conquer source. The certificate-composition assertion particularly requires a source specifying the proof format and coverage justification.

children.title: Cube–Conquer Handoff
children.top_down_role: Interface choices governing the transition from partitioning to subproblem solving.

knowledge_statements.title: Cube–Conquer Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct interface between partitioning and assumption-based SAT solving.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cube–conquer handoff for a CNF formula \(F\) consists of a finite cube set \(\mathcal C\), a coverage record establishing \(F\models\bigvee_{C\in\mathcal C}C\), and for each cube its ordered assumption literals and simplified solver state. The conquer phase must interpret every cube as conjunction, so its subproblem is \(F\land C\), not \(F\lor C\). Under this interface, models lift directly to models of \(F\), and refutations of every covered subproblem combine into a refutation of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The handoff supplies covering cubes as conjunctive assumptions. Correct interpretation lets subproblem models or complete collections of refutations certify the original formula.
assumptions_latex: Every handed-off cube is consistent with its recorded branch state.
The coverage record accounts for every branch not already refuted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is SAT}\iff\exists C\in\mathcal C:\ F\land C\text{ is SAT}\).

notation.meaning: conjunction of literals passed as solver assumptions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is appropriate, and conjunctive cube assumptions are the correct basic interface. No source supports the proposed handoff contents, and 'simplified solver state' lacks an equivalence or reconstruction condition needed for a correctness claim.

children.title: Hybrid Solver Variants
children.top_down_role: Sequential, parallel, adaptive, and recursively partitioned cube-based configurations.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Solver Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by partitioner, conquer engine, scheduling, and feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cube–conquer hybrid solver may be represented by a tuple \(H=(P,K,S,Q,G)\), where \(P\) is the look-ahead partitioner, \(K\) its cutoff rule, \(S\) a sound complete conquer solver, \(Q\) a sequential or parallel cube scheduler, and \(G\) an optional feedback channel carrying bounds or learned information. Offline variants generate all cubes before conquest; online variants interleave generation and conquest. Correctness is invariant under these choices provided cube coverage is maintained and all transferred constraints are logical consequences of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid variants differ in partitioning, cutoff, conquer solver, scheduling, and feedback, while correctness requires cube coverage and sound transferred constraints.
assumptions_latex: The partitioner outputs cubes whose surviving union covers \(F\).
The conquer solver is sound and complete under assumptions.
Feedback constraints are implied by \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every tuple satisfying these conditions decides satisfiability of \(F\) correctly, whether partitioning and conquest are offline or interleaved.

notation.meaning: partitioner, cutoff, conquer solver, scheduler, and feedback channel

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind can fit a variants container, but the tuple classification is synthetic and uncited. For online interleaving, coverage and logical consequence of feedback alone do not explicitly supply termination or fair processing conditions sufficient for the universal decision claim.

children.title: Partition-Imbalance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Subproblem distributions dominated by a small number of difficult partitions.

assumptions_latex: Cube workloads are nonnegative and measured on identical workers.
Each cube is processed by at most one worker at a time.
Inter-worker overhead is excluded from \(w_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_p\geq\max\{W/p,w_{\max}\}\), with strong imbalance when \(w_{\max}\gg W/p\).

notation.meaning: work required to solve cube i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel slowdown caused by unequal cube-solving workloads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cube workloads \(w_1,\ldots,w_m\geq 0\) assigned to \(p\) identical conquer workers, let \(W=\sum_i w_i\) and \(w_{\max}=\max_i w_i\). Any schedule has makespan \(T_p\geq\max\{W/p,w_{\max}\}\). The partition is balanced when \(w_{\max}=O(W/p)\); it is imbalance-dominated when \(w_{\max}\gg W/p\), because one hard cube determines completion time and prevents near-linear speedup regardless of the number of easier cubes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel conquest is imbalance-dominated when one cube costs far more than the average per worker, forcing that cube to determine completion time.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Imbalance Regimes

children.title: Partition-Overhead Regimes
children.top_down_role: Excessive decomposition costs or overly numerous subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Overhead Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime boundary where cube generation and dispatch erase decomposition gains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_{m mono}\) be the cost of solving \(F\) monolithically, \(P\) the cube-generation cost, \(H\) the total serialization, dispatch, and initialization overhead, and \(C_p\) the conquer makespan on \(p\) workers. Partitioning improves runtime exactly when \(P+H+C_p<T_{m mono}\). The overhead-dominated regime begins at \(P+H\geq T_{m mono}-C_p\); producing more cubes then cannot help unless the resulting reduction in \(C_p\) exceeds their additional generation and management cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning helps only if generation and management overhead plus parallel conquest cost less than monolithic solving.
assumptions_latex: All quantities measure the same runtime resource.
\(C_p\) includes conquer computation but excludes \(P\) and \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition-overhead boundary is \(P+H=T_{m mono}-C_p\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the equality is an accounting boundary defined by the introduced quantities rather than a sourced SAT cutoff result. An inspectable source is required for the decomposition model and the claimed regime interpretation.

children.title: Premature-Cutoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cutoffs that transfer insufficiently simplified subproblems.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a CNF formula.
\(T(d)=P(d)+\sum_{u\in L_d}S(F_u)\) measures total work at cutoff depth \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\) is premature exactly when some deeper cutoff has smaller measured work.

notation.meaning: residual subinstances produced at depth d
complete-solver work on residual formula G

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure boundary for choosing the look-ahead-to-complete-solver handoff depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each admissible cutoff depth \(d\), let look-ahead partitioning produce residual formulas \(\{F_u:u\in L_d\}\), and define total measured work by \[T(d)=P(d)+\sum_{u\in L_d}S(F_u).\] The cutoff \(d\) lies in the premature-cutoff regime when \[\exists d'>d\quad T(d')<T(d).\] Thus additional look-ahead refinement would reduce total work: the reduction in residual complete-solver work exceeds the extra partitioning cost. This definition is relative to the fixed cost measure, branching policy, and residual solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutoff is premature when deeper look-ahead partitioning would lower partitioning cost plus the aggregate cost of solving all residual instances.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature-Cutoff Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the operational definition is internally coherent, but no citation or inspectable locator supports this cutoff-cost model or the interpretation of premature cutoff. A relevant look-ahead hybrid SAT source is required.

children.title: Delayed-Cutoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cutoffs that spend excessive effort within the partitioning phase.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a CNF formula.
\(T(d)=P(d)+\sum_{u\in L_d}S(F_u)\) measures total work at cutoff depth \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\) is delayed exactly when some shallower cutoff has smaller measured work.

notation.meaning: residual subinstances produced at depth d
complete-solver work on residual formula G

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure boundary for excessive look-ahead before solver handoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each admissible cutoff depth \(d\), let look-ahead partitioning produce residual formulas \(\{F_u:u\in L_d\}\), and define \[T(d)=P(d)+\sum_{u\in L_d}S(F_u).\] The cutoff \(d\) lies in the delayed-cutoff regime when \[\exists d'<d\quad T(d')<T(d).\] Hence some look-ahead performed after depth \(d'\) costs more than the residual complete-solver work it avoids. The classification depends on the chosen work measure, branching policy, and residual solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutoff is delayed when handing residual instances to the complete solver earlier would reduce total measured work.
knowledge_statements.title: Delayed-Cutoff Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the shallower-cutoff comparison matches the local title. No cited source supports the total-work model or this delayed-cutoff classification, so an inspectable SAT-specific source is required.

children.title: Exact Exponential SAT Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Complete randomized and deterministic exact algorithms, separated from incomplete stochastic local search.

children.title: Exact Branching Families
children.top_down_role: Case-splitting families for exact exponential SAT solving.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Every reduction preserves satisfiability, and every branch family is exhaustive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion returns SAT exactly when \(F\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: reduced residual formula at a search node
exhaustive branch restrictions selected for G
formula G restricted by partial assignment rho

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic deterministic branching scheme underlying exact exponential SAT algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On input \(F\), repeatedly apply satisfiability-preserving reductions to obtain \(G\). If \(G\) contains an empty clause, return UNSAT; if \(G\) has no clauses, return SAT with the accumulated assignment. Otherwise choose partial assignments \(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_t\) satisfying the exhaustiveness condition \[G\text{ is satisfiable}\iff \bigvee_{i=1}^{t}\bigl(G\!\upharpoonright\!\rho_i\text{ is satisfiable}\bigr).\] Recursively solve every restricted instance until one returns SAT, and return UNSAT only if all branches return UNSAT. Finite measure decrease on every branch guarantees termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact branching algorithm applies sound reductions, recursively explores an exhaustive family of restrictions, and reports unsatisfiability only after every branch fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Branching Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Exact Branching Families, and the exhaustive-branch condition supports correctness. However, no source is cited, and strict measure decrease is stated only for branches; termination also requires the reduction phase itself to terminate and the recursion measure to be well founded.

children.title: Measure-Based Analyses
children.top_down_role: Weighted progress measures used to organize exponential running-time bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(\mu(G)\ge 0\) for every residual instance \(G\).
Polynomial work is performed at each recursion node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every branch satisfies the recurrence, the running time is \(O^*(\alpha^{\mu(F)})\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative measure of residual instance G
measure decreases in a branching rule
largest branching number among all rules

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure-and-conquer recurrence bound for a finite exact branching algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every recursive branch from \(G\) produces instances \(G_1,\ldots,G_t\) with \(\mu(G_i)\le \mu(G)-\delta_i\), where every \(\delta_i>0\). Let \(\alpha\ge 1\) be the maximum, over all branching rules, of the positive root of \[\sum_{i=1}^{t}x^{-\delta_i}=1.\] Then the search-tree recurrence \(T(m)\le \sum_i T(m-\delta_i)+m^{O(1)}\) yields \[T(F)=O^*\!\left(\alpha^{\mu(F)}\right),\] where \(O^*\) suppresses factors polynomial in the input size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive measure decreases yield an exponential search-tree bound whose base is the worst positive root of the branching recurrence.
knowledge_statements.title: Measure-Based Analyses

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits Measure-Based Analyses, but the claimed O-star bound needs a source and more explicit hypotheses concerning base cases, finitely many rule types, the relation between the measure and input size, and control of per-node polynomial work. The treatment of rules whose characteristic root is 1 also needs source-checked qualification.

children.title: Branching-Vector Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural cases distinguished by their recursive size reductions.

assumptions_latex: Each recursive child has strictly smaller measure than its parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The branching number is the unique \(\alpha>1\) satisfying \(\sum_i\alpha^{-\delta_i}=1\), except that a single branch has number \(1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local recurrence descriptor for measure-guided branching rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a branching rule maps an instance of measure \(m\) to \(t\) children whose measures are at most \(m-\delta_1,\ldots,m-\delta_t\), with \(\delta_i>0\), its branching vector is \[\boldsymbol{\delta}=(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_t).\] For \(t\ge 2\), its branching number \(\alpha(\boldsymbol{\delta})\) is the unique real \(\alpha>1\) satisfying \[\sum_{i=1}^{t}\alpha^{-\delta_i}=1.\] For \(t=1\), set \(\alpha(\boldsymbol{\delta})=1\). A regime is a collection of rules compared under one common measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching vector records the measure drop in every child; its characteristic root determines that rule's exponential recurrence base.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Vector Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the branching-vector terminal, and the characteristic-root definition is standard and internally consistent. It nevertheless has no citation or locator; an authoritative exact-algorithms or measure-and-conquer source is required.

children.title: Measure–Branching Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Alignment between branching cases and the progress measure used for analysis.

assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is evaluated on every residual instance produced by the algorithm.
\(\alpha>1\) is a proposed uniform exponential base.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility holds exactly when every applicable rule satisfies \(\delta_i>0\) and \(\sum_i\alpha^{-\delta_i}\le 1\).

notation.meaning: measure decrease from a parent to child i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate linking a chosen measure to all branching rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A measure \(\mu\) and a branching family are compatible with base \(\alpha>1\) when, for every reachable nonterminal instance \(G\) and every child \(G_i\) of its selected rule, \[\delta_i=\mu(G)-\mu(G_i)>0,\qquad \sum_i\alpha^{-\delta_i}\le 1.\] Reductions outside branching must not increase \(\mu\), and terminal instances must have bounded measure. Under these conditions the same inductive exponential bound applies at every node; failure of positivity or of the displayed inequality invalidates that bound for the proposed measure and base.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measure fits a branching family when every branch decreases it and every branching vector satisfies one common recurrence inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Measure–Branching Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the compatibility terminal. No source is supplied, and the conclusion's 'exactly when' omits additional conditions stated in the body, including nonincreasing reductions, bounded terminal cases, and implicitly terminating nonbranching processing. The precise sufficient or necessary-and-sufficient formulation must be source checked.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(k\)-CNF formula on \(n\) variables with \(k\ge 2\).
Random choices are independent and uniformly distributed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned assignment satisfies \(F\); failure after \(R\) trials is inconclusive.

notation.meaning: walk-length constant, commonly chosen at least one

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restarted Schöning walk without asserting a version-specific success constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each of \(R\) independent trials, sample \(a\) uniformly from \(\{0,1\}^n\). For at most \(cn\) steps, test whether \(a\models F\); if so, return \(a\). Otherwise select an unsatisfied clause \(C\), choose a variable \(x\in C\) uniformly, and flip \(a(x)\). If no trial finds a satisfying assignment, return FAIL. Every successful output is directly verifiable. For satisfiable \(F\), the success probability is amplified from a single-trial probability \(p>0\) to \(1-(1-p)^R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Schöning's method repeatedly starts from a random assignment and repairs a randomly chosen variable in an unsatisfied clause, returning only verified solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Schöning Random-Walk Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Schöning family and successful outputs are soundly verified. An authoritative source is required to fix the walk length, clause-selection convention, admissible clause widths, and the single-trial probability p underlying the amplification statement.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(k\)-CNF formula on variables \(V\).
A fixed bounded-width implication rule determines when a variable is forced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned assignment satisfies \(F\); repeated independent runs amplify success probability.

notation.meaning: uniformly random ordering of the variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic bounded-implication PPSZ procedure; constants depend on the selected forcing variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a uniformly random permutation \(\pi\) of \(V\), initialize \(\sigma=\varnothing\), and process variables in \(\pi\)-order. When processing \(x\), if the fixed width-\(s\) implication oracle proves that exactly one value \(b\in\{0,1\}\) is consistent with \(F\) under \(\sigma\), set \(\sigma(x)=b\); otherwise choose \(b\) uniformly and set \(\sigma(x)=b\). After all variables are assigned, return \(\sigma\) only if \(\sigma\models F\), and otherwise return FAIL. Independent repetitions amplify the probability of producing a satisfying assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PPSZ processes variables in random order, assigns provably forced values, guesses the others, and returns only assignments that satisfy the formula.
knowledge_statements.title: PPSZ Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the PPSZ family, but the width-s implication oracle is not defined precisely enough to identify a standard PPSZ variant. A versioned authoritative source must specify the forcing rule and support the associated success-amplification claim.

children.title: Covering-Code Constructions
children.top_down_role: Code families used to cover assignment space with bounded-radius neighborhoods.

assumptions_latex: \(0\le r\le n\).
Distance is Hamming distance on \(\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an \(r\)-covering code of size at most \(\left\lceil (2^n/V(n,r))(1+\ln V(n,r))\right\rceil\).
