notation.meaning: volume of a binary Hamming ball of radius r

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary Hamming covering obtained through the standard greedy set-cover bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V(n,r)=\sum_{i=0}^{r}\binom{n}{i}\). There exists a set \(C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) such that \[\forall x\in\{0,1\}^n\quad \exists c\in C\quad d_H(x,c)\le r,\] and \[|C|\le \left\lceil\frac{2^n}{V(n,r)}\bigl(1+\ln V(n,r)\bigr)\right\rceil.\] Such a set can be obtained by applying the greedy set-cover construction to the family of all radius-\(r\) Hamming balls; the statement concerns existence and deterministic construction, not efficient enumeration for arbitrary \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary radius-r covering code exists within a logarithmic factor of the Hamming sphere-volume lower bound and can be selected greedily.
knowledge_statements.title: Covering-Code Constructions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A theorem is an appropriate role for this covering-code existence bound within the constructions terminal. The coverage formula is plausible, but no relevant citation verifies the exact logarithmic factor, ceiling, or deterministic greedy-construction claim; a covering-code or set-cover theorem locator is required.

children.title: Deterministic Search-Space Coverage
children.top_down_role: Deterministic organization of assignment-space exploration.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is an \(r\)-covering code in \(\{0,1\}^n\).
The local procedure finds a solution whenever its start is within Hamming distance \(r\) of one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The deterministic enumeration finds a satisfying assignment whenever one exists.

notation.meaning: deterministic radius-r local search from center c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic replacement of random initial assignments by covering-code centers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On input formula \(F\), construct or enumerate an \(r\)-covering code \(C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\). For each \(c\in C\), run \(A(F,c,r)\); return the first assignment \(a\) for which \(a\models F\), and return UNSAT only after every invocation has exhaustively rejected its radius-\(r\) neighborhood. If \(a^*\models F\), coverage supplies some \(c\in C\) with \(d_H(a^*,c)\le r\), so the assumed completeness of \(A\) within that neighborhood guarantees discovery. Verification of any returned assignment is direct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerating all covering-code centers deterministically reaches the radius-r neighborhood of every assignment, so a complete local search cannot miss a solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Search-Space Coverage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits deterministic search-space coverage, and the coverage argument is coherent. No source is cited, and the local procedure's contract must explicitly establish completeness within each ball and justify any exhaustive rejection used before returning UNSAT.

children.title: Code-Radius Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Coverage size, neighborhood radius, and resulting search-cost regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) is an \(r\)-covering code.
Each radius-r search costs at most \(L(n,r)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(2^n/V(n,r)\le |C|\), and total search time is \(O^*(|C|L(n,r))\).

notation.meaning: cost of one radius-r local search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sphere-volume versus local-search tradeoff for binary covering-code derandomization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because the radius-\(r\) balls centered at \(C\) cover \(2^n\) assignments and each contains \(V(n,r)\) points, \[|C|V(n,r)\ge 2^n.\] Hence every such code satisfies \(|C|\ge 2^n/V(n,r)\), while standard greedy constructions attain this scale up to a logarithmic factor. Enumerating all centers and spending at most \(L(n,r)\) per center costs \[O^*\!\left(|C|L(n,r)\right).\] Increasing \(r\) decreases the required number of centers but may increase the local-search cost, so the useful radius minimizes their product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger covering radius requires fewer code centers but permits more expensive local search; deterministic time is governed by the product of both costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Code-Radius Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits the code-radius tradeoff terminal. The sphere-volume lower bound is standard, but the greedy upper-bound assertion and total-time formula lack citations; the latter also needs a stated assumption that constructing or enumerating C does not exceed the displayed O-star cost.

children.title: Derandomization Overhead Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial or computational costs introduced by deterministic coverage.

assumptions_latex: A randomized trial costs \(Q(n,r)\) and succeeds with probability at least \(p(n,r)>0\).
A deterministic cover has size \(M(n,r)\) and per-center cost \(D(n,r)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Derandomization preserves the exponential rate only if \(M(n,r)D(n,r)=O^*(Q(n,r)/p(n,r))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic boundary comparing deterministic coverage with restart-based randomized search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Independent randomized repetition has expected work at most \(Q(n,r)/p(n,r)\) until success on a satisfiable instance. Deterministic coverage costs \(M(n,r)D(n,r)\). The covering-code derandomization preserves the randomized exponential rate when \[M(n,r)D(n,r)=O^*\!\left(\frac{Q(n,r)}{p(n,r)}\right).\] It crosses the overhead failure boundary when the ratio \[\frac{M(n,r)D(n,r)p(n,r)}{Q(n,r)}\] grows exponentially in \(n\). Polynomial or subexponential construction overhead may be absorbed only according to the accuracy intended by the \(O^*\) comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derandomization loses the randomized exponential rate when code enumeration and local search exceed restart-based expected work by an exponential factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Derandomization Overhead Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, but no source supports this comparison model. The claim that rate preservation holds 'only if' the O-star inequality holds depends on whether equal exponential rate ignores polynomial factors only or also subexponential factors; the final sentence mixes these conventions. The boundary must be defined and source checked.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Width Exact-Algorithm Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary deterministic exact bound for CNF formulas of maximum clause width \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula on \(n\) variables whose clauses have width at most \(k\). Select a clause \(C\) containing \(r\) distinct variables and recursively branch over the \(2^r-1\) assignments to those variables that satisfy \(C\), simplifying \(F\) in every branch. Empty clauses reject and formulas without clauses accept. The search satisfies \[T(n)\le (2^r-1)T(n-r)+\operatorname{poly}(|F|).\] Since \((2^r-1)^{1/r}\le (2^k-1)^{1/k}\) for \(r\le k\), the worst-case running time is \[O^*((2^k-1)^{n/k}),\] with polynomial space under depth-first traversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching over all satisfying assignments of a selected width-at-most-k clause gives a deterministic exact SAT algorithm with the stated exponential bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula on \(n\) Boolean variables.
Every clause has at most \(k\) distinct literals and contains no complementary pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is decided exactly in time \(O^*((2^k-1)^{n/k})\) using polynomial space.

notation.meaning: A bound suppressing factors polynomial in the input size.
Worst-case recursive running time on n remaining variables.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the leaf and the branching analysis is plausible, but no source supports the recurrence, monotonicity step, time bound, or polynomial-space claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Parallelism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cooperative or independent portfolio of complete SAT solvers on one formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\) and complete SAT procedures \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), run one configured procedure per worker under a fair scheduler. A worker may publish learned clauses only when they are certified consequences of \(F\). Stop when a worker returns an assignment \(a\) satisfying \(F\), or returns an independently checkable refutation of \(F\). Accept a SAT result only after evaluating \(F(a)=1\), and accept an UNSAT result only after checking its refutation. If at least one worker receives unbounded computation and is complete, the portfolio eventually returns the correct status of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run diverse complete solvers concurrently and accept only checked models or refutations; fairness to one complete worker preserves termination and correctness.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
At least one \(S_i\) is complete and receives unbounded computation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The portfolio terminates with SAT exactly when \(F\) has a model, and otherwise with a checked UNSAT certificate.

notation.meaning: The complete SAT procedure assigned to worker i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits portfolio parallelism, but the fairness, certificate-checking, clause-publication, and termination claims have no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Space Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cube-based decomposition of a complete SAT search space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) use variables \(V\), and let \(D_1,	\ldots,D_m\) be cubes, each a conjunction of literals over \(V\). If every total assignment to \(V\) satisfies at least one cube, equivalently \[\models D_1\lor\cdots\lor D_m,\] then \[F\text{ is satisfiable}\iff \bigvee_{i=1}^m(F\land D_i)\text{ is satisfiable}.\] Thus the subinstances may be solved independently. An UNSAT conclusion for \(F\) is valid only after every covering subinstance \(F\land D_i\) has been refuted; pairwise disjointness of the cubes is optional but prevents duplicated search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering family of cubes decomposes SAT into independent subinstances; global UNSAT requires a refutation for every covered region.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula over \(V\).
\(\models\bigvee_{i=1}^{m}D_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable if and only if some \(F\land D_i\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: A cube defining one search-space region.
The variables of the original formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits search-space partitioning and the covering-cube equivalence is mathematically plausible, but no source supports the formulation or its global-UNSAT condition.

children.title: Clause Export Policies
children.top_down_role: Selection of locally learned clauses for transmission to peer workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Export Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound bounded selection of learned clauses for inter-worker transmission.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each newly learned clause \(C\), a worker first records a derivation establishing \(F\models C\). It computes policy features such as length \(|C|\), literal-block distance \(\operatorname{LBD}(C)\), activity, and estimated reuse. Given thresholds \(L,B\) and a communication budget \(q\), enqueue \(C\) for export only if \[|C|\le L,\qquad \operatorname{LBD}(C)\le B,\] and capacity remains; otherwise retain it locally. Any ranking or throttling rule may replace these inequalities, but it may affect only which entailed clauses are transmitted, never their validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Export only derivationally valid learned clauses selected by size, quality, activity, and bandwidth limits; selection changes performance but not correctness.
assumptions_latex: Every export candidate \(C\) has a checkable derivation from \(F\).
The export queue has finite capacity \(q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every transmitted clause \(C\) satisfies \(F\models C\), while export volume respects the configured budget.

notation.meaning: Number of distinct decision levels represented in clause C.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the proposed LBD, length, activity, reuse, and communication-budget policy is an uncited design specification rather than source-supported knowledge.

children.title: Clause Import Filtering
children.top_down_role: Admission criteria for clauses received from peer workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Import Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receiver-side validity, duplication, and resource filtering for shared clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a worker receives a clause \(C\), it checks or trusts through an authenticated proof interface that \(F\models C\), canonicalizes its literals, and rejects tautological, duplicate, or already subsumed clauses. It may additionally require \(|C|\le L\), \(\operatorname{LBD}(C)\le B\), or available storage. An accepted clause enters a pending-import queue; a rejected clause does not alter the solver state. Filtering by heuristic quality is completeness-preserving because ignoring an entailed learned clause leaves the worker's original complete search procedure unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate and canonicalize received clauses, then reject redundant or over-budget imports; ignoring valid learned clauses does not compromise completeness.
assumptions_latex: The unshared local solver is complete for \(F\).
Every accepted clause \(C\) is established to satisfy \(F\models C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Import filtering preserves the models of \(F\) and the completeness of the local solver.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits clause import filtering, but the authenticated-proof interface, subsumption filtering, and completeness-preservation claims require a specific parallel-SAT or CDCL source.

children.title: Shared-Clause Integration
children.top_down_role: Placement, prioritization, and lifecycle of imported clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Clause Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe-point incorporation of an imported learned clause into CDCL state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a solver safe point, take an accepted clause \(C\) with \(F\models C\), insert it into the clause database, and initialize its watched literals. Evaluate \(C\) under the current partial assignment \(\alpha\). If \(C\) is satisfied, continue; if it is unit, enqueue its remaining literal and perform propagation; if it is falsified, invoke ordinary conflict analysis and backtracking. The integrated database is \(F'=F\land C\), and \[\operatorname{Mod}(F')=\operatorname{Mod}(F)\] because \(C\) is entailed by \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attach an entailed imported clause at a safe point, then propagate or analyze conflict; the strengthened database has exactly the original models.
assumptions_latex: \(F\models C\).
Integration occurs where clause-database and propagation invariants can be restored atomically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After integration, the solver operates on \(F\land C\) with \(\operatorname{Mod}(F\land C)=\operatorname{Mod}(F)\).

notation.meaning: The receiving worker's current partial assignment.
Set of total Boolean models of F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits shared-clause integration and model preservation follows from entailment, but the safe-point, watched-literal, propagation, and conflict-handling procedure is uncited.

children.title: Communication-Load Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Bandwidth, synchronization, and database-pressure limits of clause exchange.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Load Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bandwidth, processing, and queue-stability limits for shared-clause traffic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(p\) workers each export at most \(q\) clauses per second, with mean encoded length at most \(s\) bits. All-to-all dissemination requires aggregate network traffic at most \[p(p-1)qs\ \text{bits per second}.\] A receiver offered clauses at rate \(\lambda\) and able to validate and integrate them at rate \(\mu\) has bounded long-run backlog only when \(\lambda<\mu\) under a work-conserving stable queue model. Hence export throttling or selective routing must enforce both available bandwidth \(W\ge p(p-1)qs\) and receiver capacity \(\lambda<\mu\); otherwise communication or pending imports can grow without bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All-to-all clause traffic scales quadratically with workers, and stable import queues require arrival rate below validation-and-integration capacity.
assumptions_latex: Exports have rate at most \(q\) and mean encoding size at most \(s\).
The receiver is modeled as a work-conserving queue with rates \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sustainable operation requires \(W\ge p(p-1)qs\) and \(\lambda<\mu\).

notation.meaning: Clause arrival rate at one receiver.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the leaf, but the all-to-all traffic calculation and especially the claim that lambda below mu yields bounded long-run backlog depend on an insufficiently specified queueing and routing model.

children.title: Parallel Proof Logging
children.top_down_role: Proof-trace production across concurrent solver workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Proof Logging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-addressed logging of parallel clause derivations for checkable UNSAT certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign every original or derived clause a globally unique identifier. Whenever a worker adds a clause \(C_j\), log its identifier, its antecedent identifiers, and a locally checkable inference establishing that the antecedents imply \(C_j\); log deletions without treating them as inferences. Imported clauses retain their identifiers or receive a recorded alias. If the combined dependency graph is acyclic, every antecedent precedes its use, and some logged inference derives the empty clause \(\bot\), then a checker can validate the merged log from \(F\) alone. The validated derivation of \(\bot\) certifies that \(F\) is unsatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally identify clauses and log checkable dependencies; an acyclic merged derivation ending in the empty clause is an UNSAT certificate.
assumptions_latex: Every logged addition is checkable in the selected proof system.
Clause identifiers are globally unique or have unambiguous recorded aliases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A validated merged derivation of \(\bot\) certifies \(F\models\bot\).

notation.meaning: A logged original or derived clause.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits parallel proof logging, but validity depends on the selected proof format and its rules for additions, aliases, ordering, and deletions; no source or precise proof system is supplied.

children.title: Deterministic Parallel Replay
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction of reproducible solver outcomes from concurrent executions.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Parallel Replay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replay from a totally ordered event log and deterministic transition semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Record the initial formula and configurations, all random seeds, and a total order \(e_1,	\ldots,e_T\) of state-changing events, including decisions, propagations, clause imports, deletions, restarts, and worker-result commitments. Starting from the recorded initial state \(s_0\), apply a deterministic transition function \(s_t=\delta(s_{t-1},e_t)\). Reject the log if an event is not enabled or its recorded result disagrees with recomputation. If solver transitions, tie-breaking, and serialization are deterministic, replay reconstructs one unique state sequence and the same final model or refutation, independently of the replay machine's thread schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete total event order, fixed seeds, and deterministic transitions reconstruct one unique execution and its checked result.
assumptions_latex: The log contains every state-changing event and all nondeterministic choices.
\(\delta\) and all tie-breaking rules are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence \(s_t=\delta(s_{t-1},e_t)\) uniquely reproduces the recorded terminal result.

notation.meaning: The t-th event in the recorded total order.
The complete replay state after event t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits deterministic replay, but the asserted sufficiency of the recorded events and deterministic serialization assumptions needs a concrete replay model and supporting source.

children.title: Proof-Trace Merge Policies
children.top_down_role: Organization of worker-local derivations into a checkable global trace.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Trace Merge Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-preserving merge of worker-local proof traces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form a directed graph whose vertices are logged clause additions and whose arcs point from each antecedent to the inference using it. Resolve identifier aliases for imported clauses, reject inconsistent duplicate identifiers, and topologically sort the graph. Emit original clauses first, then derived additions in topological order; emit a deletion only after every retained use that requires the deleted clause. Check each emitted inference in the chosen proof system. The merge succeeds exactly when dependencies are acyclic and a checked path of additions derives \(\bot\); the resulting sequential trace is then a valid refutation of the common input formula \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve shared identifiers and topologically order all derivations; a checked dependency-respecting trace ending in the empty clause is a valid refutation.
assumptions_latex: All worker traces refer to the same input formula \(F\).
Every cross-worker clause reference has an unambiguous identifier mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful merge produces a sequentially checkable derivation of \(\bot\) from \(F\).

notation.meaning: The empty clause derived at the end of a refutation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits proof-trace merging, but deletion legality and merge success are proof-format dependent, and the stated exact success condition is unsupported without a specified proof system and source.

children.title: Concurrency-Induced Nondeterminism
children.top_down_role: Scheduling, communication, and ordering effects that impair reproducibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Concurrency-Induced Nondeterminism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncommuting concurrent events prevent trace reproducibility without changing certified correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a worker's partial assignment leave \(x\) unset while two events are enabled: \(e_d\) decides \(\neg x\), and \(e_i\) imports the entailed unit clause \((x)\). Applying \(e_d\) before \(e_i\) creates an immediate conflict, whereas applying \(e_i\) first propagates \(x\) and disables \(e_d\). Thus \[\delta(\delta(s,e_d),e_i)\ne\delta(\delta(s,e_i),e_d).\] If message arrival and scheduling order are unrecorded, identical formulas, configurations, and random seeds need not yield identical search or proof traces. Soundness remains possible when every final model or refutation is independently checked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision and an imported unit clause can produce different states in opposite orders, so unrecorded scheduling destroys trace reproducibility.
assumptions_latex: \(F\models(x)\), while the receiving state has not yet propagated \(x\).
Concurrent event order is not fixed or recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The execution trace is not determined by \(F\), configuration, and random seeds alone.

notation.meaning: A decision event assigning false to x.
An event importing the entailed unit clause containing x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf and the example plausibly demonstrates noncommuting events, but the transition semantics and resulting reproducibility claim have no cited support.

children.title: SAT Formula Transformation Calculus
children.top_down_role: CNF simplification, redundancy management, structure recovery, reconstruction, and preservation boundaries.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Classical, resolution-based, and redundancy-based preprocessing; solution reconstruction; higher-level representations

children.title: Unit-Clause Simplification
children.top_down_role: Formula reduction driven by unit-clause consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Clause Simplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equisatisfiable restriction and reconstruction under a forced unit literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) contain the unit clause \((\ell)\). Set \(\ell\) to true, delete every clause containing \(\ell\), and delete \(\neg\ell\) from every remaining clause; denote the result by \(F\mathbin{|}_{\ell=1}\). If an empty clause is produced, report conflict. Otherwise repeat this operation for newly created unit clauses until none remain. Then \[F\text{ is satisfiable}\iff F\mathbin{|}_{\ell=1}\text{ is satisfiable}.\] Every model of the simplified formula extends to a model of \(F\) by assigning \(\ell=1\), together with all unit assignments recorded during propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign a unit literal true, remove satisfied clauses and its negation elsewhere, and record assignments so simplified models reconstruct original models.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula containing the unit clause \((\ell)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) and \(F\mathbin{|}_{\ell=1}\) are equisatisfiable, with model reconstruction by restoring \(\ell=1\).

notation.meaning: The literal forced true by a unit clause.
Formula obtained by restricting the unit literal to true.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits unit-clause simplification and the core claim is standard, but no authoritative source is cited, and the notation names a single restriction while the statement and reconstruction also cover iterated propagation.

children.title: Pure-Literal Simplification
children.top_down_role: Formula reduction using variables occurring with a single polarity.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Literal \(\ell\) occurs in \(F\), while \(\bar\ell\) does not.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) and \(F'\) are equisatisfiable, and every model of \(F'\) extends to a model of \(F\) by setting \(\ell\) true.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard propositional CNF pure-literal elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Delete every clause containing \(\ell\) and call the resulting formula \(F'\). Then \(F\) is satisfiable if and only if \(F'\) is satisfiable. Moreover, any satisfying assignment of \(F'\) extends to one of \(F\) by assigning the variable of \(\ell\) so that \(\ell\) is true; assignments to all other variables remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A literal appearing without its complement may be set true, allowing all clauses containing it to be deleted without changing satisfiability.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure-Literal Simplification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pure-literal simplification claim is mathematically standard, internally consistent, and appropriate as a property, but no inspectable SAT source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Simplification Interaction Order
children.top_down_role: Ordering effects between unit-driven reductions and polarity-driven reductions.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Each step is unit propagation or pure-literal elimination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every terminating sequence produces an equisatisfiable residual formula, although different legal orders can produce different residual formulas.

notation.meaning: A residual formula obtained after a terminating simplification sequence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic invariance under interleaved unit and pure-literal simplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply either rule whenever enabled, deleting satisfied clauses and deleting falsified literals after forced assignments. Every finite terminating sequence from \(F\) yields a residual \(F_i\) equisatisfiable with \(F\). The residual syntax need not be unique because one rule can remove occurrences that enable or disable the other; therefore implementations seeking a stable closure must specify an order and iterate it to a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any legal interleaving preserves satisfiability, but the residual syntax may depend on order; a deterministic preprocessor must specify and iterate its schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplification Interaction Order

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Equisatisfiability of each legal step is standard, but the precise order-dependence and fixed-point scheduling claim requires an authoritative SAT-preprocessing source with a specific locator.

children.title: Reconstruction Requirements
children.top_down_role: Assignment information needed to recover solutions after classical simplification.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is transformed to a residual CNF \(F'\) by unit and pure-literal steps.
\(\alpha'\) satisfies \(F'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reverse replay of the log constructs an assignment \(\alpha\) satisfying \(F\).

notation.meaning: A satisfying assignment of the residual formula.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model reconstruction after satisfiability-preserving literal simplifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The log \(L\) must record each eliminated variable, the assigned literal for every unit step, and a satisfiable polarity for every pure-literal step, in transformation order. Starting from \(\alpha'\), replay \(L\) backward, assigning each absent variable its recorded value while retaining existing values. The resulting total assignment \(\alpha\) must satisfy every clause removed at its corresponding step and hence satisfy \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction requires an ordered log of eliminated variables and chosen values; reverse replay extends any residual model to a model of the original formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Requirements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reconstruction certificate is coherent and fits the terminal container, but the required log contents and reverse-replay guarantee lack cited support.

children.title: Failed-Literal Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of assumptions whose propagated consequences expose inconsistency.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(\ell\) is an unassigned literal of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{UP}(F\land\ell)=\bot\), then \(F\models\bar\ell\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failed literals detected by unit propagation under a temporary assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The literal \(\ell\) is failed for \(F\) when exhaustive unit propagation on \(F\land\ell\) derives an empty clause, written \(\operatorname{UP}(F\land\ell)=\bot\). Because unit propagation is sound, no model of \(F\) can satisfy \(\ell\); consequently \(F\models\bar\ell\), and assigning \(\bar\ell\) is a satisfiability-preserving simplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A literal is failed when assuming it and applying unit propagation causes conflict; its complement is then forced by the formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Failed-Literal Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failed-literal condition and entailment are standard and precisely stated, but no authoritative source with a section, theorem, or page locator is provided.

children.title: Binary Probing
children.top_down_role: Paired polarity exploration for variable-level simplification.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(x\) is an unassigned variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conflicting branches force the opposite literal; literals propagated in both consistent branches are entailed by \(F\).

notation.meaning: The two decision literals for variable \(x\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-branch unit-propagation probing of one Boolean variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(P_x=\operatorname{UP}(F\land x)\) and \(P_{\neg x}=\operatorname{UP}(F\land\neg x)\). If exactly one closure conflicts, permanently assign the literal of the other branch. If both conflict, report \(F\) unsatisfiable. If neither conflicts, permanently assign every literal propagated in both closures. Otherwise leave \(x\) unassigned. Output the simplified formula and the recorded implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probe both values of a variable: reject conflicting branches, detect unsatisfiability if both fail, and retain literals propagated in both surviving branches.
knowledge_statements.title: Binary Probing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-branch probing algorithm is mathematically sound, including conflict and common-implication deductions, but it has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Tree-Based Probing
children.top_down_role: Multi-branch speculative exploration for stronger preprocessing consequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Based Probing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multi-level generalization of binary failed-literal probing using exhaustive binary branching at every expanded node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(T\) with an empty root. At each expanded node \(v\), compute \(P(v)=\operatorname{UP}(F\land A(v))\); close \(v\) on conflict, and otherwise select an unassigned variable \(x\) and create both children with assumptions \(x\) and \(\neg x\). Stop expanding at the prescribed depth or resource limit. Mark an internal node conflicting when both of its children are conflicting. At a nonconflicting node, retain a literal only when it belongs to the unit-propagation closure of every nonconflicting descendant leaf. Output the resulting root-level forced literals, or report unsatisfiability if the root is conflicting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree probing recursively tests both values of each selected variable. Conflicts propagate upward only across exhaustive pairs of branches, and a literal is retained only when every surviving descendant branch propagates it.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(T\) is a finite rooted binary tree.
At every expanded node, the two outgoing edges assume the two complementary literals of one variable unassigned under that node's path assumptions.
Each node is evaluated by exhaustive unit propagation under its root-to-node assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If both exhaustive children of a node conflict, that node conflicts; any literal propagated at every nonconflicting descendant leaf is entailed by \(F\) under the node's path assumptions.

notation.meaning: The conjunction of edge assumptions on the root-to-node path.
The finite exhaustive binary probing tree.

children.title: Probing Budget Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cost limits, candidate selection, and stopping criteria for speculative preprocessing.

assumptions_latex: Each unit-propagation call has a measurable cost.
A finite budget \(B\) is fixed before or during preprocessing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The probing phase must stop once cumulative measured cost reaches \(B\); all deductions obtained before stopping remain sound.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-bounded probing independent of the probe-selection heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative probe costs \(c_i\), admit probe \(k\) only while \(\sum_{i=1}^{k}c_i\le B\). A static regime fixes \(B\) in advance; an adaptive regime may update the remaining allocation using observed costs and deductions but must preserve a finite upper bound. Budget exhaustion changes completeness of detection, not soundness of any failed-literal or common-implication deduction already obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probing stops at a finite cost budget. Larger or adaptive budgets may find more deductions, but early termination does not invalidate deductions already made.
knowledge_statements.title: Probing Budget Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The soundness-versus-budget distinction is plausible, but the static and adaptive regimes are implementation-dependent and require a source defining the cost model and stopping policy.

children.title: Clause Subsumption
children.top_down_role: Detection and removal of clauses rendered redundant by stronger clauses.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Clauses \(C,D\in F\) satisfy \(C\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) and \(F\setminus\{D\}\) are logically equivalent.

notation.meaning: Clauses represented as sets of literals.
The CNF formula with clause \(D\) removed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-based subsumption for non-tautological CNF clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A clause \(C\) subsumes a clause \(D\) exactly when \(C\subseteq D\). Since every assignment satisfying \(C\) also satisfies \(D\), the conjunction containing both clauses is logically equivalent to the conjunction with \(D\) deleted. Thus, whenever \(C,D\in F\) and \(C\subseteq D\), replacing \(F\) by \(F\setminus\{D\}\) preserves every satisfying assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every literal of one clause occurs in another, the larger clause is redundant and may be deleted without changing any model.
knowledge_statements.title: Clause Subsumption

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subsumption criterion and equivalence-preserving deletion are correct and fit a property record, but no SAT source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Self-Subsuming Resolution
children.top_down_role: Literal removal enabled by resolution relationships between clauses.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) contains clauses \(C\lor x\) and \(D\lor\neg x\).
\(C\subseteq D\), and neither \(C\) nor \(D\) contains \(x\) or \(\neg x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(D\lor\neg x\) by \(D\) preserves logical equivalence of the CNF.

notation.meaning: Disjunction of the literals in set \(C\) or \(D\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard self-subsuming resolution strengthening one parent clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Resolving \(C\lor x\) with \(D\lor
eg x\) on \(x\) yields \(C\lor D=D\) because \(C\subseteq D\). The resolvent \(D\) subsumes its parent \(D\lor
eg x\). Hence replacing that parent by \(D\), while retaining \(C\lor x\), produces a CNF logically equivalent to \(F\); operationally, the literal \(
eg x\) is deleted from the second clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a resolvent subsumes one parent, that parent can be strengthened to the resolvent; equivalently, the pivot literal is deleted from it.
knowledge_statements.title: Self-Subsuming Resolution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The self-subsuming-resolution condition and strengthening conclusion are mathematically correct, but the candidate lacks an inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Subsumption Indexing
children.top_down_role: Candidate retrieval structures for subsumption-based processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Subsumption Indexing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate-generation contract for sound and complete subsumption indexing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Build an occurrence, signature, or trie index over the stored clauses. For a query clause \(D\), retrieve a candidate set \(I(D)\) satisfying \(\{C:C\text{ is stored and }C\subseteq D\}\subseteq I(D)\). Test each \(C\in I(D)\) by exact literal-set inclusion, and delete \(D\) only after confirming \(C\subseteq D\). The index may return false candidates, but complete subsumption detection requires it not to omit any true subsumer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The index must return a candidate set containing every stored subset of the query clause. Exact inclusion testing then prevents false deletion, while the candidate-set guarantee ensures complete detection.
assumptions_latex: Stored clauses and the query clause \(D\) are finite sets of literals.
The index output \(I(D)\) contains every stored clause \(C\) satisfying \(C\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact inclusion filtering over \(I(D)\) finds every stored subsumer of \(D\) and deletes \(D\) only when a genuine subsumer exists.

notation.meaning: A candidate set containing every stored subsumer of \(D\).

children.title: Strengthening-Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Search and indexing regimes where strengthening effort outweighs simplification value.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) has \(m\) clauses and total literal count \(L\).
Clauses are stored as sorted literal lists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustive pairwise subsumption and self-subsuming-resolution screening has worst-case time \(O(mL)\), and indexing does not remove this worst case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case boundary under explicit sorted-list clause comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Testing one ordered clause pair for subsumption or a fixed-pivot self-subsuming condition costs \(O(|C|+|D|)\), hence at most \(O(w)\). Exhaustively screening all pairs costs \(O(m^2w)\), equivalently \(O(mL)\) in the worst case. Signature, occurrence, or trie indexes can reduce candidates on typical instances, but an adversarial family may make every pair a candidate, preserving the same asymptotic boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full sorted-list pair scan costs at most quadratic comparisons and O(mL) time; indexes improve typical filtering but not the adversarial worst case.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthening-Cost Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The aggregate sorted-list pair-scan bound is plausible, but the self-subsuming-resolution screening model and adversarial indexing claim require a source specifying the implementation and cost assumptions.

children.title: Connected-Component Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Separation of formulas through disconnected incidence or interaction structure.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
The clause-variable incidence graph of \(F\) has connected components \(G_1,\ldots,G_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\equiv\bigwedge_{i=1}^{k}F_i\), and \(F\) is satisfiable exactly when every \(F_i\) is satisfiable.

notation.meaning: The clauses belonging to incidence component \(G_i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition using connected components of the bipartite clause-variable incidence graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each component \(G_i\), let \(F_i\) contain its clause vertices and let \(V_i\) contain its variable vertices. Then \(V_i\cap V_j=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\), and \(F\equiv\bigwedge_{i=1}^{k}F_i\). Consequently, \(F\) is satisfiable if and only if every \(F_i\) is satisfiable; satisfying component assignments combine uniquely on the disjoint variable sets, apart from variables absent from \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence-graph components have disjoint variables, so the CNF is their conjunction and is satisfiable exactly when all component formulas are satisfiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Connected-Component Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incidence-component representation and satisfiability decomposition are mathematically correct and fit the container, but no relevant source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Variable-Separator Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Partitioning around variables that mediate otherwise weakly connected regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Separator Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separator representation for a finite CNF partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=F_1\land\cdots\land F_k\) be a finite CNF formula, and let \(S\) contain every variable occurring in more than one \(F_i\). For an assignment \(\alpha:S\to\{0,1\}\), let \(F_i\mathbin{|}\alpha\) denote restriction followed by deletion of satisfied clauses and falsified literals. Then
\[
F\text{ is satisfiable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists\alpha:S\to\{0,1\}\;\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\;F_i\mathbin{|}\alpha\text{ is satisfiable}.
\]
When the right side holds, compatible satisfying assignments of the restricted subformulas combine with \(\alpha\) into a satisfying assignment of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CNF split across a variable separator is satisfiable exactly when some separator assignment makes every resulting component satisfiable.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(S\) contains all variables shared by distinct components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is satisfiable iff some assignment to \(S\) makes every \(F_i\mathbin{|}\alpha\) satisfiable.

notation.meaning: component restricted by the separator assignment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separator satisfiability characterization is mathematically plausible and matches the leaf, but no SAT source or inspectable locator is supplied. The record states a satisfiability property rather than primarily giving a representation, so the selected content kind also requires reconsideration after sourcing.

children.title: Independent Subproblem Management
children.top_down_role: Scheduling, solving, and recombination of independent formula components.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Subproblem Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solving and recombining variable-disjoint CNF components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite CNF formula \(F=F_1\land\cdots\land F_k\) with pairwise disjoint variable sets. Solve each \(F_i\) independently. Stop and output UNSAT as soon as one component is unsatisfiable. Otherwise obtain a satisfying assignment \(\alpha_i\) for every component and output SAT with
\[
\alpha=\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i.
\]
Disjointness makes this union well-defined. The output is correct because \(F\) is satisfiable exactly when every \(F_i\) is satisfiable; component results may therefore be scheduled, cached, or processed in parallel without changing the logical result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve variable-disjoint components separately; one unsatisfiable component proves UNSAT, while the union of all component models proves SAT.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite.
\(\operatorname{var}(F_i)\cap\operatorname{var}(F_j)=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns the correct satisfiability status and, for SAT, a model of \(F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm for solving pairwise variable-disjoint components and combining their models is precise and locally appropriate, but it has no cited SAT source with a specific locator.

children.title: Decomposition Overhead Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Granularity and bookkeeping regimes where decomposition provides limited benefit.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Overhead Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case cost of exhaustive separator enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a separator decomposition with \(s=|S|\) and exhaustive enumeration of all assignments \(\alpha:S\to\{0,1\}\). If forming and managing one branch costs at most \(h\), and solving restricted component \(i\) in branch \(\alpha\) costs \(T_i(\alpha)\), then its total running time satisfies
\[
T_{\mathrm{dec}}\le \sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1\}^{S}}\left(h+\sum_{i=1}^{k}T_i(\alpha)\right)\le 2^s\left(h+\max_{\alpha}\sum_{i=1}^{k}T_i(\alpha)\right).
\]
Thus separator enumeration introduces an exponential boundary in \(s\); absent pruning or reuse, decomposition is beneficial only when component savings compensate for this branching and management cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustively branching on a separator of size s creates up to 2^s branches, so component savings must offset enumeration and management costs.
assumptions_latex: Every assignment to the separator is enumerated unless search terminates early.
Branch construction and management cost at most \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{dec}}\le 2^s\bigl(h+\max_{\alpha}\sum_iT_i(\alpha)\bigr)\).

notation.meaning: cost of solving restricted component i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed exhaustive-enumeration bound follows from the stated per-branch cost assumptions and the complexity-bound kind fits the leaf. No relevant source or inspectable locator supports the cost model or boundary claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolution elimination subject to a prescribed growth bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite CNF formula \(F\), a variable \(x\), and a bound \(B\), let \(P\) and \(N\) be the clauses containing \(x\) and \(\neg x\), respectively. Form every non-tautological resolvent
\[
R(C,D)=(C\setminus\{x\})\cup(D\setminus\{\neg x\}),\qquad C\in P,\ D\in N.
\]
If the prescribed cost of these resolvents, such as their count or total literal count, exceeds \(B\), leave \(F\) unchanged. Otherwise replace \(P\cup N\) by the resolvents and simplify. The resulting formula is equisatisfiable with \(F\), and any resulting model can be extended by a suitable value of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate a variable by resolution only when the generated resolvents satisfy a chosen size or growth bound; satisfiability is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
All non-tautological resolvents on \(x\) are generated when elimination is accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted elimination produces a CNF formula equisatisfiable with \(F\).

notation.meaning: positive and negative occurrence clauses for the eliminated variable
resolvent of C and D on x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The resolution-elimination step is plausible, and the algorithm kind fits. A source is required to confirm the exact bounded-variable-elimination convention, including which resolvent cost or growth test defines acceptance and what simplification and reconstruction guarantees accompany it.

knowledge_statements.title: Hyper-Binary Resolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary consequences obtained by a hyper-resolution pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) contain a clause \(C=(l_1\lor\cdots\lor l_k)\), where \(k\ge2\), and binary clauses \((\neg l_i\lor l)\) for every \(i<k\). Hyper-binary resolution adds
\[
(l\lor l_k),
\]
a consequence obtained by resolving \(C\) successively with those binary clauses and deleting duplicate literals. Tautological conclusions are discarded; an already present or subsumed conclusion need not be inserted. Repeating this rule until a resource limit or fixpoint preserves logical equivalence because every inserted binary clause is entailed by the current formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve one long clause against a family of binary clauses to derive an entailed binary clause, discarding tautological or redundant conclusions.
assumptions_latex: All displayed premises occur in the current CNF formula.
Literals are interpreted over Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models(l\lor l_k)\), so adding the derived binary clause preserves equivalence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed inference is an entailed binary resolvent under the stated premises, but hyper-binary resolution has multiple polarity and operational formulations. No authoritative source with a specific locator confirms that this is the intended variant for the leaf.

children.title: Clause Vivification
children.top_down_role: Propagation-guided removal of literals from existing clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Vivification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-propagation strengthening of an existing clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite CNF formula \(F\) and an ordered clause \(C=(l_1\lor\cdots\lor l_k)\in F\). Temporarily remove \(C\), successively assume \(\neg l_1,\ldots,\neg l_j\), and perform unit propagation after each assumption. If the least conflict index is \(j<k\), replace \(C\) by
\[
C'=(l_1\lor\cdots\lor l_j).
\]
The propagation conflict certifies \(F\setminus\{C\}\models C'\); hence replacement preserves logical equivalence. If no conflict or other certified shortening is found, retain \(C\). Stop after the clause is processed or a propagation budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negate a clause's literals in sequence and use unit-propagation conflicts to replace it by a shorter entailed prefix.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite.
Unit propagation is performed on \(F\setminus\{C\}\) under the temporary assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A conflict-derived replacement \(C'\) yields \((F\setminus\{C\})\land C'\equiv F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conflict-derived prefix strengthening is mathematically plausible and algorithmically appropriate, but no source confirms this exact vivification procedure, its least-conflict convention, or its equivalence claim at a specific locator.

children.title: Clause Distillation
children.top_down_role: Clause reduction through implication analysis and redundancy discovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Distillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterated propagation-based deletion or shortening of clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite CNF formula \(F\) and an ordered collection of clauses, process each clause \(C\) against \(F\setminus\{C\}\). Delete \(C\) if propagation establishes that the remaining formula entails it; otherwise replace it by any strictly shorter clause \(C'\subset C\) whose entailment
\[
F\setminus\{C\}\models C'
\]
is certified by unit propagation under negated literals. Commit each accepted change before processing the next clause, and repeat passes until no change occurs or a budget is exhausted. Every step preserves logical equivalence, although the budgeted procedure need not reach a unique or globally minimal formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly use propagation certificates to delete entailed clauses or replace them with shorter entailed subclauses until a fixpoint or budget limit.
assumptions_latex: Every deletion or shortening has a unit-propagation entailment certificate.
Only strict subclauses replace existing clauses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every intermediate and final distilled formula is logically equivalent to \(F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certified deletion and shortening operations would preserve equivalence as stated, but clause distillation terminology and operational scope vary in SAT literature. A specific authoritative locator is needed to establish that this generic iterative procedure matches the intended leaf.

children.title: Candidate-Clause Selection
children.top_down_role: Prioritization of clauses for propagation-intensive strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Clause Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted deterministic selection for clause strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite clause set \(\mathcal C\), a computable priority score \(s:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\), an eligibility predicate \(E\), and an integer budget \(b\ge0\). Form
\[
Q=\{C\in\mathcal C:E(C)=1\},
\]
order \(Q\) by nonincreasing \(s(C)\), breaking ties by a fixed total order, and submit the first \(\min\{b,|Q|\}\) clauses to the strengthening procedure. Selection alone does not alter the formula; logical soundness depends only on accepting strengthening operations carrying valid entailment certificates. The score may incorporate clause length, activity, age, or estimated propagation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter eligible clauses, rank them by a fixed score, and strengthen at most the budgeted number; selection itself makes no logical change.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is finite.
The score, eligibility predicate, tie order, and budget are fixed for the selection call.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(b\) eligible clauses are selected deterministically, without changing the CNF formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic ranking procedure is internally coherent and selection itself does not modify the formula. However, it is a generic policy rather than a sourced SAT candidate-selection method, and no locator supports its placement or claimed canonical role.

children.title: Strengthening Budget Regimes
children.top_down_role: Limits on frequency, effort, and search disruption for clause strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Strengthening Budget Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource conditions for sound budgeted clause refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let strengthening calls consume nonnegative costs \(c_1,c_2,\ldots\), and fix a budget \(B\ge0\). A budget-admissible regime executes call \(t\) only when
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{t}c_j\le B,
\]
and commits its result only if the replacement or deletion has a checkable entailment certificate. The regime terminates when no admissible call remains, a fixpoint is reached, or the budget is exhausted. The budget controls completeness and preprocessing time, not soundness: for every \(B\), the committed output remains equivalent to the input, while different budgets or schedules may produce different strengthened formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run strengthening only while cumulative cost stays within budget, and commit only certified changes; budgets affect completeness and runtime, not equivalence.
assumptions_latex: Each call has a nonnegative measured cost.
Every committed transformation is equivalence preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output remains equivalent to the input for every \(B\ge0\).

notation.meaning: resource cost of strengthening call t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Given the assumption that every committed transformation preserves equivalence, the budget-independence of soundness is valid. The proposed cumulative-cost regime is nevertheless unsourced, and the exact cost and admissibility model requires an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent-Literal Substitution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CNF simplification by certified literal equivalences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite CNF formula \(F\), literals \(l,m\), and a certificate that
\[
F\models(l\leftrightarrow m),
\]
choose one literal as representative and replace every occurrence of the other and its complement consistently, so \(l\) is replaced by \(m\) and \(\neg l\) by \(\neg m\). Remove duplicate literals and tautological clauses, and propagate any resulting units. The simplified formula is equisatisfiable with \(F\). A model is reconstructed by assigning the eliminated variable the value forced by the certified equivalence, including the polarity reversal when the representative is a complemented literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a certified literal equivalence to merge literals, simplify clauses, and reconstruct eliminated variable values from the chosen representative.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
The equivalence \(F\models(l\leftrightarrow m)\) is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistent substitution yields an equisatisfiable formula with model reconstruction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The substitution and reconstruction description is plausible and the algorithm kind fits. A SAT preprocessing source is needed to confirm the exact certified-equivalence precondition, representative handling, simplifications, and model-reconstruction guarantee.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocked-Clause Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Satisfiability-preserving deletion of blocked CNF clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a clause \(C\in F\) and literal \(l\in C\), call \(C\) blocked on \(l\) if, for every clause \(D\in F\) with \(\neg l\in D\), the resolvent
\[
(C\setminus\{l\})\cup(D\setminus\{\neg l\})
\]
is tautological. Blocked-clause elimination repeatedly deletes any blocked clause until none remains or a budget is reached. Each deletion preserves satisfiability: every model of the reduced formula can be converted, if necessary, into a model of the preceding formula by changing the variable of \(l\). The transformation need not preserve logical equivalence or the complete model set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete a clause when all resolvents on one of its literals are tautologies; satisfiability and model reconstruction are preserved, but equivalence need not be.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Blocking is checked against the current formula.

children.title: Covered-Clause Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal of clauses identified through covered-literal structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Covered-Clause Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion after covered-literal extension reaches a blocked clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C\in F\) and \(l\in C\), consider clauses \(D\in F\) containing \(\neg l\) whose resolvent with \(C\) on \(l\) is non-tautological. Any literal occurring in every such \(D\setminus\{\neg l\}\) is a covered literal for \(C\) on \(l\). Repeatedly add covered literals to obtain an extension \(C^+\). If \(C^+\) is blocked in \(F\), then \(C\) is covered and covered-clause elimination deletes \(C\). Covered-literal addition and the final deletion preserve satisfiability, so the reduced formula is equisatisfiable with \(F\), though generally not equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extend a clause by literals common to its relevant resolution partners; if the extension becomes blocked, delete the original clause while preserving satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Covered literals and blocking are computed against the current formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deletion of a covered clause yields a formula equisatisfiable with \(F\).

children.title: Elimination Preservation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model reconstruction and proof-support constraints on covered or hidden elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Preservation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes satisfiability preservation from equivalence and model preservation for covered-hidden elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Covered- and hidden-clause elimination generally preserve only existence of a model, not the complete model set. For example, let \(F=(x\lor y)\land(
eg x\lor
eg y)\) and \(C=(x\lor y)\). The clause \(C\) is blocked by \(x\), because its only resolvent on \(x\) is \(y\lor
eg y\). Hence blocked-clause elimination, and therefore any elimination family subsuming it, may delete \(C\). The reduced formula \(F'=
eg x\lor
eg y\) is satisfiable exactly when \(F\) is satisfiable, but the assignment \(x=0,y=0\) satisfies \(F'\) and not \(F\). Thus logical equivalence and direct preservation of all models cannot be claimed without reconstruction information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These eliminations preserve satisfiability but may add models. A deleted blocked clause gives a concrete failure of logical equivalence.
assumptions_latex: Elimination permits deletion of blocked clauses.
Models are total Boolean assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SAT}(F)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{SAT}(F')\), while \(F\not\equiv F'\) and \(\operatorname{Mod}(F)\subsetneq\operatorname{Mod}(F')\).

notation.meaning: set of total assignments satisfying F

review_flags: Concrete boundary is directly checkable, but an authoritative SAT-preprocessing source is still required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly exhibits satisfiability preservation without model-set preservation and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but no authoritative source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Autarky-Based Simplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause deletion induced by a partial assignment satisfying every clause it touches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite CNF formula and \(\alpha\) a partial Boolean assignment. Say that \(\alpha\) touches a clause when the clause contains a variable in \(\operatorname{dom}(\alpha)\). The assignment \(\alpha\) is an autarky for \(F\) when every touched clause contains a literal made true by \(\alpha\). Let \(T_\alpha\) be the set of touched clauses. Then autarky simplification replaces \(F\) by \(F\setminus T_\alpha\). Every model of the residual formula can be combined with \(\alpha\), resolving shared variables according to \(\alpha\), to obtain a model of \(F\); consequently the original and residual formulas are equisatisfiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An autarky satisfies every clause involving one of its assigned variables. All such clauses can be deleted without changing satisfiability.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite propositional CNF formula.
\(\alpha\) is a consistent partial Boolean assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SAT}(F)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{SAT}(F\setminus T_\alpha)\).
review_flags: Standard autarky theorem lacks a relevant supplied source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The autarky condition and equisatisfiability property fit the topic, but the nontrivial simplification theorem lacks a source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Clause Addition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact satisfiability-redundancy criterion and its stronger implication-based special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite CNF formula and \(C\) a clause. Addition of \(C\) is satisfiability-redundant precisely when \(F\) and \(F\land C\) are equisatisfiable. A stronger, model-preserving condition is \(F\models C\); under this condition every model of \(F\) already satisfies \(C\), so \(F\equiv F\land C\). If only equisatisfiability is established, adding \(C\) may discard models and a model-reconstruction argument or certificate is required when an original model must be returned. If \(F\) is unsatisfiable, every clause is satisfiability-redundant, although implication-based certification remains the directly checkable stronger condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clause is addition-redundant when adding it preserves satisfiability. Entailment is a stronger condition that preserves every model.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite propositional CNF formula.
\(C\) is a clause over the ambient Boolean variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\models C\Longrightarrow F\equiv(F\land C)\Longrightarrow(\operatorname{SAT}(F)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{SAT}(F\land C))\).

notation.meaning: every model of F satisfies C

review_flags: The supplied redundant-constraint locators are not specific enough to certify the SAT clause-addition formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly separates satisfiability redundancy from entailment-based model preservation and fits the leaf, but no SAT-specific authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Boolean Gate Recovery

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Gate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of an AND gate from its complete definitional CNF pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For distinct Boolean variables \(x,y,z\), the three-clause pattern \((
eg z\lor x)\land(
eg z\lor y)\land(z\lor
eg x\lor
eg y)\) is logically equivalent to the gate equation \(z\leftrightarrow(x\land y)\). Boolean gate recovery may therefore replace this complete clause set by the gate record having inputs \(x,y\), output \(z\), and type AND, provided occurrence and ownership bookkeeping preserves any clauses outside the pattern. Recovery is semantic only when all defining directions are present: the first two clauses enforce \(zightarrow x\land y\), whereas the third enforces \(x\land yightarrow z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complete three-clause definitional encoding of an AND relation can be recovered as a gate, with both implication directions required.
assumptions_latex: \(x,y,z\) are distinct Boolean variables.
All three displayed clauses occur in the formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\((
eg z\lor x)\land(
eg z\lor y)\land(z\lor
eg x\lor
eg y)\equiv z\leftrightarrow(x\land y)\).

children.title: Circuit-Fragment Recovery
children.top_down_role: Assembly of recovered gates into larger functional regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Circuit-Fragment Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional recovery of an acyclic gate subgraph from verified local CNF patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\), enumerate candidate gate templates whose complete defining clause sets occur in \(F\). Accept a candidate only after checking that the conjunction of its matched clauses is equivalent, on the candidate variables, to its proposed gate relation. Form a directed graph from each recovered gate's inputs to its output, reject or separately classify candidates creating an unsupported directed cycle, and resolve overlapping clause claims by retaining only a jointly consistent selection. The output is a circuit fragment \(G\) together with a map from each gate to its defining clauses. Replacing mapped clauses by \(G\) preserves their Boolean relation; unmatched clauses remain as residual CNF constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verify complete gate patterns, orient them into a consistent dependency graph, and retain unmatched clauses as residual CNF constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite propositional CNF formula.
Each accepted gate template has an independently checkable relational encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\equiv \operatorname{Enc}(G)\land F_{\mathrm{res}}\) for a clause-disjoint, equivalence-checked recovery.

notation.meaning: CNF encoding of the recovered fragment

review_flags: Recovery policy for overlaps and cycles is implementation-sensitive and requires a dedicated source.

children.title: Ambiguous-Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Overlapping, incomplete, or noncanonical encodings that limit structural recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous-Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local CNF equivalence need not determine gate orientation, ownership, or a unique circuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Gate recovery is not unique without structural conventions. The CNF \((\neg x\lor z)\land(x\lor\neg z)\) expresses \(x\leftrightarrow z\), so it supports both a buffer with input \(x\) and output \(z\), and a buffer with input \(z\) and output \(x\). Clause truth tables alone cannot select an orientation. More generally, clauses may participate in several overlapping complete templates, and auxiliary variables may have external occurrences inconsistent with exclusive gate ownership. Therefore a recovery procedure may certify the recovered relation but must mark direction and decomposition as ambiguous unless occurrence restrictions, designated outputs, or independent circuit metadata resolve them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CNF relation can admit multiple gate orientations or overlapping decompositions. Semantics alone does not always recover a unique circuit.
assumptions_latex: Recovery observes only CNF clauses unless additional metadata is stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\neg x\lor z)\land(x\lor\neg z)\equiv(x\leftrightarrow z)\), but this equivalence does not distinguish \(x\to z\) from \(z\to x\).

notation.meaning: candidate buffer orientation from x to z

children.title: XOR Constraint Detection
children.top_down_role: Recognition of parity structure represented through CNF clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: XOR Constraint Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection of a parity equation through its complete canonical CNF clause family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\) be distinct Boolean variables and \(b\in\{0,1\}\). For each assignment \(a\in\{0,1\}^k\) with \(a_1\oplus\cdots\oplus a_k\ne b\), define the clause \(D_a:=\bigvee_{i:a_i=0}x_i\lor\bigvee_{i:a_i=1}\neg x_i\), which excludes exactly \(a\). The conjunction of all \(2^{k-1}\) such clauses is equivalent to \(x_1\oplus\cdots\oplus x_k=b\). An exact canonical-pattern detector reports an XOR constraint only when every required clause is present; subsets provide implications but do not certify the parity equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parity equation is exactly the conjunction of clauses excluding every assignment of the wrong parity. Exact detection requires the full family.
assumptions_latex: \(k\ge 1\) and \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\) are distinct Boolean variables.
Detection uses the direct canonical CNF encoding without auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigwedge_{a:\,\bigoplus_i a_i\ne b}D_a\equiv\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^k x_i=b\right)\).
review_flags: Canonical parity encoding is directly checkable, but no SAT/XOR detection source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The canonical parity encoding is correct and fits XOR Constraint Detection, but exact-pattern detection and its completeness boundary have no cited SAT/XOR source.

children.title: Gaussian Elimination
children.top_down_role: Linear-algebraic processing of recovered parity constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row reduction of recovered XOR equations over the binary field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb F_2^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb F_2^m\), form the augmented matrix \([A\mid b]\). For successive columns, choose a row having entry \(1\) as pivot, swap it into the next pivot position, and add that row modulo \(2\) to every other row having entry \(1\) in the pivot column. Stop after all columns are processed. A row \([0\ \cdots\ 0\mid1]\) certifies inconsistency. Otherwise, pivot variables are expressed as affine XORs of free variables, yielding all solutions of \(Ax=b\); rows with a single unassigned pivot also yield immediate Boolean propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduce the binary augmented matrix by swaps and XOR row additions. A zero row with right side one proves inconsistency; otherwise pivots describe all solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are over the field \(\mathbb F_2\).
Row swaps and row additions are the permitted elementary operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([A\mid b]\sim[R\mid c]\), with \(Ax=b\) inconsistent exactly when \([R\mid c]\) contains \([0\mid1]\).

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: XOR Matrix Management

knowledge_statements.title: XOR Matrix Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental maintenance, propagation, and consistency checking of an XOR row system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain recovered XOR constraints as an augmented binary matrix \([A\mid b]\) in row-echelon form, together with maps from variables to columns and constraints to rows. On insertion, reduce the new row by current pivots; discard it if it becomes \([0\mid0]\), report conflict if it becomes \([0\mid1]\), and otherwise install its leading \(1\) as a pivot and eliminate that column from other rows. On a Boolean assignment \(x_j=v\), substitute \(v\) into every incident row and restore echelon form. Emit a propagation when a row has exactly one unassigned variable, and retain row-combination provenance for each conflict or propagated literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep XOR equations in incremental echelon form, update them under insertions and assignments, and derive conflicts or unit-parity propagations with provenance.
assumptions_latex: All XOR equations are represented over \(\mathbb F_2\).
Assignments and inserted rows are processed consistently with the current variable-column map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained matrix has the same solution set as all active XOR constraints and assignments, unless a derived row \([0\mid1]\) certifies inconsistency.

notation.meaning: Boolean assignment substituted into the matrix

children.title: CNF–XOR Integration Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Coordination costs between clause reasoning and algebraic parity reasoning.

assumptions_latex: The CNF formula \(F\) and XOR system \(Ax=b\pmod 2\) use Boolean variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sound integration requires a shared assignment trail and explanation interface; otherwise XOR-derived propagation or conflict learning need not be justified in the CNF proof system.

notation.meaning: Parity equations over the field with two elements

review_flags: integration and proof-logging variants should be checked
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between clausal reasoning and Gaussian elimination over \(\mathbb F_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula and let \(Ax=b\pmod 2\) be a recovered parity subsystem. A sound integrated solver may propagate an XOR-implied literal \(\ell\) only when \(F\land(Ax=b)\models \ell\), and may report an XOR conflict only when the current trail makes \(Ax=b\) inconsistent. Any learned clause \(C\) exported to the CNF engine must satisfy \(F\land(Ax=b)\models C\). Treating parity equations as independent clauses without an equisatisfiable encoding, or exporting unexplained XOR consequences to a clausal certificate, crosses the integration boundary and can invalidate proof checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CNF and XOR engines may exchange only semantically implied consequences with checkable explanations; naive clause treatment or unexplained parity learning can invalidate soundness.
