knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pre-search detection of syntactic CNF symmetries by graph automorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct the colored incidence graph \(G(F)\) with clause vertices, literal or variable vertices, occurrence edges, and colors preserving clause type and literal polarity. Compute generators \(S\) of \(\operatorname{Aut}(G(F))\). Translate each \(\pi\in S\) into a polarity-consistent permutation of literals and retain it only after checking \(\pi(\neg x)=\neg\pi(x)\) and \(\pi(F)=F\). Output the retained generators. Each output permutation maps satisfying assignments of \(F\) to satisfying assignments of \(F\), although the procedure need not find semantic symmetries absent from the chosen graph representation.

The representative-selection predicate is sound for every orbit of admissible search states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-based pruning using symmetries valid at the current search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given generators of \(H_t\), define a canonical representative \(\operatorname{can}_t(s)\in H_t s\) for each admissible state or partial assignment \(s\). During branching or propagation, reject \(s\) when \(s\neq\operatorname{can}_t(s)\), or add a symmetry-breaking constraint excluding precisely the noncanonical portion of its orbit. Apply a constraint only while the symmetries used to derive it remain valid, unless the constraint is globally entailed. Output either a representative branch or a checkable exclusion. Since every orbit retains a representative, satisfiability is preserved.

assumptions_latex: Symmetries are used to prune a SAT search or to add symmetry-breaking constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and lifetime limits of symmetry-based SAT pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At time \(t\), a permutation \(\pi\) is usable only if it preserves the relevant current semantics, namely \(\pi(\operatorname{Mod}(S_t))=\operatorname{Mod}(S_t)\), and respects literal complementation. Clause learning can shrink the syntactic automorphism group, clause deletion can enlarge it, and assumptions can restrict it to a stabilizer. Consequently, a locally justified symmetry-breaking constraint must not survive a state transition unless it is independently entailed by the permanent formula or is guarded by the context that justified it. Violating this lifetime boundary can remove the last representative of a satisfiable orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetries must preserve the current state; locally justified pruning cannot outlive the clauses, assumptions, or context supporting it unless globally entailed.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns an equisatisfiable transformed state and associated reconstruction or proof information after each scheduled invocation.
review_flags: schedule and preservation interfaces vary by solver
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic inprocessing under an explicit search-event schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an initial state \(S_0\), an increasing schedule \(T=\{t_1,t_2,\ldots\}\), an inprocessor \(P\), and budgets \(B_i\). Continue ordinary search until event counter \(t_i\) is reached, suspend search, and apply \(P\) to the current state for at most \(B_i\) units of work. Require the returned state \(S'\) to be equisatisfiable with the suspended state and retain every reconstruction or proof record required by eliminated structure. Resume search from \(S'\); stop when SAT, UNSAT, or an external resource limit is reported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At predetermined search events, pause solving, run a bounded semantics-preserving inprocessor, retain reconstruction or proof data, and resume from the transformed state.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduled Inprocessing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches scheduled inprocessing, but the schedule, preservation, reconstruction, and proof-record interfaces are solver-dependent and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Search-Triggered Inprocessing
children.top_down_role: Inprocessing activated by observed search state or performance signals.

assumptions_latex: The solver exposes measurable search signals \(z_t\) and a trigger predicate \(Q\).
The inprocessor preserves satisfiability and records required reconstruction or proof information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Inprocessing is invoked exactly when the search signal satisfies the trigger and its cooldown and budget conditions.

notation.meaning: Vector of search measurements at event \(t\)

review_flags: trigger semantics and preservation interface need sourcing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive inprocessing initiated by measured search behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a solver state, measurements \(z_t\), trigger predicate \(Q\), cooldown \(d\), budget rule \(B(z_t)\), and inprocessor \(P\). After each monitored search event, update \(z_t\). If \(Q(z_t)\) is false or fewer than \(d\) events have elapsed since the previous invocation, continue search. Otherwise suspend search, apply \(P\) for budget \(B(z_t)\), validate its preservation interface, retain reconstruction or proof records, reset the trigger state, and resume. Terminate when the solver reports SAT, UNSAT, or a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monitor search behavior and invoke bounded inprocessing when a specified signal predicate fires, subject to cooldown, preservation, and reconstruction requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Triggered Inprocessing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits search-triggered inprocessing, but the trigger state, cooldown behavior, preservation validation, and budget interface are presented without an authoritative source.

children.title: Trigger-Signal Families
children.top_down_role: Conflict, propagation, restart, database, and stagnation signals used for activation.

assumptions_latex: At each monitored event \(t\), the solver provides a finite measurement vector \(z_t\).
Thresholds and comparison windows are fixed before each trigger decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A trigger is a Boolean combination of measurable resource, progress, stagnation, structural, or memory predicates.

notation.meaning: A measured signal and its threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicates used to decide when SAT inprocessing begins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_t\) contain monitored quantities such as conflicts since the last invocation, propagation rate, learned-clause growth, memory use, variable count, clause count, restart count, or a stagnation statistic. An admissible trigger has the form \(Q(z_t)=\Phi(q_1(z_t),\ldots,q_m(z_t))\), where \(\Phi\) is a Boolean formula and each atomic predicate is a specified threshold or window comparison, for example \(q_j(z_t)=[z_t^{(j)}\geq\theta_j]\) or \(q_j(z_t)=[z_t^{(j)}-z_{t-w}^{(j)}\leq\theta_j]\). The trigger fires precisely when \(Q(z_t)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trigger signals form explicit Boolean combinations of thresholded resource, progress, stagnation, structural, and memory measurements taken during search.
knowledge_statements.title: Trigger-Signal Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is appropriate, but the proposed signal family is solver-dependent and no source supports it as a recognized SAT-inprocessing taxonomy.

children.title: Inprocessing Interruption Costs
children.top_down_role: Search disruption, state synchronization, and amortization concerns across trigger regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Inprocessing Interruption Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work accounting for pauses caused by SAT inprocessing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one invocation, decompose the work after the pre-invocation phase as \(C_P+C_I+C_{\mathrm{post}}\), where \(C_P\) counts transformation work, \(C_I\) counts interruption and rebuilding work, and \(C_{\mathrm{post}}\) counts subsequent search work. Relative to uninterrupted remaining work \(C_{\mathrm{base}}\), the invocation has nonnegative work savings exactly when \(C_P+C_I+C_{\mathrm{post}}\leq C_{\mathrm{base}}\). For invocations indexed by \(i\), the directly charged transformation and interruption overhead is \(\sum_i(C_{P,i}+C_{I,i})\); an accounting policy that measures interruption cost must include both terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inprocessing is work-saving only when its reduced future search work covers both transformation work and the cost of suspending and rebuilding search state.
assumptions_latex: A search phase without interruption would require remaining work \(C_{\mathrm{base}}\).
An inprocessing call incurs transformation work and may invalidate or require rebuilding search structures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The invocation is work-saving exactly when its transformation, interruption, and subsequent-search work do not exceed the uninterrupted remaining work.

notation.meaning: Remaining search work without the invocation

review_flags: cost decomposition is a formal accounting model
empirical SAT source required for operational interpretation

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Reconstruction Stacks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse model extension after variable-eliminating SAT transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a transformation sequence \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_k\), reconstruction operators \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\), and a model \(M_k\models F_k\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), compute \(M_{i-1}=R_i(M_i)\), restoring eliminated variables or overwritten assignments while preserving assignments already fixed outside the step's reconstruction scope. Each operator must satisfy \(M_i\models F_i\Rightarrow R_i(M_i)\models F_{i-1}\). Output \(M_0\). The stack order is necessarily the reverse of transformation order; applying records forward need not produce a model of \(F_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store a model-extension record for every simplification, then apply records in reverse order to lift a final model back to the original variables.
assumptions_latex: Each simplification step maps a formula \(F_{i-1}\) to an equisatisfiable formula \(F_i\).
Each step emits a reconstruction record sufficient to extend any model of \(F_i\) to a model of \(F_{i-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reverse application of the records reconstructs a model of the original formula from any model of the final simplified formula.

notation.meaning: Partial model after reconstruction through step \(i\)

review_flags: individual transformation records need formal specifications

assumptions_latex: An incremental SAT interface solves a permanent formula under changing assumptions or clause additions.
A preprocessing transformation may eliminate variables, delete clauses, or introduce reconstruction dependencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transformation is reusable across calls only if future updates can be translated consistently and prior semantic, model, and proof interfaces remain valid.

notation.meaning: Preprocessing transformation and its update translation

review_flags: incremental interface variants require separate treatment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifetime boundary for preprocessing across incremental SAT calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose call \(t\) asks whether \(F_t\land A_t\) is satisfiable and preprocessing produces \(P(F_t)\). Reusing this state after an update \(\Delta_t\) is sound only when an update translation \(U_P(\Delta_t)\) is defined and \(P(F_t\land\Delta_t)\) is equisatisfiable with \(P(F_t)\land U_P(\Delta_t)\), with compatible model reconstruction and proof logging. Variable elimination based on clauses later removed, or assumptions later changed, generally lacks this property. Such transformations must be frozen, guarded, undone, or recomputed before the affected incremental call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preprocessing may persist across incremental calls only when later clauses and assumptions translate coherently and model reconstruction and proof obligations remain valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental-Preprocessing Tension

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the proposed update-translation equivalence, reconstruction obligations, and claims about clause removal and changing assumptions depend on the incremental interface and preprocessing method. No supporting source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Logging Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility for certifying unsatisfiability after a SAT-preserving formula transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) transform a CNF formula \(F\) into \(F'=T(F)\), while emitting a trace \(\lambda\). For a proof system \(P\), the transformation is proof-logging compatible if there is a polynomial-time reconstruction map \(R\) such that, for every \(P\)-refutation \(\pi'\) of \(F'\), \(R(F,F',\lambda,\pi')\) is a valid \(P\)-refutation of \(F\). Moreover, both \(\lambda\) and the reconstructed refutation must be checkable without rerunning the transformation, and their combined size must be polynomial in \(|F|+|\lambda|+|\pi'|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformation is proof-logging compatible when its trace lets a polynomial-time checker reconstruct and verify an original-formula refutation from every transformed-formula refutation.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(T(F)\) are CNF formulas.
\(P\) has a polynomial-time proof checker.
\(T\) preserves unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(F,T(F),\lambda,\pi')\) is a polynomially reconstructible, checkable \(P\)-refutation of \(F\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the proof-logging leaf, but the polynomial reconstruction and size requirements are a strong, proof-system-dependent formalization. No cited source supports this exact compatibility standard.

children.title: Simplification-Induced Search Hardness
children.top_down_role: Cases where formula reduction produces less favorable solver search behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplification-Induced Search Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative hardness for a fixed randomized SAT search algorithm and transformed formula family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a randomized search algorithm \(A\), a satisfiable CNF family \((F_n)_{n\geq 1}\), and satisfiability-preserving transformations \(T_n\). Let \(H_A(G)\) be the expected number of search steps until \(A\) finds a satisfying assignment of \(G\), with \(H_A(G)=\infty\) when the hitting probability is less than one. The transformations induce search hardness for \(A\) on \((F_n)\) when \(H_A(T_n(F_n))/H_A(F_n)\) is superpolynomial in \(|F_n|\) along an infinite subsequence, despite \(|T_n(F_n)|\) being polynomial in \(|F_n|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplification induces search hardness when it causes a superpolynomial increase in a fixed algorithm’s expected solution time while keeping representation size polynomial.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and its initialization distribution are fixed across the family.
\(F_n\) and \(T_n(F_n)\) are satisfiable.
\(|T_n(F_n)|\leq \operatorname{poly}(|F_n|)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_A(T_n(F_n))/H_A(F_n)\) grows superpolynomially along infinitely many \(n\).

notation.meaning: expected search steps of algorithm A on formula G

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm-relative definition is plausible, but no source establishes this terminology or threshold. Satisfiability alone does not ensure finite positive H_A(F_n), so the displayed ratio can be undefined.

children.title: Simplification-Induced Proof Hardness
children.top_down_role: Cases where transformed formulas or traces become harder to certify or check.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplification-Induced Proof Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative refutation-size hardness under a fixed propositional proof system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a proof system \(P\), an unsatisfiable CNF family \((F_n)_{n\geq 1}\), and unsatisfiability-preserving transformations \(T_n\). Let \(L_P(G)\) denote the minimum symbol length of a \(P\)-refutation of \(G\), with \(L_P(G)=\infty\) if none exists. The transformations induce proof hardness in \(P\) when \(L_P(T_n(F_n))/L_P(F_n)\) is superpolynomial in \(|F_n|\) along an infinite subsequence, while \(|T_n(F_n)|\) remains polynomial in \(|F_n|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simplification induces proof hardness when shortest refutations become superpolynomially longer in a fixed proof system although transformed formulas remain polynomially sized.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is fixed for the entire family.
\(F_n\) and \(T_n(F_n)\) are unsatisfiable.
\(|T_n(F_n)|\leq \operatorname{poly}(|F_n|)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_P(T_n(F_n))/L_P(F_n)\) grows superpolynomially along infinitely many \(n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the proof-hardness leaf, but the proposed ratio-based definition is uncited. Its reliability also depends on the fixed proof system, encoding-based length measure, and existence of refutations.

children.title: Structural Information Loss
children.top_down_role: Loss of exploitable syntactic or semantic organization during simplification.

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Information Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irrecoverability of an original structural feature from a simplified SAT representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\) be a formula transformation and let \(s:\mathcal F\to\mathcal S\) record a structural feature, such as variable incidence, clause ancestry, or model correspondence. Structural information about \(s\) is lost by \(T\) precisely when \(s\) is not constant on a fiber of \(T\): there exist \(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal F\) with \(T(F_1)=T(F_2)\) but \(s(F_1)\neq s(F_2)\). Equivalently, no decoder \(D:\mathcal G\to\mathcal S\) can satisfy \(D(T(F))=s(F)\) for every \(F\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformation loses a structural feature when two formulas with different feature values have the same transformed representation, making universal decoding impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and the feature map \(s\) are defined on the same formula class \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists D:\mathcal G\to\mathcal S\;\forall F\in\mathcal F,\ D(T(F))=s(F)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fiber criterion and decoder equivalence are mathematically coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no source connects this information-theoretic formalization to structural loss under SAT simplification.

children.title: Hardness Tradeoff Regimes
children.top_down_role: Formula-size reductions that exchange preprocessing gains for downstream difficulty.

knowledge_statements.title: Hardness Tradeoff Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto regimes balancing transformed size, search cost, and proof cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a formula \(F\), transformation \(T\), search procedure \(A\), and proof system \(P\), define the cost vector \(c(T;F)=(|T(F)|,H_A(T(F)),L_P(T(F)))\), restricting the third coordinate to unsatisfiable instances and the second to satisfiable instances or corresponding benchmark subfamilies. A transformation regime \(\mathcal R\) is a hardness-tradeoff regime when its attainable cost vectors contain incomparable pairs under componentwise order. A transformation \(T\in\mathcal R\) is Pareto efficient if no \(U\in\mathcal R\) has \(c(U;F)\leq c(T;F)\) componentwise with at least one strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hardness-tradeoff regime contains transformations whose representation size, search cost, and proof cost cannot all be improved simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(P\), the instance family, and all cost conventions are fixed.
Only defined cost coordinates are compared on each satisfiability class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pareto-efficient transformations form the nondominated boundary of \(\{c(T;F):T\in\mathcal R\}\).

notation.meaning: size, search, and proof cost vector

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits a tradeoff-regime leaf, but it combines search and proof costs that are defined on different satisfiability classes. A precise family-level benchmark convention and a source for this Pareto formalization are required.

children.title: Stochastic SAT Local Search
children.top_down_role: Incomplete assignment-space search, scoring, memory, diversification, and characteristic failure regimes. Randomized algorithms retaining exact completeness guarantees are placed under complete solving.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapter 6: Incomplete Algorithms; Chapter 10: Random Satisfiability

knowledge_statements.title: GSAT Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy single-variable-flip local search with random tie-breaking and optional restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a CNF formula \(F\), a flip budget \(B\), and a restart budget \(R\). For each restart, sample an assignment \(a\). At every step, compute \(\Delta_a(x)=u(a)-u(a\oplus x)\) for every variable \(x\), where \(u(a)\) is the number of clauses falsified by \(a\). If \(u(a)=0\), return \(a\). Otherwise choose uniformly among variables maximizing \(\Delta_a(x)\), set \(a\leftarrow a\oplus x\), and continue until \(B\) flips have occurred. After \(R\) unsuccessful restarts, return failure together with the best assignment encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GSAT repeatedly flips a variable giving the greatest reduction in unsatisfied clauses, using random tie-breaking and restarting after a fixed budget.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(B,R\in\mathbb N\) are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a satisfying assignment of \(F\) or failure with a minimum-\(u\) assignment encountered.

notation.meaning: number of clauses falsified by assignment a
assignment obtained by flipping variable x
decrease in falsified-clause count after flipping x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and greedy maximum-gain rule fit GSAT, but restarts, initialization, tie-breaking, sideways moves, and returned best assignment vary across the family. An original or authoritative GSAT citation with a precise locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: WalkSAT Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Focused stochastic clause repair using noise-controlled random or minimum-break flips.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a CNF formula \(F\), noise \(p\in[0,1]\), flip budget \(B\), and restart budget \(R\). Initialize each restart with a sampled assignment \(a\). If \(a\) satisfies \(F\), return \(a\). Otherwise choose uniformly a clause \(C\) falsified by \(a\). With probability \(p\), choose a uniformly random variable of \(C\); with probability \(1-p\), choose uniformly among variables of \(C\) minimizing \(\operatorname{break}_a(x)\). Flip the chosen variable and repeat for at most \(B\) flips. Return failure after \(R\) unsuccessful restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: WalkSAT selects an unsatisfied clause, then flips either a random clause variable or one minimizing newly broken clauses, according to a noise probability.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula with no empty clause.
\(p\in[0,1]\) and \(B,R\in\mathbb N\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a satisfying assignment if one is reached within the budgets, and failure otherwise.

notation.meaning: number of currently satisfied clauses falsified by flipping x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The focused random/minimum-break procedure is WalkSAT-like, but canonical variants differ, notably in zero-break priority and noise semantics. A source is needed to identify and support the exact variant stated.

children.title: Novelty Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Local-search choices balancing score quality against recent variable use.

knowledge_statements.title: Novelty Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-focused Novelty rule using score rank, variable age, and noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a CNF formula \(F\), noise \(p\in[0,1]\), and a flip budget \(B\). Start from an assignment \(a
eq\models F\) with flip timestamps. At each step choose a falsified clause \(C\), rank its variables by decreasing score \(\Delta_a(x)=u(a)-u(a\oplus x)\), breaking score ties by greater age. Let \(x_1,x_2\) be the first two ranked variables, or set \(x_2=x_1\) when \(|C|=1\). If \(x_1\) is the most recently flipped variable in \(C\), flip \(x_2\) with probability \(p\) and \(x_1\) otherwise; if not, flip \(x_1\). Stop upon satisfaction or after \(B\) flips.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Novelty usually flips the best-scoring variable in an unsatisfied clause but may choose the second best when the best was changed most recently.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Each variable has a maintained last-flip timestamp.
\(p\in[0,1]\) and \(B\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a satisfying assignment if reached within \(B\) flips, and failure otherwise.

notation.meaning: number of clauses falsified by assignment a
score improvement caused by flipping x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits, but the exact Novelty rule depends on score direction, age tie-breaking, clause selection, and noise convention. These choices require a specifically located authoritative source.

children.title: Adaptive-Novelty Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Novelty variants with dynamically adjusted selection behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Novelty Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Novelty search with feedback adaptation of its noise probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run a Novelty heuristic with a time-dependent noise parameter \(p_t\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\). Let \(b_t=\min_{0\leq s\leq t}u(a_s)\), and let \(q_t\) count consecutive flips without decreasing \(b_t\). Given threshold \(L\) and increments \(\eta_+,\eta_->0\), update after flip \(t\) by \(p_{t+1}=\min\{p_{\max},p_t+\eta_+\}\) when \(q_t\geq L\), by \(p_{t+1}=\max\{p_{\min},p_t-\eta_-\}\) when \(b_t<b_{t-1}\), and by \(p_{t+1}=p_t\) otherwise. Use \(p_{t+1}\) in the next Novelty choice; stop at satisfaction or the flip budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive Novelty raises noise during prolonged nonimprovement and lowers it after finding a better assignment, while retaining the underlying Novelty rule.
assumptions_latex: \(0\leq p_{\min}\leq p_0\leq p_{\max}\leq1\).
\(L\in\mathbb N\) and \(\eta_+,\eta_->0\).
A finite flip budget is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every noise value satisfies \(p_t\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\), and the output follows the stated satisfaction-or-budget rule.

notation.meaning: best falsified-clause count seen through flip t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a generic bounded feedback controller rather than an established Adaptive Novelty algorithm as stated. A canonical source is required to determine the correct update formula, trigger schedule, and parameter semantics.

children.title: Novelty Noise Regimes
children.top_down_role: Fixed, reactive, and state-dependent noise configurations.

knowledge_statements.title: Novelty Noise Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavioral partition induced by the Novelty second-choice probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Novelty transition rule with noise \(p\), three regimes are distinguished. If \(p=0\), the highest-ranked variable is always chosen, so the rule is deterministic once clause selection and tie-breaking are fixed. If \(0<p<1\), both the highest-ranked and, when the recency condition holds, second-ranked moves have positive probability. If \(p=1\), the second-ranked variable is always selected whenever the highest-ranked variable is the clause's most recently flipped variable. Thus only the interior regime assigns positive probability to both competing recency-conditioned moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Novelty noise separates deterministic best-choice, mixed, and forced second-choice behavior; only interior noise permits both alternatives when recency activates the rule.
assumptions_latex: The clause-selection and ranking conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<p<1\) holds exactly when both recency-conditioned choices have positive probability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The endpoint/interior probability partition follows from the stated Novelty variant, and property is the correct kind. Because that underlying noise convention is uncited and variant-dependent, the claim needs source confirmation.

children.title: Novelty Stagnation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cycling, overdiversification, and weak-adaptation regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Novelty Stagnation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed non-solution classes and deterministic cycles that prevent Novelty from reaching satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_p\) be the transition kernel of a fixed Novelty variant on assignments augmented by its recency state. A set \(S\) is a stagnation class when it contains no satisfying state and is closed: \(K_p(z,S)=1\) for every \(z\in S\). From any initial state in \(S\), the probability of reaching a satisfying assignment is zero. In particular, at \(p=0\), any repeated augmented state on a deterministic trajectory begins a cycle; if that cycle contains no satisfying assignment, the search stagnates indefinitely unless a restart or perturbation changes the state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Novelty stagnates when its augmented-state process enters a closed set without a solution; at zero noise, a repeated state creates a permanent unsatisfying cycle.
assumptions_latex: The formula, clause-selection rule, tie-breaking rule, and recency update are fixed.
The augmented state space is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_0\in S\) implies \(\Pr_{z_0}(\tau_{\mathrm{sat}}<\infty)=0\).

notation.meaning: Novelty transition kernel at noise p
first hitting time of a satisfying state

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed-class implication is mathematically standard and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but its application to Novelty requires a source and a fully specified augmented state and deterministic selection rules for the zero-noise cycle claim.

children.title: Focused Local Search
children.top_down_role: Flip selection restricted to variables associated with currently unsatisfied clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Focused Local Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local SAT search restricting every candidate flip to an unsatisfied clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite CNF formula \(F\), an initial assignment \(a_0\), a distribution \(Q_a\) over clauses falsified by \(a\), a variable-selection kernel \(P_a(\cdot\mid C)\) supported on variables of \(C\), and a budget \(B\). For \(t=0,\ldots,B-1\), return \(a_t\) if it satisfies \(F\); otherwise sample \(C_t\sim Q_{a_t}\), sample \(x_t\sim P_{a_t}(\cdot\mid C_t)\), and set \(a_{t+1}=a_t\oplus x_t\). Return failure if no satisfying assignment has appeared by time \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Focused local search always chooses a currently unsatisfied clause and flips one of its variables according to a specified selection kernel.
assumptions_latex: Every nonsatisfying assignment falsifies at least one nonempty clause.
\(Q_a\) and \(P_a(\cdot\mid C)\) are probability distributions.
\(B\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every performed flip satisfies \(x_t\in\operatorname{var}(C_t)\) for a clause \(C_t\) falsified by \(a_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The kernel formulation captures focused local search, but no authoritative source supports this exact abstraction. The pseudocode also returns failure without testing the assignment produced by the B-th flip, despite saying satisfaction through time B should succeed.

children.title: Random-Walk Local Search
children.top_down_role: Randomized movement through assignment space for diversification.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Walk Local Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure focused random walk for CNF satisfiability with a finite stopping budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula \(F\), an assignment \(a_0\), and a step budget \(T\), repeat for \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\): if \(a_t\models F\), return \(a_t\); otherwise choose a clause \(C_t\) uniformly from the clauses falsified by \(a_t\), choose a variable \(x_t\) uniformly from \(\operatorname{Var}(C_t)\), and obtain \(a_{t+1}\) by complementing only \(a_t(x_t)\). If no satisfying assignment has been reached after \(T\) flips, return the final assignment together with failure-to-find status; this status does not certify unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose a currently false clause and randomly flip one of its variables, stopping at a satisfying assignment or a prescribed flip limit.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(T\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_t\models F\) is a valid SAT witness whenever the algorithm returns success.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical focused random-walk SAT procedure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role and focused random-walk statement fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the precise clause-selection, variable-selection, or stopping conventions.

children.title: Focus-Selection Variants
children.top_down_role: Clause-focused and variable-focused candidate-selection regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Focus-Selection Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability laws for selecting the falsified clause on which a focused flip operates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For assignment \(a_t\), let \(U_t\) be the set of clauses falsified by \(a_t\). A focus-selection rule is a probability distribution \(q_t\) supported on \(U_t\). The weighted family has \[q_t(C)=\frac{r_t(C)}{\sum_{D\in U_t}r_t(D)},\qquad C\in U_t,\] where \(r_t(C)>0\). Uniform focus uses \(r_t(C)=1\); clause-weight focus uses \(r_t(C)=w_t(C)\); age-biased focus uses \(r_t(C)=g(A_t(C))\) for positive \(g\). After drawing \(C_t\sim q_t\), the flip variable must be selected from \(\operatorname{Var}(C_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Focused variants differ through a probability distribution over currently false clauses, including uniform, clause-weighted, and age-biased selection.
assumptions_latex: \(U_t\neq\varnothing\).
\(r_t(C)>0\) for every \(C\in U_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{C\in U_t}q_t(C)=1\) and \(q_t(C)=0\) for \(C\notin U_t\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized priority representation of focused selection
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but the asserted weighted and age-biased families need variant-specific support; in particular, the clause-age quantity A_t(C) is not defined.

children.title: Randomization Balance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Exploration versus score-guided exploitation across randomized variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomization Balance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixture parameter separating greedy, randomized, and pure-walk focused flips.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a falsified clause \(C\), a flip score \(s_t(x)\) for \(x\in\operatorname{Var}(C)\), and \(p\in[0,1]\). Let \(G_t(C)=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\operatorname{Var}(C)}s_t(x)\). The balanced selection law is \[P_t(x\mid C)=\frac{p}{|\operatorname{Var}(C)|}+(1-p)\frac{\mathbf{1}\{x\in G_t(C)\}}{|G_t(C)|}.\] The regime \(p=0\) is purely score-greedy with uniform tie-breaking, \(0<p<1\) mixes exploration and exploitation, and \(p=1\) is a pure random walk within the focused clause.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixture parameter interpolates between greedy best-score flips and uniform random flips within the selected false clause.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty.
\(s_t(x)\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{Var}(C)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_t(\cdot\mid C)\) is a probability distribution on \(\operatorname{Var}(C)\).

notation.meaning: best-scoring variables in the focused clause

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits a balance-regime leaf and the mixture law is mathematically normalized, but its exact parameterization and interpretation are solver-dependent and uncited.

children.title: Make Scores
children.top_down_role: Candidate-flip benefit measured through newly satisfied clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Make Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-count make score for a single-variable flip under a fixed assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite CNF formula, let \(a\) be an assignment, and let \(a^{\oplus x}\) denote the assignment obtained by complementing variable \(x\). The make score of \(x\) at \(a\) is \[\operatorname{make}_a(x)=\bigl|\{C\in F: a\not\models C\ \text{and}\ a^{\oplus x}\models C\}\bigr|.\] Thus it counts exactly the clauses that are falsified before the flip and satisfied afterward; clauses whose truth value does not change and clauses already satisfied before the flip contribute zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The make score counts false clauses that become true when the selected variable is flipped.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(a\) is a total Boolean assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\operatorname{make}_a(x)\leq |F|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard SAT local-search make count
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise, matches the make-score leaf, and agrees with the plain statement, but it has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Break Scores
children.top_down_role: Candidate-flip cost measured through newly unsatisfied clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Break Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-count break score for a single-variable flip under a fixed assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a finite CNF formula, let \(a\) be an assignment, and let \(a^{\oplus x}\) denote the assignment obtained by complementing variable \(x\). The break score of \(x\) at \(a\) is \[\operatorname{break}_a(x)=\bigl|\{C\in F: a\models C\ \text{and}\ a^{\oplus x}\not\models C\}\bigr|.\] It counts exactly the clauses destroyed by the flip. In particular, only clauses for which the literal of \(x\) is the unique currently true literal can contribute to this score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The break score counts true clauses that become false when the selected variable is flipped.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(a\) is a total Boolean assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq\operatorname{break}_a(x)\leq |F|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard SAT local-search break count
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise, matches the break-score leaf, and agrees with the plain statement, but it has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Variable-Age Scores
children.top_down_role: Recency-based signals used to distinguish otherwise similar flip candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Age Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recency score determined by the number of iterations since a variable was last flipped.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let \(\ell_t(x)\leq t\) be the most recent iteration at which variable \(x\) was flipped, with \(\ell_t(x)=0\) when \(x\) has not previously been flipped. The variable age is \[A_t(x)=t-\ell_t(x).\] An age score is any specified monotone transformation \(s_t^{\mathrm{age}}(x)=\phi(A_t(x))\). With increasing \(\phi\), larger scores favor variables not flipped recently; with decreasing \(\phi\), larger scores favor recently flipped variables. The direction of preference must therefore accompany the score definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable age is elapsed iterations since the last flip; a monotone transformation turns this recency information into a selection score.
assumptions_latex: \(t\in\mathbb{N}\).
\(0\leq\ell_t(x)\leq t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_t(x)\in\mathbb{N}_0\).

notation.meaning: age of x at iteration t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elapsed-time definition of variable age
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the last-flip indexing and initialization convention are not universal and require a cited source; assigning zero both to never-flipped variables and flips at iteration zero also needs clarification.

children.title: Composite Flip Scores
children.top_down_role: Combined use of satisfaction gain, disruption cost, and recency signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Flip Scores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear composite of clause gain, clause loss, and variable-age signals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a variable \(x\) under assignment \(a_t\), a linear composite flip score is \[S_t(x)=\alpha\operatorname{make}_{a_t}(x)-\beta\operatorname{break}_{a_t}(x)+\gamma\phi(A_t(x)),\] where \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\), \(\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\phi\) is a declared age normalization. A maximizing rule selects an admissible variable from \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_x S_t(x)\), with an explicit tie-breaking law. The coefficients determine the tradeoff between satisfying false clauses, preserving true clauses, and applying a recency preference; rescaling all coefficients by the same positive constant leaves the maximizers unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite flip score combines newly satisfied clauses, newly falsified clauses, and an age term with declared coefficients and tie-breaking.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\).
\(\phi(A_t(x))\in\mathbb{R}\) for each candidate variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_x S_t(x)\) defines the best-scoring admissible flips.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional weighted synthesis of local-search signals
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is suitable for this leaf, but the particular linear synthesis of make, break, and age signals is presented as conventional without a supporting source or a specified admissible-variable domain.

children.title: Configuration Checking
children.top_down_role: Eligibility control based on changes in a variable's local configuration.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Checking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step neighborhood-change memory used to suppress immediate cycling in SAT local search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N(x)\) be the variables sharing a clause with \(x\). Initialize \(c_0(x)=1\) for every variable. At iteration \(t\), a variable \(x\) is configuration-eligible only if \(c_t(x)=1\), subject to any separately declared aspiration rule. After flipping \(x_t\), set \(c_{t+1}(x_t)=0\), set \(c_{t+1}(y)=1\) for every \(y\in N(x_t)\), and leave all other flags unchanged. Consequently, a previously flipped variable becomes ordinarily eligible again only after the assignment of at least one neighboring variable has changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flipped variable is disabled until some clause-sharing neighbor changes, reducing immediate returns to the same local configuration.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
\(N(x)\) is the open neighborhood of \(x\) in the primal graph of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_t(x)=0\) excludes \(x\) from ordinary selection at iteration \(t\).

notation.meaning: variables sharing a clause with x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but configuration checking has multiple published update and aspiration variants. A specialized citation is needed to validate this exact flag initialization and neighborhood-update rule.

children.title: Tabu Memory
children.top_down_role: Temporary restrictions based on recent flips or search states.

knowledge_statements.title: Tabu Memory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tenure prohibition on recently flipped variables, with an optional incumbent-improvement aspiration rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), assign each variable \(x\) a positive integer tabu tenure \(\tau_x\) and last-flip time \(\ell_t(x)\). The tabu predicate is \[T_t(x)=\mathbf{1}\{t-\ell_t(x)<\tau_x\}.\] Ordinarily, \(x\) is admissible exactly when \(T_t(x)=0\). Under incumbent aspiration, a tabu variable is also admissible when flipping it produces an assignment whose number of falsified clauses is strictly smaller than the best number previously observed. Thus tabu memory prevents short-term reversal without making the prohibition absolute when the declared aspiration condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable remains forbidden for a fixed tenure after being flipped, unless an explicit aspiration test overrides the prohibition.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_x\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\).
\(0\leq\ell_t(x)\leq t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is admissible if and only if \(T_t(x)=0\) or the aspiration predicate holds.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-tenure tabu predicate with aspiration
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the strict tenure inequality, last-flip initialization, and incumbent aspiration rule are convention-dependent and uncited.

children.title: Memory-Horizon Regimes
children.top_down_role: Short, long, fixed, and adaptive memory-duration choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Horizon Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by the amount of search history on which the next-flip law depends.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_t\) denote the complete observable search state at iteration \(t\). A local-search controller has horizon \(H\in\mathbb{N}_0\) when its next-flip distribution can be written as \[\Pr(x_t=x\mid z_0,\ldots,z_t)=K_H(x\mid z_{\max\{0,t-H\}},\ldots,z_t).\] The regime \(H=0\) is memoryless relative to \(z_t\); fixed \(0<H<\infty\) is bounded short-term memory; a horizon growing with \(t\) is expanding memory; and dependence that cannot be bounded uniformly in \(t\) is unbounded-history memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Memory regimes are classified by whether decisions use only the current state, a fixed recent window, a growing window, or unbounded history.
assumptions_latex: \((z_t)_{t\geq0}\) is the observable search-state sequence.
\(K_H\) is a probability kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\) bounds the number of preceding state transitions that may affect the next-flip law.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed regime classification is uncited and not evidently standard SAT terminology. Moreover, calling z_t the complete observable state may allow it to encode prior history, undermining the intended horizon distinction unless the state representation is constrained.

children.title: Memory-Induced Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Overrestriction, cycling, and delayed revisitation caused by memory policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Induced Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deadlock boundary for a focused search whose memory filter admits no repair variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let \(U_t\) be the falsified clauses and let \(E_t\) be the variables admitted by the memory rule. Define the available focused moves by \[M_t=E_t\cap\bigcup_{C\in U_t}\operatorname{Var}(C).\] If \(U_t\neq\varnothing\) but \(M_t=\varnothing\), every variable capable of participating in a focused repair is excluded, so a focused algorithm requiring its next flip to lie in \(M_t\) cannot advance. This is memory-induced stagnation. It is avoided only by changing the memory state, applying aspiration, permitting a nonfocused move, restarting, or terminating without a SAT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search deadlocks when the formula remains unsatisfied but memory excludes every variable occurring in every currently false clause.
assumptions_latex: \(U_t\neq\varnothing\).
The algorithm permits only focused flips satisfying the memory filter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_t=\varnothing\) implies that no permitted focused flip exists at iteration \(t\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is correct and the set-theoretic deadlock implication is precise, but no inspectable source establishes this terminology or its intended SAT-local-search scope.

children.title: Clause Weighting
children.top_down_role: Weight-based prioritization of persistently unsatisfied clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Clause Weighting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive weighted-unsatisfaction objective that emphasizes persistently falsified clauses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(w_0(C)=1\) for every clause \(C\) of a CNF formula \(F\), and define \(L_t(a)=\sum_{C\in F}w_t(C)\mathbf{1}\{a\not\models C\}\). At iteration \(t\), select an admissible flip using the decrease \(L_t(a_t)-L_t(a_t^{\oplus x})\), with a declared random tie or diversification rule. After the flip, if the prescribed weight-update condition holds, choose \(\delta>0\) and set \[w_{t+1}(C)=w_t(C)+\delta\mathbf{1}\{a_{t+1}\not\models C\};\] otherwise retain \(w_{t+1}(C)=w_t(C)\). Stop upon satisfaction or at the external search limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause weighting minimizes weighted unsatisfaction and raises the weights of clauses that remain false when an update is triggered.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
The update-trigger and tie-breaking rules are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_t(C)>0\) for all \(t\) and \(C\), and persistently falsified clauses can acquire greater selection influence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical additive clause-weight adaptation template
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the clause-weighting leaf, but the update trigger, admissible-flip rule, and diversification mechanism are left as placeholders, while published clause-weighting algorithms use materially different conventions. A specialized source is required.

children.title: Weight Smoothing
children.top_down_role: Reduction or redistribution of accumulated clause weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weight Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generic affine smoothing step for dynamically weighted SAT local search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a CNF formula have clause set \(\mathcal C\), positive clause weights \(w_C\), baseline weights \(b_C>0\), and smoothing factor \(\rho\in[0,1]\). When a prescribed smoothing trigger fires, update every clause by \[w_C^{+}=\rho w_C+(1-\rho)b_C,\qquad C\in\mathcal C.\] Between smoothing events, retain the current weights and apply the chosen clause-weight increment rule. The smoothing step outputs \(w^{+}\); it preserves positivity and contracts every deviation from baseline according to \(w_C^{+}-b_C=\rho(w_C-b_C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a smoothing event, replace each clause weight by a convex combination of its current and baseline weights, contracting deviations by the smoothing factor.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is finite and \(b_C>0\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C\).
\(0\leq\rho\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_C^{+}>0\) and \(w_C^{+}-b_C=\rho(w_C-b_C)\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C\).

notation.meaning: positive baseline weight of clause C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is internally consistent and fits the leaf, but affine baseline smoothing is only one clause-weight smoothing convention. No cited evidence establishes it as the intended SAT operation.

children.title: Weight–Smoothing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavioral regimes determined by the balance between accumulation pressure and smoothing.

knowledge_statements.title: Weight–Smoothing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regime classification for affine smoothing by its retention parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the smoothing map \(S_\rho(w)=\rho w+(1-\rho)b\) with \(\rho\in[0,1]\), the parameter space separates into three exact regimes: \(\rho=1\) gives no smoothing, \(0<\rho<1\) gives partial smoothing, and \(\rho=0\) gives complete reset to baseline. After \(k\) consecutive smoothing events without intervening weight increments, \[S_\rho^{k}(w)=b+\rho^{k}(w-b).\] Thus partial smoothing retains geometrically decaying weight memory, whereas the two boundary regimes respectively preserve all memory or erase it immediately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retention one preserves weights, retention zero resets them, and intermediate retention makes deviations from baseline decay geometrically across smoothing events.
assumptions_latex: \(w,b\in(0,\infty)^{|\mathcal C|}\).
\(\rho\in[0,1]\) is fixed across the stated smoothing events.
review_flags: classification is tied to the affine smoothing convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regime classification follows mathematically from the stated affine map and representation is an appropriate kind, but the map and regime terminology are unsupported and convention-dependent.

children.title: Adaptive Noise Control
children.top_down_role: Dynamic adjustment of stochastic search noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Noise Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback control of the random-move probability in stochastic SAT local search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix bounds \(0\leq p_{\min}<p_{\max}\leq1\), step sizes \(\eta_+,\eta_->0\), and a stagnation indicator \(s_t\in\{0,1\}\). At iteration \(t\), select a random admissible move with probability \(p_t\) and the heuristic move otherwise. After observing feedback, update \[p_{t+1}=\begin{cases}\min\{p_{\max},p_t+\eta_+\},&s_t=1,\\ \max\{p_{\min},p_t-\eta_-\},&s_t=0.\end{cases}\] The output is the next noise level \(p_{t+1}\), which always remains within the prescribed probability interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the probability of a random move during stagnation and decrease it during progress, always clipping it to a valid interval.
assumptions_latex: \(s_t\) is computed only from information available through iteration \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_t\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\) for every \(t\geq0\).
review_flags: adaptive-noise variants differ in feedback and update rules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clipped update is well-defined and preserves the interval, but it is one invented adaptive-noise policy among materially different SAT variants. A source must fix the feedback and update rule.

children.title: Parameter-Control Policies
children.top_down_role: Online control of local-search parameters beyond noise alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Control Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-adapted policies for controlling stochastic local-search parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\) be the search history through iteration \(t\), and let \(\Theta\) be the admissible parameter space. A parameter-control policy is a sequence of maps \(\pi_t:H_t\mapsto\theta_t\in\Theta\) such that \(\theta_t\) depends only on information observed no later than iteration \(t\). A deterministic policy assigns one parameter vector to each history; a randomized policy assigns a probability distribution \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid H_t)\) on \(\Theta\). The controlled local-search transition at iteration \(t\) uses the selected \(\theta_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter-control policy maps the observed search history to an admissible deterministic or randomized parameter choice used by the next transition.
assumptions_latex: \(H_t\) contains only observations available through iteration \(t\).
\(\Theta\) is the specified admissible parameter set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_t=\pi_t(H_t)\in\Theta\), or \(\theta_t\sim\pi_t(\cdot\mid H_t)\) in the randomized case.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The history-adapted policy definition is coherent and the content kind fits, but no SAT-specific source supports this formal interpretation of the terminal container.

children.title: Adaptation Feedback Signals
children.top_down_role: Search-state indicators used to guide adaptive control.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation Feedback Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable progress and stagnation signals for adaptive SAT control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(x)\) be the number or total weight of clauses falsified by assignment \(x\), and fix a window length \(L\geq1\). A feedback vector available at iteration \(t\) may be represented by \[z_t=\bigl(E(x_t),\ E(x_t)-E(x_{t-1}),\ \min_{t-L\leq j<t}E(x_j)-E(x_t),\ a_t\bigr),\] where \(a_t\) is the number of iterations since the most recent strict improvement of the incumbent objective. Each component is computable from the observed trajectory and may serve as input to a history-adapted parameter-control policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feedback can combine current violation cost, one-step change, windowed improvement, and time since the last incumbent improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(E(x)\) is defined for every Boolean assignment \(x\).
The required assignments and incumbent values are retained in the search history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_t\) is determined by the search history through iteration \(t\).

notation.meaning: iterations since the last strict incumbent improvement

review_flags: feedback vector is a generic formalization
canonical SAT feedback signals require sourcing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed feedback vector is computable from retained history, but its components are an uncited illustrative selection rather than an established representation of SAT adaptation signals.

children.title: Random-Restart Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for abandoning the current trajectory and initiating a fresh search.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Restart Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart scheduling and assignment resampling for stochastic SAT local search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a CNF formula on \(n\) variables, a sequence of positive run budgets \((B_r)_{r\geq1}\), and restart distributions \((\mu_r)_{r\geq1}\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), initialize run \(r\) with \(x_{r,0}\sim\mu_r\). Apply the prescribed local-search transition for at most \(B_r\) moves. Stop and output \(x_{r,t}\) immediately if it satisfies every clause; otherwise discard the active trajectory after move \(B_r\), increment \(r\), and sample a new initial assignment. If no satisfying assignment is found, the policy continues through its specified restart schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run local search for a scheduled budget, return any satisfying assignment, and otherwise resample an initial assignment for the next run.
assumptions_latex: \(B_r\in\mathbb N_{>0}\) for every run \(r\).
Each \(\mu_r\) is a probability distribution on \(\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs a satisfying assignment when one is encountered; otherwise it advances to run \(r+1\).

notation.meaning: assignment at move t of run r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restart algorithm is coherent and matches the leaf, but the run-budget and resampling formulation lacks a SAT-local-search citation and does not establish which restart policy the taxonomy intends.

children.title: Search-State Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Partial disruption of assignments or search memory within a continuing run.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-State Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial randomization of a Boolean local-search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current assignment be \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), choose a perturbation size \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(Q_x\) be a distribution on the \(k\)-element subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Sample \(S\sim Q_x\), set \(x_i^{+}=1-x_i\) for \(i\in S\), and set \(x_i^{+}=x_i\) otherwise. Resume local search from \(x^{+}\), optionally retaining auxiliary state only when its consistency with \(x^{+}\) is restored. The perturbation changes exactly \(k\) variable values and therefore has Hamming radius \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a set of variables, flip exactly those variables, repair any inconsistent auxiliary data, and resume local search from the perturbed assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_x\) is supported on subsets of cardinality \(k\).

notation.meaning: sampled set of variables to flip

review_flags: perturbation operator is one standard generic form

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exact-k flipping correctly yields Hamming distance k and algorithm is a suitable kind, but this is only one perturbation operator. No source establishes it as the intended SAT search-state perturbation.

children.title: Restart–Perturbation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Diversification choices between full renewal and partial disruption.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart–Perturbation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative memory–diversification tradeoff under independent bit perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From an assignment \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), independently flip each variable with probability \(q\in[0,1/2]\), producing \(X^{+}\). Then \(d_H(x,X^{+})\) has distribution \(\operatorname{Binomial}(n,q)\), so \[\mathbb E[d_H(x,X^{+})]=nq,\qquad \Pr(X^{+}=x)=(1-q)^n.\] At \(q=1/2\), \(X^{+}\) is uniform on \(\{0,1\}^n\), exactly matching a uniform random restart. Hence increasing \(q\) decreases retention of the current assignment while increasing diversification, with uniform restart as the maximal-noise endpoint of this perturbation family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent bit flips interpolate between retaining the current assignment and a uniform restart; expected Hamming displacement is the number of variables times the flip probability.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) is fixed.
Variable flips are mutually independent with common probability \(q\in[0,1/2]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[d_H(x,X^{+})]=nq\), and \(X^{+}\) is uniform when \(q=1/2\).
review_flags: elementary calculation lacks supplied supporting source
tradeoff model covers independent-bit perturbations only

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binomial and uniform-endpoint claims are mathematically precise, and property fits the tradeoff leaf. Nevertheless, no citation supports using independent bit flips as the governing restart–perturbation model.

children.title: Promising-Variable Selection
children.top_down_role: Candidate-variable prioritization based on recent or predicted search value.

knowledge_statements.title: Promising-Variable Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variables promising an immediate decrease in falsified-clause cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a CNF formula with positive clause weights \(w_C\), define \(E_w(x)=\sum_{C:x\not\models C}w_C\). For variable \(i\), let \(x^{\oplus i}\) be the assignment obtained by flipping \(i\), and define its gain by \(g_i(x)=E_w(x)-E_w(x^{\oplus i})\). Variable \(i\) is promising at \(x\) when \(g_i(x)>0\). A greedy promising-variable selector chooses an element of \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i:g_i(x)>0}g_i(x)\), with a specified tie-breaking distribution, and reports failure when this set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable is promising when flipping it strictly lowers weighted falsified-clause cost; greedy selection chooses one having maximum positive gain.
assumptions_latex: The CNF formula has finitely many variables and clauses.
\(w_C>0\) for every clause \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\) is promising at \(x\) exactly when \(E_w(x^{\oplus i})<E_w(x)\).

notation.meaning: weighted cost of clauses falsified by x
assignment obtained by flipping variable i
cost decrease caused by flipping variable i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Positive gain is a coherent definition, but “promising variable” is algorithm-dependent and the record also embeds a greedy selection algorithm under definition. A source is needed to fix both terminology and mathematical role.

children.title: Promising-Clause Selection
children.top_down_role: Candidate-clause prioritization for focused local-search moves.

knowledge_statements.title: Promising-Clause Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Biased selection of an unsatisfied clause for the next local-search move.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At assignment \(x\), let \(U(x)=\{C\in\mathcal C:x\not\models C\}\). Assign each \(C\in U(x)\) a nonnegative priority \(h_C(x)\), with positive total priority whenever \(U(x)\neq\varnothing\). If \(U(x)=\varnothing\), stop and output \(x\). Otherwise sample a clause according to \[\Pr(C_t=C\mid x_t=x)=\frac{h_C(x)}{\sum_{D\in U(x)}h_D(x)},\qquad C\in U(x),\] then pass \(C_t\) to the variable selector. Uniform unsatisfied-clause selection is recovered by taking all priorities equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign priorities to currently unsatisfied clauses, sample one proportionally to its priority, and pass it to the variable-selection rule.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is finite.
If \(U(x)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\sum_{C\in U(x)}h_C(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_t\in U(x_t)\) almost surely whenever \(U(x_t)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: set of clauses falsified by assignment x
selection priority of clause C at x

review_flags: notion of promising clause is not canonical
priority construction requires an algorithm-specific source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The priority-normalized clause sampler is valid, but it merely selects an unsatisfied clause; it does not define why a clause is “promising.” An algorithm-specific source must establish the intended priority semantics.

children.title: Variable–Clause Selection Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordination between clause-level focus and variable-level move choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable–Clause Selection Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorization of clause-first SAT local-search move selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U(x)\) be the clauses falsified by assignment \(x\). A clause-first variable-selection mechanism is specified by a clause kernel \(P_C(C\mid x)\), supported on \(U(x)\), and a conditional variable kernel \(P_V(i\mid C,x)\), supported on variables occurring in \(C\). Its joint move law and induced variable marginal are \[P(C,i\mid x)=P_C(C\mid x)P_V(i\mid C,x),\qquad P(i\mid x)=\sum_{C\in U(x)}P_C(C\mid x)P_V(i\mid C,x).\] Thus clause priorities and within-clause variable scores jointly determine the probability of every variable flip.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clause-first local search factors a move into selecting an unsatisfied clause and then a variable in it; summing over clauses gives each flip probability.
assumptions_latex: \(P_C(\cdot\mid x)\) is a probability distribution supported on \(U(x)\).
\(P_V(\cdot\mid C,x)\) is a probability distribution supported on variables of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(i\mid x)=\sum_{C\in U(x)}P_C(C\mid x)P_V(i\mid C,x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The kernel factorization and marginalization are correct and representation fits the leaf, but no SAT source establishes this clause-first factorization as the intended coupling rather than one possible architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Local-Search Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel interface combining SAT local search with an external search component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be a common search-state space, \(K_{\mathrm{LS}}\) a local-search transition kernel, and \(K_{\mathrm{ext}}\) a transition kernel induced by an external solver, propagator, or construction heuristic after state translation. For a measurable control \(\lambda:\mathcal S\to[0,1]\), a hybrid interface defines \[K_{\mathrm{hyb}}(s,A)=\lambda(s)K_{\mathrm{LS}}(s,A)+(1-\lambda(s))K_{\mathrm{ext}}(s,A).\] Both components must return states satisfying the representation invariants of \(\mathcal S\). The formula gives a valid transition kernel and makes the component-selection rule explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid interface translates components to one state space and mixes their transition kernels using a state-dependent control probability.
assumptions_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{LS}}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{ext}}\) are transition kernels on the same measurable state space \(\mathcal S\).
\(\lambda\) is measurable and takes values in \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\mathrm{hyb}}\) is a transition kernel on \(\mathcal S\).
review_flags: hybrid interface has several incompatible algorithmic meanings
no supplied source fixes the intended SAT hybridization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A measurable convex mixture of two kernels is valid, but hybrid local-search interfaces can instead alternate, exchange incumbents, invoke propagation, or use staged control. No source supports reducing this broad topic to the proposed mixture.

children.title: Local Minima
children.top_down_role: Search states lacking locally improving moves.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Minima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-flip local minima of the unsatisfied-clause objective for a finite CNF formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a CNF formula on variables \(V\), let \(E_F(a)\) denote the number of clauses falsified by assignment \(a\in\{0,1\}^{V}\), and let \(a^{\oplus v}\) be obtained by flipping variable \(v\in V\). The assignment \(a\) is a one-flip local minimum when \[E_F(a)\le E_F(a^{\oplus v})\quad\text{for every }v\in V.\] It is strict when every displayed inequality is strict. An unsatisfying local minimum, characterized additionally by \(E_F(a)>0\), is a local-search trap for algorithms that accept only strictly improving flips.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assignment is a one-flip local minimum when flipping any single variable cannot reduce the number of unsatisfied clauses; it is a trap if it remains unsatisfying.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Neighborhoods consist of single-variable flips.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\text{ is locally minimal}\iff (\forall v\in V)\ E_F(a)\le E_F(a^{\oplus v})\).

notation.meaning: Number of clauses of F falsified by assignment a.
Assignment obtained from a by flipping variable v.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard one-flip local-minimum definition for SAT energy landscapes
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-flip definition is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no inspectable SAT-specific citation is supplied. The plain statement also calls every unsatisfying local minimum a trap without preserving the LaTeX statement's restriction to algorithms accepting only strictly improving flips.

children.title: Search Plateaus
children.top_down_role: Extended regions of equal or weakly differentiated search score.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Plateaus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connected constant-energy regions of the one-flip SAT search graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a CNF formula \(F\), form the graph on \(\{0,1\}^{V}\) whose edges join assignments at Hamming distance one. A search plateau at level \(h\) is a maximal connected set \(P\) such that \(E_F(a)=h\) for every \(a\in P\). It is an exitless plateau for non-increasing one-flip search when \[E_F(b)>h\quad\text{for every }a\in P\text{ and every one-flip neighbor }b\notin P.\] A plateau with \(h>0\) can therefore trap a search rule that neither accepts worsening moves nor performs a nonlocal restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search plateau is a maximal one-flip-connected set of assignments with equal cost. It is exitless when every move leaving it increases cost.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a finite CNF formula.
Search adjacency is Hamming distance one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ is a plateau at }h\iff P\text{ is maximal connected and }(\forall a\in P)\ E_F(a)=h\).

notation.meaning: Set of assignments forming the plateau.
Common unsatisfied-clause level on the plateau.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard constant-objective plateau definition on a neighborhood graph
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports the selected plateau convention. Moreover, positive level alone does not imply trapping: the final claim requires the plateau also to be exitless under the stated move policy.

children.title: Search Cycles
children.top_down_role: Repeated returns to previously encountered assignments or move patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Cycles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic recurrence in the assignment trajectory of a SAT local-search rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((a_t)_{t\ge0}\) be the assignment trajectory generated by a local-search rule for a finite CNF formula. The trajectory enters a search cycle of period \(k\ge1\) at time \(t_0\) when \[a_{t+k}=a_t\quad\text{for every }t\ge t_0,\] and \(k\) is the least positive integer with this property. The cycle is non-solving when \(E_F(a_t)>0\) throughout one period. For a deterministic, memoryless update rule, revisiting any assignment forces subsequent repetition and hence produces such a cycle unless that assignment is terminal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search cycle is an eventually periodic sequence of assignments. It is non-solving when every assignment in the repeated period leaves at least one clause unsatisfied.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and its assignment space are finite.
The stated recurrence concerns the realized local-search trajectory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((a_t)\text{ cycles with least period }k\iff (\forall t\ge t_0)\ a_{t+k}=a_t\).

notation.meaning: Assignment visited at search step t.
Least period of the recurring trajectory.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard eventual-periodicity definition on a finite state trajectory
source requested for the SAT update-rule formulation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The eventual-periodicity definition and deterministic memoryless recurrence claim are coherent and fit the leaf, but no source with a specific locator supports the SAT-local-search formulation.

children.title: Noise-Sensitivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Performance variation induced by changes in stochastic noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Sensitivity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon sensitivity of stochastic SAT success probability to a scalar noise parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For instance \(I\), noise parameter \(p\in[0,1]\), and budget \(T\), let \(S_{I,T}(p)\) be the probability that the stochastic local search reaches a satisfying assignment by time \(T\). For radius \(\delta>0\), define \[\omega_{I,T}(p;\delta)=\sup_{q\in[0,1],\ |q-p|\le\delta}|S_{I,T}(q)-S_{I,T}(p)|.\] Given tolerance \(\tau\in[0,1]\), the algorithm is noise-stable at \((I,p,T,\delta,\tau)\) when \(\omega_{I,T}(p;\delta)\le\tau\), and noise-sensitive when this inequality fails. Regime boundaries are parameter values at which the predicate changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise stability means that nearby noise settings change finite-budget success probability by at most a specified tolerance; sensitivity is failure of that condition.
assumptions_latex: The local-search transition rule is defined for every \(p\in[0,1]\).
Success is measured within a fixed finite budget \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{noise-stable}\iff\omega_{I,T}(p;\delta)\le\tau\).

notation.meaning: Probability of solving instance I within T steps at noise p.
Worst local change in success probability around p.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this finite-horizon sensitivity convention.
Alternative derivative-based and runtime-based regimes require editorial selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-horizon modulus is a precise proposed condition, but the title does not uniquely select this convention over derivative-, runtime-, or scaling-based sensitivity regimes. A domain-specific source is required.

children.title: Cross-Instance Parameter Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of tuned parameters across formulas, distributions, or scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Instance Parameter Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate transfer of a tuned noise parameter between SAT-instance distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_s\) and \(D_t\) be source and target distributions over SAT instances, and define \(J_D(p)=\mathbb{E}_{I\sim D}[S_{I,T}(p)]\) for \(p\in\mathcal P\). A source-selected parameter \(p_s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{p\in\mathcal P}J_{D_s}(p)\) is \(\varepsilon\)-transferable to \(D_t\) when \[\sup_{p\in\mathcal P}J_{D_t}(p)-J_{D_t}(p_s)\le\varepsilon.\] Thus transfer is assessed by target regret, not merely by similarity between the numerical parameter values independently optimized on the two distributions.
